# MASTER LESSONS: Dominion, every experiment and lesson in one file

> Feed this file to your AI system as context before you start work on the Herculaneum scrolls. It holds what we
> learned from every Dominion experiment, start to finish, so a new session can skip our dead ends.
>
> Size: about 126,822 words (roughly 229k tokens). The parts are ordered by value: if your model's context is smaller,
> give it Parts 0-5 (rules, all lessons, retracted claims, where to pick up) and leave out the timeline and the register.
>
> Dominion was directed by Joseph Balmaceda and run by Claude research agents (Anthropic), September-October 2026.
> Cite: see CITATION.cff in https://github.com/abundantjoe/scroll-lessons. Scroll data: Vesuvius Challenge - CT Scans of
> Herculaneum Papyri (Angelotti et al.), CC BY-NC 4.0. Data used in the preparation of the PHerc. Paris 4 material were
> obtained from the EduceLab-Scrolls dataset (Parsons et al. 2023, doi:10.48550/arXiv.2304.02084). Text: CC BY-NC 4.0.

## Part 0. Read this first

### What this file is

This is the full lesson record of **Dominion**, an AI-run research programme (24 September to 15 October 2026) that tried to find ink inside carbonized Herculaneum scrolls from public X-ray CT, for the Vesuvius Challenge.

- One owner directed it, and Claude agents did the work.
- An orchestrating session kept an append-only, hash-chained decision log, the "research log" (`RULES.md`, 6,152 lines).
- Sibling worker sessions ran single experiments on their own git branches: 118 sibling sessions were registered between 25 September and 2 October (on 95 branches; with sub-sibling branches, 118 experiment branches in all, including `data` and `fl4t`), and a further 52 sessions in the 9 October fleet ([L443](#l443-session-count-is-not-compute)).
- Separate repositories held the PHerc0268 work, the Paris 4 title package and the public tools.

This file merges all of them. Its parts, in order of value:

- **Part 0:** how to use the file, the state of the field when we stopped, and the golden rules.
- **Parts 1-3:** the numbered lessons L001-L508 (294 VERIFIED, 181 MEASURED, 33 INFERENCE) by theme: data, geometry and rendering; ink, validation and reading; agents, process, compute and tools.
- **Part 4:** the claims we retracted.
- **Part 5:** open problems, data, models, tools and the glossary.
- **Part 6:** the timeline, start to finish.
- **Part 7:** the experiment register.

It is not a working pipeline. **No letters are claimed on any scroll.** Its value is a precise account of what was tried, what failed and why, so that a new session can avoid our mistakes.

**Lesson format.** Trap = the mistake. Evidence = the record that shows it. Fix = what to do instead. The labels are:

- **VERIFIED:** backed by a recorded test (a pre-registered test, a control, an independent audit or an exact reproduction).
- **MEASURED:** a recorded number, not a decisive test.
- **INFERENCE:** reasoned but untested.
- **RETRACTED:** withdrawn. Never use it as a fact.

**Citations** take the form `repo:ref:path`:

- `dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5` is the research-log branch `claude/gifted-bell-gavnl5`.
- `dominion:<lane>` (e.g. `sib-p4-core`, `fl4t`, `data`) is the experiment branch `claude/gifted-bell-gavnl5-<lane>`; `@<sha>` pins a commit.
- `dominion:main` is the October 2026 Progress Prize release.
- In the public repository [abundantjoe/scroll-lessons](https://github.com/abundantjoe/scroll-lessons) every one of these is a branch: `<lane>` (e.g. `sib-p4-core`), `research-log` for the research log, and `dominion-release` for `dominion:main`. Those snapshots are scrubbed: personal data removed, large raw arrays listed in each branch's `DATA_MANIFEST.tsv`, prize-candidate details withheld.
- `pherc0268`, `paris-4`, `xsec`, `ringstrip` and `orgsec-ink` are the other repositories.
- `RULES.md#D1-VERDICT` names a section of the log.
- `survey:expmap_raw.json:<family>` is the private experiment-map survey of 2026-10-15 (not published); the public summary is `dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json`. For Paris 4 items its underlying records are withheld for prize review.

Times are UTC. Numbers are copied from the sources; do not round them.

**Withheld material.** Some work concerns candidate patches for the First Letters and First Title prizes. Prize rules forbid publishing a discovery before the prize is announced, so here it appears only as "a candidate was found and tested; details withheld for prize review". No location, tile name or letter identity is given. Do not try to reconstruct them. If you find a candidate, the same rule applies to you.

### How to use it

1. Attach the whole file to the AI session as context. Read it once in full, then search it by lesson ID (`L176`), scroll ID (`PHerc0268`) or term (Part 5 glossary).
2. Give the session a task with the prompt below. Fill in the angle brackets.
3. At the end of the session, have it add new lessons in the same format (Trap / Evidence / Fix / Label / When / Sources), starting from the next free number (L509), and add any claim it withdraws as RETRACTED.

```text
Context: MASTER_LESSONS.md (attached) is the complete lesson record of the Dominion
programme (Sep-Oct 2026) on finding ink in Herculaneum scroll CT. Treat it as the
prior work of the team you are joining.

Task: <e.g. "plan a First Letters attempt on PHerc0268" / "test whether ink model X
transfers to scroll Y" / "continue open problem OP03 from Part 5">.
Resources: <GPU/CPU, RAM, disk>, <time and usage budget>, <data access>.

Before you touch any data:
1. List the golden rules (Part 0) that apply to this task and say how the plan meets each.
2. Name the Part 5 open problem this task belongs to and its recorded best next step.
3. Search the lessons for every scroll, model, tool and method in the plan. List the
   lesson IDs and the trap each one warns about.
4. Write a declaration: the question, the material, a positive control on known text of
   the same scan, a negative control (for example a displaced copy), bars checked against
   the reference's own score, the decision rule, and the result that would stop the work.
Then propose the smallest experiment that can fail, and wait for my go-ahead before
spending compute.
Rules: cite lesson IDs for every claim you take from the file; never use a RETRACTED
item as a fact; copy numbers exactly; do not reconstruct withheld prize details.
```

Prize rules, the data catalogue and the public tools keep changing. Before relying on any rule or catalogue number here, re-fetch the live prize page and the catalogue ([L001](#l001-read-the-prize-rules-section-by-section-with-file-and-line), [L004](#l004-catalogue-facts-that-differ-from-the-fact-sheet-sept-2026), [L359](#l359-re-fetch-the-prize-page-and-licence-terms-before-relying-on-the-catalogue)).

### The state of the field as we left it (15 October 2026)

Nobody in this programme read a letter on an unread scroll. Two things failed together:

- the geometry did not give surfaces that stay on one sheet;
- public ink models did not show ink on new scans at a level readers could use.

Every null we recorded is bounded by these two failures. Most of the lasting value is in the controls that exposed them.

**What works (tested here):**

- **Exact reproduction of organizer products.** Called correctly, the official villa renderer reproduces the organizer surface volume essentially exactly ([L138](#l138-the-official-renderer-reproduces-the-organizer-surface-volume-essentially-exactly-when-called-correctly)). The 9 um base ink chain without mirror TTA passed its fidelity gate at 0.99960 ([L169](#l169-do-not-use---tta-mirror-with-the-base-ink9um-checkpoint-it-lowers-forward-auc-below-the-regression-bar)). The 2.4 um chain on CPU reproduced the organizer map at r 0.999986 in the forward order on a `--flip-normals` render ([L135](#l135-name-the-depth-order-by-the-render-frame-never-by-the-word-reverse)). These checks are cheap ([L455](#l455-exact-reproduction-checks-against-published-artefacts-are-cheap-and-remove-a-whole-class-of-input-doubts-before-fitting)).
- **A small ink model trained on the target scroll.** P4-OWN is a 232,697-parameter CNN trained from scratch on Paris 4's own labels outside a certified 3-D exclusion zone. It reached held-out pixel AUC 0.9418 / 0.9415 / 0.9401 (NULL 0.4972-0.5240) and 0.978 on never-trained known text. It passed a blind legibility gate at 63.9 % / 80.6 % against a 30 % bar ([L183](#l183-a-small-cnn-trained-from-scratch-on-the-scrolls-own-labels-detects-its-ink-where-a-cross-scroll-model-failed), [L184](#l184-train-on-the-target-scroll-itself-with-a-certified-3-d-exclusion-margin-around-the-prize-region)). A cross-scroll checkpoint was blind on the same scan ([L176](#l176-a-cross-scroll-ink-model-can-be-completely-blind-on-a-new-scroll-gate-it-on-that-scrolls-known-text-first)).
- **Official 2.4 um Paris 4 predictions on known text.** Readers read 135 of 171 known-text tiles as writing. But 38 of 39 target positives lay within 1.2 mm of the model's training labels, so these predictions cannot give candidates there ([L019](#l019-measure-training-label-adjacency-before-spending-reads-on-official-model-output)).
- **Sealed blind reads with real nulls.** Keys and briefs are committed first ([L275](#l275-sealed-read-harness-commit-keys-and-briefs-before-any-reader-never-let-the-harness-see-answers)). Rotated self-nulls with 40 or more null tiles are used, because 4-tile nulls manufacture leads ([L321](#l321-a-4-tile-null-manufactures-leads-a-rotated-self-null-plus--40-null-tiles-kills-them)). Transcripts are audited ([L284](#l284-session-validity--transcript-audit-allow-exactly-one-re-run-of-a-void-session)). Hidden positives and negatives calibrate the readers ([L293](#l293-an-uncalibrated-blind-read-is-uninformative-hide-known-letters-and-no-ink-strips-among-the-targets)).
- **Process.** Declarations before data, hash-pinned code, a hash-chained log and independent audits cost minutes and caught many errors ([L297](#l297-declare-before-data-pin-code-by-hash-and-keep-an-append-only-hash-chained-log), [L348](#l348-pre-register-decision-bars-and-label-exploratory-arms-it-is-what-exposed-the-strip-artifact), [L349](#l349-list-superseded-claims-explicitly-the-same-day)).
- **Geometry pieces.**
  - Non-affine PHerc0841 registration passed (r 0.863, RMS 0.977 vox) where a single affine failed ([L060](#l060-pherc0841-9366---2403-um-registration-is-non-affine-a-single-affine-fails-held-out-patches)).
  - Normal-grid grows follow the sheet in gross terms (median |cos| 0.93 against 0.16) ([L100](#l100-grows-without-normal-grids-are-data-independent-know-the-failure-signatures)).
  - The organizers' extractor regenerates spiral tracks exactly ([L049](#l049-published-pherc0268-spiral-tracks-stop-at-z--4500-regenerate-the-missing-21--with-the-organizers-own-extractor)).
- **The blank-margin fill.** It restores most of the ink on thin strips (recall 0.646 against 0.386) but about doubles the off-letter strong pixels ([L162](#l162-margin-fill-restores-sensitivity-but-raises-off-letter-strong-pixels-measure-its-no-ink-floor)).

**What does not work (tested and failed here):**

- **Public 9 um maps on unseen text.** Pixel AUC was about 0.73 on PHerc0841, yet 18 calibrated readers named 0 letters (D1). Readers still named 0 after an in-domain fine-tune (D3). Legible maps need an effective blur of about 0.30 mm or less ([L196](#l196-the-base-9-um-model-detects-unseen-scroll-ink-at-pixel-level-auc-073-but-its-maps-are-not-letter-legible), [L167](#l167-fine-tuning-the-9-um-base-model-on-nearby-same-scroll-papyrus-did-not-make-unseen-text-legible), [L268](#l268-calibrated-legibility-falls-smoothly-with-blur-maps-need-an-effective-blur-of--030-mm-to-be-read)).
- **Cross-scroll checkpoints on a new scan.** The known-text gate on Paris 4 was 0/3 ([L176](#l176-a-cross-scroll-ink-model-can-be-completely-blind-on-a-new-scroll-gate-it-on-that-scrolls-known-text-first)). Validation on the training scroll overstated transfer ([L190](#l190-validation-on-the-training-scroll-overstated-transfer)).
- **Model-free raw-CT displays of carbon ink.** Slab means, thin slabs, surface-following faces, crackle and row periodicity all failed on known Paris 4 text ([L203](#l203-raw-ct-slab-means-do-not-show-carbon-ink-to-blind-readers-even-next-to-known-text), [L204](#l204-model-free-raw-ct-channels-did-not-detect-known-carbon-ink-on-paris-4-at-24-um), [L205](#l205-crackle-texture-energy-carries-real-but-weak-ink-information-not-an-independent-ink-channel)).
- **Composition channels.** These exclude mineral inks only at CT-detectable thickness, and they are blind to organic colourants ([L202](#l202-mineral-pigment-high-z-ink-is-ruled-out-on-the-traced-paris-4-surfaces-with-injection-recovery-limits), [L215](#l215-a--60-um-dense-pigment-sweep-closes-mineral-inks-only-at-ct-detectable-thickness), [L216](#l216-dual-energy-ct-cannot-see-organic-or-lake-colourants-a-null-means-untestable)).
- **Grows without normal grids.** They ignored the CT: identical areas across seeds (generation caps of 26.5-31.1 cm2 in FL-2; the same ~11.665 cm2 square in every FL-4 grow), cutting across windings. With a positive-control gate that was never sensitive, this voided the FL-1/FL-2/FL-3 nulls on all 22 eligible scrolls and the FL-4 reads ([L100](#l100-grows-without-normal-grids-are-data-independent-know-the-failure-signatures), [L283](#l283-a-0-positive-census-under-a-gate-that-never-passed-is-uninformative), R007, R008). With normal grids, surfaces still jump layers at cracks, unseen by every numeric gate we tested ([L101](#l101-numeric-surface-gates-are-blind-to-layer-jumps-on-crushed-scrolls-look-at-cross-sections)).
- **Crushed-scroll geometry at 8.64 um (PHerc0268).** Sheet identity is lost within about 0.3 mm ([L115](#l115-local-sheet-identity-tracking-at-864-um-fails-across-the-whole-of-pherc0268)). The umbilicus is uncertain by 2-7 mm ([L117](#l117-pherc0268-umbilicus-is-a-curvature-centre-estimate-good-to-only-2-7-mm-at-mid-heights)). CPU spiral fits are off the sheet in orientation (42 deg against 6 deg) ([L124](#l124-the-fit-failure-signature-is-orientation-not-phase-median-normal-angle-42-deg-vs-6-deg-for-the-recipe)). Window fits do not stitch: seams of 8-56 vox, and winding indices that disagree by 3-15 sheets ([L131](#l131-independent-z-window-fits-do-not-stitch-seams-of-8-56-voxels-and-winding-indices-that-disagree-by-3-15-sheets)).
- **Thin strips with blank render margins.** They halve real ink on the PHerc0343 control and painted false bands on about 2/3 of 56 PHerc0268 strips ([L249](#l249-the-blank-margin-bug-partly-blank-inference-patches-create-or-suppress-ink)).
- **CPU-trained 8.64 um ink models.** From scratch reached AUC 0.579 against a 0.90 bar, and fine-tuning gave no gain over the public 0.760 ([L192](#l192-cpu-trained-from-scratch-ink-models-at-864-um-stalled-far-below-a-public-baseline), [L191](#l191-fine-tuning-on-pseudo-labels-produced-by-another-model-can-pull-a-stronger-model-toward-the-labellers-errors)).
- **Uncalibrated blind AI reads and automated selectors.** Readers' AUC of 0.875-0.900 sat below a colour-only baseline of 0.975, so they responded to colour, not letter shape ([L293](#l293-an-uncalibrated-blind-read-is-uninformative-hide-known-letters-and-no-ink-strips-among-the-targets), [L295](#l295-readers-are-ai-agents-say-so-and-keep-coarse-roc-caveats)). A row-structure score flagged 1.8 % of known text against a 25 % bar ([L233](#l233-an-automated-row-structure-score-did-not-detect-known-text-on-9-um-maps)).

**Unsolved:**

- A reproducible pipeline to legible letters on any unread scroll (OP01).
- On-sheet surfaces in crushed scrolls; PHerc0268's winding count is about 90 to about 140 (OP08-OP14).
- Ink-model transfer without the scan's own labels. PHerc0268 has about 0.42x the sheet contrast of PHerc0343 ([L195](#l195-pherc0268-has-about-half-the-ct-sheet-contrast-of-pherc0343-sensitivity-shown-on-the-control-does-not-carry-over)).
- The blank-margin sign flip and the upstream fix (OP16-OP18).
- **The Paris 4 title.** There is a carbon-ink null in the expected end-title slot ([L219](#l219-state-the-scope-of-every-null-the-own-model-title-slot-null-is-a-carbon-ink-null-only)), and other inks cannot be tested with the published scans. The innermost windings are unsegmented ([L086](#l086-paris-4-official-meshes-start-at-w010-inner-windings-w000-w009-are-unsegmented)), and an initial title on the outer windings remains open ([L229](#l229-initial-titles-exist-search-both-ends-of-a-roll), [L232](#l232-do-not-assume-the-first-text-you-confirm-is-the-rolls-first-column)).

**Prize position:**

- No letter is claimed on any scroll. On 3 October the push across 22 eligible volumes ended "no First Letters candidate exists in the project; nothing submittable" (`dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#FL6-RESULT`).
- For both the Paris 4 title search and a later calibrated blind read on PHerc0268: a candidate was found and tested; details withheld for prize review. The declared physical tests of the PHerc0268 candidate have no recorded results.
- **First Letters** (read on 24 September 2026) pays $50,000 per eligible volume for 10 letters in a single 4 cm2 area, with a deadline of 25 June 2027. You must show the text is not hallucinated ([L001](#l001-read-the-prize-rules-section-by-section-with-file-and-line)).
- 22 scrolls were eligible on 25 September 2026, after PHerc1447 was removed. The open-source condition covers code, data, weights and results. How it applies to CC BY-NC derived data is unresolved (OP37).
- Packaging is covered in [L018](#l018-prize-packaging-name-the-official-mesh-licensed-instead-of-redistributing-it-and-build-the-image-in-code), [L374](#l374-submission-kits-must-leave-owner-only-fields-empty-and-contain-no-filing-path) and [L385](#l385-know-what-a-title-or-first-letters-submission-needs-before-the-evidence-exists). A form submission needs the owner's signed-in account ([L474](#l474-google-forms-prize-submission-requires-the-owners-signed-in-account)).

### The golden rules

These 25 rules were drawn from the whole record. Each links to the lesson that proves it.

1. Gate every ink model and display on known text of the same scan before computing or reading a single target tile. [L176](#l176-a-cross-scroll-ink-model-can-be-completely-blind-on-a-new-scroll-gate-it-on-that-scrolls-known-text-first)
2. Do not run or report a census whose positive-control gate has not passed; its nulls are uninformative. [L283](#l283-a-0-positive-census-under-a-gate-that-never-passed-is-uninformative)
3. Grow surfaces only with the organizers' normal grids; area plus zero self-intersections is not a surface gate. [L100](#l100-grows-without-normal-grids-are-data-independent-know-the-failure-signatures)
4. Inspect grown surfaces in cross-sections; numeric and radial-normal gates cannot see layer jumps at cracks. [L101](#l101-numeric-surface-gates-are-blind-to-layer-jumps-on-crushed-scrolls-look-at-cross-sections)
5. Gate every surface for sheet-following (off-sheet control, CT-mask occupancy) before spending ink-model or reader time on it. [L097](#l097-test-sheet-following-with-an-off-sheet-control-and-ct-mask-occupancy-before-rendering)
6. Never ink strips that carry blank render margins; patch normalisation turns empty rows into fake ink or hides real ink. [L249](#l249-the-blank-margin-bug-partly-blank-inference-patches-create-or-suppress-ink)
7. Push a known-letters control through the identical pipeline before reading any null. [L256](#l256-push-a-known-letters-control-through-the-identical-pipeline-before-reading-any-null)
8. Calibrate every blind read with hidden same-format positives and colour-matched negatives, and report nothing if calibration fails. [L293](#l293-an-uncalibrated-blind-read-is-uninformative-hide-known-letters-and-no-ink-strips-among-the-targets)
9. Cap every image shown to an AI reader at 1068 px per side; larger images are silently resampled. [L259](#l259-agent-harness-silently-resamples-images-larger-than-1068-px-per-side)
10. Declare bars before data, pin code by hash and keep an append-only, hash-chained decision log. [L297](#l297-declare-before-data-pin-code-by-hash-and-keep-an-append-only-hash-chained-log)
11. Compute the reference's own score under your metric before declaring any bar. [L300](#l300-a-gate-bar-above-the-references-own-score-can-never-pass)
12. Compare a number only with a bar measured at the same pipeline stage. [L120](#l120-compare-a-number-only-with-a-bar-from-the-same-pipeline-stage)
13. Train on the target scroll's own labels with a certified 3-D exclusion margin around the search region. [L184](#l184-train-on-the-target-scroll-itself-with-a-certified-3-d-exclusion-margin-around-the-prize-region)
14. Measure every tile's 3-D distance to the model's training labels before reading official model output. [L019](#l019-measure-training-label-adjacency-before-spending-reads-on-official-model-output)
15. Check each checkpoint's documented training data before running it on a target scroll. [L175](#l175-check-each-checkpoints-documented-training-data-before-any-inference-eligibility-is-a-documentation-check)
16. Name the depth order by the render frame and confirm it reproduces the organizer map on a labelled control. [L135](#l135-name-the-depth-order-by-the-render-frame-never-by-the-word-reverse)
17. Read only the reading-face ink map on a fixed absolute scale; never average recto and verso or stretch per image. [L158](#l158-never-average-recto-and-verso-maps-or-stretch-each-ink-image-on-its-own)
18. Treat missing CT (404 chunks, zero-valued pixels) as unobserved, never as blank papyrus. [L015](#l015-missing-ct-chunks-masquerade-as-blank-papyrus)
19. State the scope of every null (ink type, depth, region); a carbon-ink null is not "no title". [L219](#l219-state-the-scope-of-every-null-the-own-model-title-slot-null-is-a-carbon-ink-null-only)
20. Do not expect model-free raw-CT displays to show carbon ink; every one tried failed on known text. [L204](#l204-model-free-raw-ct-channels-did-not-detect-known-carbon-ink-on-paris-4-at-24-um)
21. Copy a recipe's full optimisation schedule, not just its step count, before judging a fit. [L121](#l121-villas-spiral-fit-defaults-assume-30000-steps-a-2000-step-horizon-never-switches-on-trackdt)
22. Make every long job resumable from on-disk checkpoints; containers restart and wipe RAM disks. [L402](#l402-long-jobs-need-checkpoints-that-survive-a-container-restart)
23. Never route around a safety or permission block; record it and ask the owner. [L350](#l350-never-work-around-safety-or-permission-blocks)
24. Treat only a direct owner instruction as consent; relayed messages do not lift a stop. [L361](#l361-a-relayed-instruction-does-not-lift-a-direct-owner-stop-continuing-on-a-new-branch-routes-around-it)
25. Get approved paths for downloads, detached jobs and pushes before fanning out workers. [L386](#l386-session-permission-layers-refuse-remote-model-code-third-party-downloads-and-detached-launches-plan-approved-paths-up-front)

## Part 1. Lessons: data, geometry and rendering

**Data and access (L001-L049).** What the published scans, labels, metadata and prize rules actually contain, and how to fetch, identify and register data without silent errors.

### L001. Read the prize rules section by section, with file and line
- **Trap:** Misattributing rule text across prize sections, or submitting large-window model letters without showing they are not hallucinated.
- **Evidence:** scrollprize docs/34_prizes.md line 122 ('Data derived from higher resolution scans of the submitted scroll volume cannot be used.') is inside the 2027 Grand Prize section (lines 101-194), not First Letters (195-256); line 224 (First Letters): large windows are fine but you must demonstrate the text is not hallucinated, e.g. by finding different plausible letters on a held-out region. First Letters = $50,000 per eligible volume, 10 letters within a single 4 cm^2 area, deadline June 25 2027. No AI-disclosure rule found.
- **Fix:** Quote rule text with file, line and section when deciding eligibility; build held-out/sealed evidence and NULL/REV controls to answer the hallucination clause explicitly; keep stricter handling (rescans as ground truth only) where unsure.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#D0-PRIZE-CHECK

### L002. Official PHerc0841 label layers: 'validation' is a coverage mask, not a held-out split
- **Trap:** Treating the label_set 20260918 'validation' zarr as held-out data, or assuming all ink lies inside 'supervision'.
- **Evidence:** Layers are uint8 {0,255}; 'validation' has IoU 0.997 with data coverage; 12 % of w00 ink pixels lie outside 'supervision'. The supervision mask barely leaves the J (T-shell) area: only 0.066 cm^2 outside it, all on segment 214732.
- **Fix:** Use ink = inklabels inside supervision, blank = supervision without ink; do not count on any official held-out split for 0841.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#B0841-BANK, #HECATE-SCREEN

### L003. 'Clean' PHerc0139 segments may be re-traced by base-training segments
- **Trap:** Trusting catalogue 'clean control' labels: w047 was listed clean for the base model.
- **Evidence:** KD-tree test: w047 re-traced by base-training w045 (1.39e5 vox^2, ~0.12 cm^2) and by w046 (which re-traces w045); w024 re-traced by w023/w025 and w053 by w052/w054 (not base training).
- **Fix:** Run the same-papyrus KD-tree test of every candidate window against every training trace and its re-traces before using it as held-out.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#RCBANK-1

### L004. Catalogue facts that differ from the fact sheet (Sept 2026)
- **Trap:** Relying on a written fact sheet about segment counts, rescans, spiral tracks and checkpoints.
- **Evidence:** PHerc0139 has 39 segments (38 with 2.399 um maps); 0841: 9.366 um and 2.403 um volumes, no transform.json, but a 2.403<->9.366 um affine (7 landmarks) in the bucket root index; 0841 ink maps exist on the 2.403 um canvas only; 2.4 um SVs ~32 GB per segment, 9 um SVs ~0.6 GB; 0332 matches neither JULY nor MAY protocol; rescans only for 1203 and 0846A (2.403 um, ~36 mm bands, unregistered); spiral tracks for 18 of 23 eligible volumes; displacement checkpoints carry no licence; Hecate expects renders resampled to 9.6 um.
- **Fix:** Re-verify catalogue facts with sha256 of each fetched source at session start and log corrections.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-24 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#D0-KNOWN-TEXT, #D0-PRIZE-CHECK

### L005. Acquisition z direction and the catalogue's top-to-bottom flag are different fields
- **Trap:** Inferring up/down or mirroring from the acquisition z order, or treating a null top-to-bottom flag as known.
- **Evidence:** PHerc0358 and PHerc0846B have descending acquisition z (z_start > z_end); the root catalogue's z_direction_is_top_to_bottom disagrees with the acquisition order in places and is null for PHerc0125, PHerc0846A, PHerc1203 (and PHerc0490A/B among eligible volumes). Null-flag volumes keep a 180-degree up/down ambiguity but no mirror ambiguity.
- **Fix:** Record both fields per volume; decide mirror state by the geometry rule and up/down by the flag or a winding check.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-census:logs/sib/census/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-handed:logs/sib/handed/REPORT.md

### L006. Sync whole normal-grid planes per volume; per-seed partial syncs save almost nothing
- **Trap:** Planning per-seed partial downloads of normal grids, or using archive timings for trace cost.
- **Evidence:** Normal grids are one file per slice in xy (indexed by z), xz (per y) and yz (per x); xz/yz files span the whole z range and are needed whole. The union of 60 seeds' files covers 87-94 % of a volume's planes at 45 generations, so a full-plane sync (8.4-16.5 GB per volume, previews excluded) is the plan. Measured trace time on the container type: 259.7 s for one 45-generation seed at 1 thread, 3.7x the archive-scaled 70 s; 60 seeds at 4 parallel take 1.08 h (45 gen) / 3.01 h (75 gen).
- **Fix:** Sync one volume's full planes, trace, delete, next; budget with measured, not archive, timings. The m7 surface prediction is binary 0/255, 6 levels, 192^3 chunks.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-census:logs/sib/census/REPORT.md

### L007. Official ink labels carry no letter identities
- **Trap:** Planning letter-level validation (e.g. of mirror state) from the official ink labels.
- **Evidence:** Label arrays (inklabels.zarr, supervision.zarr, validation.zarr for PHerc0841) are single-channel uint8 OME-Zarr 0.5 masks with no class table. A substitute column-slant (Maas) test was underpowered: 0 columns measurable on 8 labelled PHerc0139 segments (widest ink run 20.8 mm, narrower than one column). Labels' canvas_offset_yx was already applied by the organizers; label and mesh canvases agree exactly.
- **Fix:** Use geometric checks (or letter-identity labels made separately) for letter-level questions.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-handed:logs/sib/handed/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-chain2um:logs/sib/chain2um/REPORT.md

### L008. Do not re-apply the label zarr's canvas_offset_yx; labels are already within about 4 px of the reference map
- **Trap:** Official ink-label zarrs carry a canvas_offset_yx from their transfer; applying it again misplaces every label.
- **Evidence:** PHerc0009B labelled segment: labels vs 2.401 um reference ink map best offset (+4.28, +4.26) canvas px (about 10 um, 0.5 px at 9 um), NCC 0.722 at both zero and best offset (gain 0.0007); metadata canvas_offset_yx (-38.35, -44.94). 81.1 % of labelled pixels have ref >= 150.
- **Fix:** Measure label-vs-map alignment directly before applying any stored offset; treat transfer offsets in metadata as already applied unless the measurement says otherwise.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-reg0009b:logs/sib/reg0009b/REPORT.md

### L009. Pyramid levels are exact 2x2x2 means: get the half-voxel offset right
- **Trap:** Treating level-L voxel i as level-0 coordinate i * 2^L shifts everything by half a coarse voxel.
- **Evidence:** PHerc0841 pyramid check: level L is an exact rounded 2x2x2 mean (MAE 0 against level 1), so level-L voxel i sits at level-0 coordinate i * 2^L + (2^L - 1)/2; pairs0139's gate spec uses level-1 = (level-0 + 0.5)/2 - 0.5 and verified level 1 = 2x2 mean of level 0 (max |diff| 0.5, r 0.99997).
- **Fix:** Convert pyramid coordinates with the half-voxel offset and verify it once per volume with a pyramid check.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-reg0841:logs/sib/reg0841/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-pairs0139:logs/sib/pairs0139/gate_spec.json

### L010. Read voxel size and protocol from each volume's own metadata.json
- **Trap:** Assuming a scroll matches the JULY (9.362 um, 113 keV) or MAY (8.64 um) protocol from its name or catalogue.
- **Evidence:** Protocol check from the root index and each metadata.json (scan.tomo.acquisition.detector.samplePixelSize): PHerc0814 and PHerc0500P2 match JULY 7/7, PHerc1451 matches MAY 4/4, PHerc0332 matches neither; several volumes have no readable metadata.json (404). PHerc0500P2 segments were traced on its 4.317 um MAY-session volume with ink maps on a 2.215 um scan. PHerc1545's FL-2 volume is 9.362 um, not 8.64 um.
- **Fix:** Hash the root index, read voxel size from every volume's metadata.json, and raise when it is missing; never take it from file names.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-pairs0814:logs/sib/pairs0814/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-pairs0814b:logs/sib/pairs0814b/fl2/STATUS.md

### L011. Do not list S3 recursively into zarr volumes
- **Trap:** A recursive S3 listing of a scroll prefix descends into millions of surface-volume chunks.
- **Evidence:** reg0009b's recursive listing was too slow and was replaced by a per-directory walk (20 segment prefixes, 201 objects, 903,122,426 B downloaded and hashed).
- **Fix:** Walk prefixes one level at a time and stop at .zarr directories; read .zarray/.zattrs explicitly.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-reg0009b:logs/sib/reg0009b/REPORT.md

### L012. Do not trust the bucket's landmark transform.json at sub-voxel level
- **Trap:** Using the organizer's landmark affine between 8.64 um and 2.401 um volumes as an exact mapping.
- **Evidence:** PHerc0009B transform.json holds a 6-landmark affine with landmark residuals up to 17 2.4-um vox (about 4.7 9-um vox), mostly along z.
- **Fix:** Use landmark transforms only as a coarse start and register CT-to-CT (with depth correction) for anything finer.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-reg0009b:logs/sib/reg0009b/REPORT.md

### L013. Some planned windows do not fit the material
- **Trap:** Planning 2 x 2 cm windows on narrow segments.
- **Evidence:** 0139 title segment canvas 5360 x 1780 px = 1.67 cm tall; 0814 segments are 1.4-1.7 cm-tall ribbons; only 1 of 4 fresh PROBE-2 windows qualified (946 of 947 candidates overlapped earlier windows).
- **Fix:** Run a numbers-only feasibility count before declaring window material, with a declared fallback.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#RCBANK-1, #DECL-READCAL-PROBE2-A1

### L014. Manual annotation of an eligible scroll, and reading a scroll with a model trained on its own labels, invalidate a First Letters claim
- **Trap:** Accepting team members' hand labels on an eligible scroll, or training on a scroll's own rescan/labels and reading that same scroll.
- **Evidence:** Owner proposal logged as a conflict; resolved by the stricter rule: FL-09 forbids manual character annotation (including memorised annotation) and requires model output not to overlap training data.
- **Fix:** Use only own work and official organizer products; cross-pair rescan labels (train on 1203, read 0846A and vice versa) only; keep submission regions >= 128 vox from any window found with 2.4 um help.
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#OWNER-CONFLICT-LABELS

### L015. Missing CT chunks masquerade as blank papyrus
- **Trap:** Reading tiles whose surface-volume chunks are absent from the public bucket (HTTP 404) as negatives or using them as nulls.
- **Evidence:** 22 of 46 own-model tiles of one outer region had missing chunks; 4 maps were constant (std <= 1). The model outputs exactly 91 on zero input, which is what a missing chunk gives. An earlier census read such tiles as blank, and a phase-2 N0 included tiles with 2112 and 656 missing chunks (a partly no-data null). Later, 32 of ~81, 33 of 143 and 47 of 171 tiles per region were NO-DATA. Also: 69 of 106 read-eligible 1.129 um control prediction tiles are >= 5 % zero because of missing CT input; official prediction products are already masked (0 nonzero pixels outside the mesh-valid mask in every eligible inner-strip tile). A coverage rule excluded 40 of 100 half-valid 1.129 um title-strip tiles, leaving 60.
- **Fix:** Flag NO-DATA from map numbers only, before any read: std < 1 or a large fraction of in-mesh pixels equal to the zero-input constant (5 % first; > 50 % for later regions, with 5-50 % tiles flagged 'partial' and partial windows kept in the null so chunk edges are controlled). Drop windows touching NO-DATA; report them as unobserved, never as nulls.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-25-A12, #DECL-P4-25-A11-A1, #DECL-P4-25-A14-A3; dominion:sib-fl-pherc0483b:README.md; dominion:sib-p4-tiles-b:README.md; dominion:sib-p4-tiles-a:logs/sib/p4-tiles-a/m2a/coverage_A1_summary.json, logs/sib/p4-tiles-a/REPORT.md; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census

### L016. Inventory scan coverage and registration before designing a composition or K-edge test
- **Trap:** Assuming no K-edge test is possible with published Paris 4 scans, or pairing scans through the canonical frame without checking residuals.
- **Evidence:** Scan inventory: the 137 keV 2.4 um scan is registered and with the 78 keV scans brackets Au 80.7, Hg 83.1 and Pb 88.0 keV, but covers only 4.7 % / 3.0 % of the inner-strip mesh points (a band of 12-49 % per tile on one row). The 110 keV 45.5 um scan has no published transform.json. Pairing through the canonical frame carries landmark residuals of ~6-20 um. Also: Only 3.01 % of the title-strip mesh vertices lie inside the 137 keV 2.4 um extent (control 4.40 %). The only Au-discriminating pair (74 + 110 keV) is at 45.5 um and the 110 keV volume has no published transform; 78 + 137 keV at 2.4 um has Au specificity only 1.19x (74+110: 1.72; 74+137: 1.06). No usable Au K-edge scan pair exists.
- **Fix:** Compute coverage from metadata and mesh geometry only (no target bytes) and include the covered fraction in any claim; a null on 3 % of a strip is a null on 3 % of the strip.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-pig-gold:logs/sib/p4-pig-gold/kedge_inventory.json, logs/sib/p4-pig-gold/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-p4-purple-de:logs/sib/p4-purple/de/overlap.json; dominion:sib-p4-highz@68030b270:logs/sib/p4-highz/REPORT.md (section 6, scans.json), logs/sib/p4-highz/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-p4-pig-gold@973fe81fd:logs/sib/p4-pig-gold/STATUS.md (kedge_inventory.json); survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-pigments; dominion:sib-p4-highz:logs/sib/p4-highz/REPORT.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#P4-CHANNELS-RESULT-1

### L017. A data-licence acceptance must reach the session that uses the data directly
- **Trap:** Relaying an owner's licence acceptance through an orchestrator message and expecting the worker session to act on it.
- **Evidence:** The organizers' 2024 title-search meshes live on the registered data server under a separate licence (non-redistribution, citation requirement). The owner's acceptance reached the layout lane only as a relay; its safety check refused the computation ('Real-World Transactions'), the 89 MB of fetched meshes were deleted and no number was derived. The transform was validated, but the mapping question stayed open.
- **Fix:** Have the owner state licence acceptance in the session that will use the data (or add a permission rule), or run the computation in a session that holds the owner's direct message; cite the dataset as the licence requires.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-layout:README.md, logs/sib/p4-layout/ASK.md; dominion:sib-p4-layout@148c75afe:logs/sib/p4-layout/REPORT.md; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census

### L018. Prize packaging: name the official mesh (licensed) instead of redistributing it, and build the image in code
- **Trap:** Bundling official segment meshes or hand-annotated images into a prize submission or public repo.
- **Evidence:** Official Paris 4 segments are EduceLab-licensed: they were named, never included. The submission image is a programmatic composite with a 1 cm scale bar, named after its mesh, with each tile's sha256 matching the builder manifest and no manual annotation of characters; the form needs the owner's own sign-in and the material must not be public before any official announcement.
- **Fix:** Keep a manifest of tile hashes, generate figures in code, name meshes, and keep candidate material private until the prize team announces.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-27 · **Sources:** paris-4:gifted-bell-gavnl5:SUBMISSION.md, README.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:CHANGELOG.md, logs/owner/HANDOFF.md

### L019. Measure training-label adjacency before spending reads on official model output
- **Trap:** Testing a model on strips that lie within millimetres of the organizer-labelled segments it (or its parent) was trained on.
- **Evidence:** Labelled-adjacent (< 1.2 mm) tiles: 120 of 160 and 139 of 171 on the two 2.4 um strips, and 106/106 and 100/100 on the two 1 um prediction strips. Also: Paris 4 core: windings about 0.1-0.3 mm apart, so all 100 tiles of the inner grid were within 1.2 mm of a labelled segment (max 0.793 mm); joint census 124 tiles, 61 positives, 124 labelled-adjacent, 0 candidates; all 15 title-scale windows were also <= 1.2 mm.
- **Fix:** Before any read, compute every tile's minimum 3-D point-to-surface distance to every labelled segment and exclude tiles < 1.2 mm; outside that, use the official predictions; inside, use an eligible model.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-17-A2, CHANGELOG.md; dominion:sib-p4-excl:README.md, logs/sib/p4-excl/STATUS.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#P4-D-RESULT, #P4-L4-PREGATE-RESULT; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:logs/p4/census_d_joint_excl_summary.json, RULES.md#P4-D-RESULT; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-2-A4, #P4-B-PHASE2-RESULT; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:logs/p4/census_b1_summary.json, logs/p4/census_a_summary.json, RULES.md#DECL-P4-2-A4, logs/p4/p2_1_score.json

### L020. 78/137 keV dual energy on the published Paris 4 scans: units fail, registration is critical, and only Cu/As/Au are reachable
- **Trap:** Expecting a two-energy decomposition of the published 2.4 um volumes to give composition maps for purple or lake inks.
- **Evidence:** Both 2.4 um volumes are Paganin + unsharp, polychromatic, float units unpublished; the 137 keV unit check failed (void 0.044, gain ~0.63 vs 78 keV), so the decomposition used an empirical papyrus line (k 0.679). Published affine off by 7.8 um median; after correction held-out residual 1.7 um median / 3.2 um p90 (sheet surface 2.4 um median, 18 um p90). Carbon-ink AUC 0.48 [0.33, 0.63]; FPR 0.022 per patch (nominal 0.01) rising to 0.118 with 250 um misregistration. Detectable at 10-20 um: CuO, orpiment, gold only; not detectable at <= 20 um: Tyrian purple, purpurissum, lakes, carbon ink, ochre (0.76 at 20 um), cinnabar and lead white (0.39-0.50).
- **Fix:** Use depth-column residuals (+-60 um) rather than voxel ratios, refine registration on a control with held-out blocks, validate on known ink and injected classes, and state insensitivities before applying to a target.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-purple-de:README.md, logs/sib/p4-purple/de/REPORT.md, logs/sib/p4-purple/de/validation.json; dominion:sib-p4-purple-de@c149c983c:logs/sib/p4-purple/de/REPORT.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md (METRIC-HASH-40); survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-pigments

### L021. Phase retrieval changes what a voxel encodes: model the actual reconstruction, not raw attenuation
- **Trap:** Predicting colourant visibility from X-ray absorption alone for volumes that were Paganin phase-retrieved and unsharp-masked.
- **Evidence:** xraylib table for 25 colourants at 5/10/20 um, 78 and 137 keV: in the published 2.4 um Paganin volume thin deposits are seen by electron density, so purple, lake and organic inks would be 0.9-1.4x as bright as carbon ink of equal thickness; absorption alone would make intact Tyrian purple 2.9x carbon ink. Reconstruction metadata: 78 keV Paganin delta/beta 1000 + unsharp 4; 137 keV 2000 + unsharp 5. Absolute contrasts are upper bounds: a 5 um carbon layer should saturate, yet only 0.064 % of control slab maxima do.
- **Fix:** Take the reconstruction chain (Paganin delta/beta, unsharp, clipping, uint8 window) from the published metadata and model contrast through it; treat absolute CNR predictions as upper bounds until checked against known ink.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-purple:README.md, logs/sib/p4-purple/REPORT.md, logs/sib/p4-purple/colourants.json; dominion:sib-p4-purple@887b74423:logs/sib/p4-purple/REPORT.md; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-pigments

### L022. Paris 4's innermost windings have no traced surface and need GPU tools that a CPU container lacks
- **Trap:** Planning to read the innermost core from official products.
- **Evidence:** No traced surface covers the windings inward of the innermost labelled winding; the published spiral fit has windings 10-63 only. The core is estimated at radius about 0.7-1.6 mm and area about 66-80 cm2 (Σr model validated against mesh-area ratio 0.98 vs 1.05); the 1.129 um volume covers only z 67.4-135.3 mm (about 54 % of the written region, ~29-31 cm2 of core). The official fit_spiral.py needs an NVIDIA GPU, and the 1 um ink model is not on Hugging Face.
- **Fix:** Before committing, test in one 2 x 2 cm window that the surface prediction separates sheets (sheet count vs the expected 10, seam consistency); do not start a full-strip trace or a CPU ResNet-152 run.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-inner:logs/sib/p4-inner/RECON.md, logs/sib/p4-inner/STATUS.md

### L023. Intensity alone cannot separate pigment from natural minerals; Cu and Fe have no K-edge at the Paris 4 energies
- **Trap:** Building a pigment detector on brightness when common minerals and volcanic glass are equally bright at 78 keV.
- **Evidence:** Egyptian blue attenuates 11.4x papyrus at 78 keV vs augite 10x, calcite 8x, quartz 6x; Egyptian blue saturates uint8 (occupancy 0.18-0.30 exceeds T_hi 233). Standard ochre is 4.5x papyrus in electron density and 10.9x in mu; ochre, Vesuvius glass (4.7-6.5x) and Ti-magnetite (9.6-31x) cannot be told apart per voxel at 78 keV, and Fe has no K-edge between 60 and 100 keV; Cu offers no K-edge test at the Paris 4 energies.
- **Fix:** Use morphology (letter-scale, on-sheet, stroke-shaped clusters) plus injection-recovery and a known-text control; never claim composition from single-energy intensity.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-pig-cu:logs/sib/p4-pig-cu/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4-pig-fe:logs/sib/p4-pig-fe/REPORT.md

### L024. Identify downloaded data by sha256, not by declared byte counts
- **Trap:** Checking a download against a size written into a declaration.
- **Evidence:** The declaration gave the 1.129 um control prediction as 1,175,621,659 B; the bucket listing and the downloaded file are 1,175,621,159 B (a one-digit typo). The builder used the sha256 to identify the file.
- **Fix:** Record and verify sha256 for every fetched file (downloads.jsonl), and treat byte counts in prose as unreliable.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-tiles-b:logs/sib/p4-tiles-b/m2b/REPORT.md

### L025. A downsampled pyramid level suffices for an 18.7 um display
- **Trap:** Reading level-0 2.4 um data for display tiles that are shown at about 18.7 um per pixel wastes bandwidth.
- **Evidence:** Paris 4 E2 census build used surface-volume level 2 (9.6 um in-plane) with one HTTP range request per chunk of 45 contiguous slices (46,714 reads, 896 absent chunks as fill 0); rebuilding a tile from level 1 gave mean |diff| 1.28 u8, p99 6 u8, Pearson 0.99936; 160 tiles took 1728 s at 32 range threads.
- **Fix:** Read the coarsest pyramid level at or below the display resolution with contiguous-slice range requests, and cross-check one tile at the next finer level.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-pairs0814b:logs/sib/pairs0814b/e2/REPORT.md

### L026. Partial-coverage scans: predictions are 0 where the mesh leaves the scan volume
- **Trap:** Tiling official predictions from a 1.129 um scan that covers only the central/inner scroll; tiles outside the scan are blank (21 byte-identical PNGs) and would dilute the census.
- **Evidence:** Per-tile zero fraction tracked the fraction of mesh points outside the volume's L0 extent (Pearson 0.998); coverage rule kept 64 of 106 mesh-valid tiles on the known-text strip.
- **Fix:** Add a geometric eligibility rule (< 50 % of a tile's mesh points outside the scan extent), set before any read and never using prediction values.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-4-A1, #METRIC-HASH-27

### L027. Paris 4 title search: official statements and odds
- **Trap:** Assuming the Paris 4 title region is located or has visible ink.
- **Evidence:** Organizers state the expected title region 'has shown no detectable ink so far', possibly a different ink, and that its top rows are physically missing; no official page gives the title's winding, segment or coordinates; the title follows the end of the primary text. The project estimated its odds at well under 3 %. The prize needs a tifxyz mesh with low-distortion flattening and an image papyrologists can read.
- **Fix:** Treat title search as low-odds; never infer title words from scholarship; let organizers' papyrologists read the image.

### L028. The 8 Paris 4 labelled segments are in ink_9um's training set
- **Trap:** Measuring base-model AUC on Paris 4 labelled segments as generalisation.
- **Evidence:** Reconnaissance: the ink_9um aligned Paris 4 set has 8 cases (no w04; w08 unused), and step-075000 seed42 trained on all 8.

### L029. No official ink predictions exist on the First Letters eligible volumes
- **Trap:** Hoping to read organizer ink maps of eligible scrolls.
- **Evidence:** A bucket scan found official ink predictions only on PHerc1447, which had left eligibility.

### L030. The published Paris 4 volume is SAM2-masked, so anything outside the scroll body is gone
- **Trap:** Searching for detached tags/fragments or recovering no-data areas from the published 2.4 um volume.
- **Evidence:** The SAM2 mask zeroes 99.5-100 % of the 0.5-5 mm search shell around the body (P4-TAG NOT TESTABLE; the detector itself found 17/24 planted tabs). Raw-CT coverage of 46 no-data test tiles equals the official present share (correlation 1.000, extra <= 1.9 %): the raw volume is absent exactly where the surface volume is, so recovery is not feasible (and would cost about 16-20 h/tile with the numpy renderer).
- **Fix:** Check mask coverage before designing outside-body or gap-filling searches; an unmasked volume is needed for them.

### L031. Map labels at the training grid's resolution, not one sample per mesh vertex
- **Trap:** Using per-vertex label sampling (one sample per 20 x 20 px vertex cell) for a stride-4 (9.6 um) loss on 10-20 um ink deposits.
- **Evidence:** own-lead requested label shards on the x4 per-tile grid with bilinear UV interpolation inside strip quads; p4-excl delivered 229 shards (x4 grid, 37,166,343 covered px, 9,404,274 ink px) that never touch the excluded zone.
- **Fix:** Sample labels per output pixel (bilinear UV, exact closest point on the labelled segment) and record the label resolution in the recipe before training.

### L032. Published Paris 4 layout (Cronache Ercolanesi 54, 2024)
- **Trap:** Estimating column layout from noisy census patterns alone.
- **Evidence:** Extracted by an isolated agent (layout only, 0 Greek characters): last column short (7 lines) ending with a final stop; up to 18-19 lines per column within <= 11.37 cm revealed height of a 16.75 cm roll; upper margin lost; column width ~6.2 cm, intercolumn ~1.7 cm, pitch 7.9 cm; 16 columns over ~1.2 m revealed, ~160 columns in the roll; the title was not found and is probably near the final columns in an unsegmented area; data were the 2019 EduceLab scans.
- **Fix:** Use published layout facts to set priors, extracted by an isolated agent so the orchestrator stays blind to the edited text.

### L033. Check where organizer labels exist before reading 'no detectable ink' statements
- **Trap:** Assuming the organizers annotated the expected title slot as blank.
- **Evidence:** Per-tile label coverage (computed in code, never displayed): coverage 0 in every expected-title-slot tile except 141 of 145,132 samples at one edge; the adjacent known-text column had coverage 0.05-0.29 with ink fractions 0.19-0.34. The slot was never annotated; the organizers' statement concerns model output on an unlabelled area.

### L034. No-data holes of the public 2.4 um Paris 4 scan cannot be recovered from the raw CT
- **Trap:** Planning to re-render missing surface-volume areas from the raw volume.
- **Evidence:** Across 46 listed tiles the raw-CT share present equals the surface-volume share present (correlation 1.000; at most 1.9 % extra); the raw volume is masked wherever the surface volume is missing. The render method itself was faithful (per-layer median Pearson 0.9887-0.9955) but cost 16-20 h and ~5.0 GB of raw data per tile.
- **Fix:** Treat such areas as unobserved; only a new scan can cover them. Check raw-CT presence before any expensive re-render.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#P4-NODATA-RECOVERY-RESULT; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md#P4-NODATA-RECOVERY-RESULT; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census

### L035. Organizer segments smaller than one 2 x 2 cm cell yield few or no tiles
- **Trap:** Expecting First Letters material from a scroll's organizer segments without checking their area against the 4 cm2 tile.
- **Evidence:** PHerc0800: all 6 organizer segments are 0.41-2.45 cm2; the three rendered (1.62-2.37 cm2) gave 2, 0 and 0 tiles under the 50 % valid rule, so most material had to come from auto-grow. The FL-1 worker found the specified grow input (surface-m7) absent; only a lasagna representation existed, and growing from it would be a new, undeclared method.
- **Fix:** Inventory segment areas and available representations per scroll before assigning a pipeline; declare any new grow representation before data.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4v-06:README.md; dominion:sib-p4-layout:logs/sib/fl-pherc0800/ASK.md

### L036. Many eligible scrolls have no organizer segments; grow your own and stream the surface prediction
- **Trap:** Planning a First Letters pass that expects organizer tifxyz segments on every scroll.
- **Evidence:** No segments/ prefix (or 0 tifxyz) on the bucket for PHerc0826, PHerc0175A, PHerc0846A, PHerc0490A and PHerc0490B; PHerc0826's surface prediction is about 1.1 TB raw at level 0 (16920 x 8169 x 8169 u8, 192^3 chunks) and cannot be downloaded on 26 GB free; vc_grow_seg_from_seed at villa 41701aa accepts s3:// volumes. PHerc1203's organizer segments ranked 4-9 were all below 16 cm^2, so pass 2 had nothing to render.
- **Fix:** List the bucket per scroll first, plan auto-growth with declared and tested grow parameters, seed from the official umbilicus where available, and stream predictions remotely with a bounded cache.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-rh-e2:logs/sib/rh-e2/ASK.md; dominion:sib-tracer:logs/sib/fl-pherc0175a/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-pairs0814b:logs/sib/fl2-pherc0846a/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-pairs0139c:logs/sib/fl2-pherc1203/STATUS.md

### L037. Raw 404 chunk counts over-flag missing data near mesh edges
- **Trap:** Using a tile's total count of missing chunks as its no-data measure.
- **Evidence:** On the top row of the title-zone strip tiles had 761-1127 missing chunks, rising with the off-mesh fraction (0.139-0.194), because the count includes off-mesh area and the 160 px halo; yet the known-text tiles there (761-832 missing) read 8-10 letters.
- **Fix:** Measure missingness inside the mesh-valid area only (or from the zero-input constant in the map); never apply a raw-count rule to a positive-control area.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:logs/owner/AUDIT_2026-09-30.md, RULES.md#DECL-P4-25-A11-A1

### L038. PHerc0268's roll axis is volume z, not y: axial telescoping fools a quick look
- **Trap:** In the inner ~25 mm the sheets lie nearly parallel to the z-slices (face-on crosshatched fibres in xy, horizontal strata in xz/yz), so interior slices suggest a horizontal (y) roll axis. The repo README and earlier exploratory notes stated 'Roll axis = volume y'; a y-axis umbilicus file had no control_points and frac_z_confident 0.0.
- **Evidence:** Rim structure tensor on 24 chunks (z ~6000/9000/11500, 8 azimuths) in a cylinder frame about the umbilicus: E[n_phi^2]=0.089 (isotropic 0.333), E[n_r^2]=0.460, E[n_z^2]=0.451. U2, 215 L2 blocks: in-plane normals point radially, mean |cos| 0.900 vs 0.637 random, equally in y-offset (0.906) and x-offset (0.895) blocks. Body 110.6 mm in z vs 83.4 (y) / 88.3 mm (x); principal axis (0.94, 0.33, -0.06). Catalog flags and the published tracks also use the z layout.
- **Fix:** Decide the roll axis from structure-tensor normals decomposed in a cylinder frame at the rim (n_phi^2 ~ 0 about the true axis) at both y-offset and x-offset azimuths, plus shape and photo, before any banding. villa spiral fitting has no option for an axis other than z, so a wrong axis cannot be configured away.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-09..2026-10-10 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/SPIRAL_STUDY.md, docs/units/U2-umbilicus.md, README.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#UMB-GEOMETRY-RESULT; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (UMB-GEOMETRY-RESULT); pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/units/U2-umbilicus.md; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (PHerc0268 frame (roll-axis) determination)

### L039. Measure sheet thickness, pitch and chunk layout natively instead of assuming them
- **Trap:** Designing operators around an assumed 100-200 um sheet and 192^3 chunks.
- **Evidence:** At level 0 in an edge window: sheet width median 122 um (p10 54, p90 295; 12-14 voxels), pitch median 380 um. In the crushed interior the competitor distance is p10/p50 8-10/14-16 voxels with no lattice (autocorrelation at lag 44 median -0.19). Level-0 chunks are 128^3 (2.1 MB), not 192^3; level-2 CT rows were sparse (385 of 696 chunks present). PHerc0268 exists only at 8.64 um in the open data.
- **Fix:** Read .zarray metadata and run a small native census before freezing any operator parameter.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#UNR-X0-SURVEY-RESULT, #DECL-E2E-2, #OBS-SURVEY-RESULT, #VC3D-AUDIT-RESULT

### L040. Outward sense CW comes from catalog flags only; catalog values can be wrong and a wrong sense cannot be fitted away
- **Trap:** Taking spiral_outward_sense from the catalog (z_direction_is_top_to_bottom=false, left_handed_coordinates=false -> CW) as confirmed.
- **Evidence:** Every spiral transform component preserves orientation, so a wrong CW/ACW cannot be absorbed by the flow; checkpoints refuse a mismatched sense. The villa README example lists PHerc0826 as CW but its catalog flags (true, false) give ACW. U2's own CT trace of one sheet through a full turn was inconclusive (telescoping, folds, radial cracks; a thin outer line was the container film).
- **Fix:** Confirm the sense independently: an A/B fit CW vs ACW on one band with laminated outer turns (unit SEN1), or a VC3D trace of one sheet through a full turn at >= 3 heights. PHerc0343 has the same flags and fitted with CW, which is supporting but not confirming.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/SPIRAL_STUDY.md, docs/units/U2-umbilicus.md

### L041. Extract one z band of the 25 GB published tracks with HTTP range reads instead of downloading everything
- **Trap:** Downloading the full 13.2 GB DBM + ~13 GB .vctracks per sandbox (disk 30 GB; the full DBM load also takes ~260 s).
- **Evidence:** band_tracks.py downloads 3 x 376 MB index arrays, then multipart Range requests (nginx answers 400 at ~14 kB of Range header; <= 7000 header chars, ~300 ranges per request). Band 9500-10000: 2,659,851 tracks in 75.5 s, 2.51 GB peak RSS, 787 MB DBM; validated IDENTICAL (SHA-256 match) to the full DBM through villa load_tracks_from_dbm; fit load 9.8 s vs 258 s from the full DBM.
- **Fix:** Use tools/tracks/band_tracks.py Z0 Z1 --name 2um_ds2_ps256_surf_v2.dbm with a wider-than-fit window (a wider store is harmless, a narrower one loses tracks); keep --index-cache between bands.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/units/U3-tracks.md

### L042. Lasagna group/scale must be paired: normal_zarr_group '2' <-> lasagna_scale 4; the defaults misregister silently
- **Trap:** Leaving the defaults normal_zarr_group '4' with lasagna_scale 4 on PHerc0268.
- **Evidence:** Store .zattrs: group 2 scale 4.0, 3 = 8.0, 4 = 16.0. With defaults ('4', 4): z_begin >= 3712 raises 'lasagna z-ROI is empty'; smaller z_begin reads the 16x store at 4x indices (spatially misregistered) with only a WARNING, and only if scroll_zarr is set.
- **Fix:** Set normal_zarr_group '2' with lasagna_scale 4 (or 3<->8, 4<->16) in spiral-scroll.json and check prepare_lasagna_volume accepts z_origin = floor(z_begin/4).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/SPIRAL_STUDY.md, docs/units/U2-umbilicus.md

### L043. Two incompatible 'spiral fitting methods' exist; the one that read PHerc0343 is the pinned 0fb38c45 version
- **Trap:** Following the live tutorial code (villa main, a329895) and assuming it is the method that produced the PHerc0343 letters.
- **Evidence:** Main (A) has no surf-SDT input and no phase mode (dense spacing grad_mag or winding_model; winding_model needs a GPU-made winding_inference + shell); 0fb38c45 (B) uses tracks + lasagna normals + surf-SDT + umbilicus, phase mode, no patches, 30000 steps on a GPU. B's spiral-scroll.json is strict (unknown keys are errors), A is lenient; fiber coordinate scale is always 0.25 in B.
- **Fix:** Produce B inputs first (automatic, CPU-feasible), pin both SHAs in every config, keep a B-strict spiral-scroll.json and a separate A variant passed with --scroll-spec.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/SPIRAL_STUDY.md

### L044. Several spiral inputs cannot be produced automatically or have no consumer at all
- **Trap:** Spending effort to produce every input listed in the reference dataset.
- **Evidence:** winding_inference/ needs a CUDA GPU, a trained 3-D winding model and a prior fit; fiber_directions.npz needs a fiber prediction that does not exist for PHerc0268; fibers/, PCL winding annotations and patch verification need a person in VC3D; eval_fibers and patch_normals are read by no code in A or B.
- **Fix:** Build only what the chosen code path reads (for B: spiral-scroll.json, umbilicus, tracks, lasagna nx/ny, surf-SDT); route human inputs to a separate human unit.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/SPIRAL_STUDY.md

### L045. Lasagna normals are not CT-masked and under-represent z-dominant sheet normals
- **Trap:** Trusting lasagna nx/ny (weight 100 in phase mode) as unbiased sheet normals on a telescoped roll.
- **Evidence:** Outside the scroll the stores hold 218 = (0.709, 0.709, 0); mean n_z^2 0.22-0.23 from lasagna vs 0.55 from the CT structure tensor. Cause unknown.
- **Fix:** Pack resident pools with CT masking; per band compare decoded nx/ny with CT tensor normals in ~10 blocks; if biased, A/B-test a lower loss_weight_dense_normals.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/SPIRAL_STUDY.md

### L046. The masked PHerc0268 volume is truncated on chunk boundaries: those faces are not the physical ends
- **Trap:** Treating z 896 and z 13951 as the ends of the roll.
- **Evidence:** Papyrus continuous z 896-13695; z 13696-13823 empty (exactly chunk 107); a detached slab z 13824-13951; z 13952-14335 blanked (constant 43); holder slab z 632-759; both faces flat on 128-slice chunk boundaries.
- **Fix:** Treat the ends as masking/export truncations; ask whether an unmasked volume exists before claiming anything about the roll's ends.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/units/U2-umbilicus.md, docs/SPIRAL_STUDY.md

### L047. m7 is effectively binary; the SDT threshold choice is moot
- **Trap:** Tuning the m7 binarisation threshold for the distance field.
- **Evidence:** One m7 level-1 block (28,311,552 voxels) holds only 0 (19,565,880) and 255 (8,745,672), so every threshold 1..255 gives the same mask (checked on one block, not the whole volume).
- **Fix:** Keep threshold 128 from the recipe; spend effort elsewhere.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/units/U4-sdt.md

### L048. Audit calibration and validation sets for scroll identity
- **Trap:** A renderer-calibration pool contained a sample from another scroll (PHerc1203), contaminating the calibration.
- **Evidence:** The pool contained a PHerc1203 organizer segment sampled in the PHerc0268 volume; the VC3D calibration was withdrawn (SUPERSEDED_CLAIMS S2). The five real PHerc0268 VC3D surfaces were 10-76 deg off the sheet orientation. The FL-2/FL-4 squares behind an earlier '43 reads, 0 positives' sat at random orientation (58-74 deg): those reads are void.
- **Fix:** Before any read or calibration, check each surface's source scroll/uuid and its normal-vs-structure-tensor angle; void reads on surfaces that fail.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#2, docs/SUPERSEDED_CLAIMS.md#S2; pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/POC.md, docs/FL_SEARCH.md; pherc0268:43e91ca:commit-message

### L049. Published PHerc0268 spiral tracks stop at z = 4500; regenerate the missing ~21 % with the organizers' own extractor
- **Trap:** Assuming the published tracks cover the whole scroll; low-z bands then load no tracks (or fail to load at all).
- **Evidence:** extract.json: z_min 4500 / effective_z_bounds [4500, 14833] (a batch-wide setting also used for PHerc0343, 0826, 0139, 0343P, 0800, 0009B, not a Scroll 1 default). About 20.8 % of CT papyrus (>90) and 24.2 % of predicted surface lie below z 4500. T0's CPU wrapper around villa extract_surface_tracks.py with the published parameters reproduced the published tracks exactly on the overlap (horizontal 601,994/601,994 identical; vertical exact on the full-slab test) at 42.6 min, 7.5 GiB peak and 3.5 GB of m7 mirror per 640-slice band.
- **Fix:** Run tools/lowz/extract_band.py (published parameters set as module constants, Z0' = 4 mod 8) and validate_lowz.py (must print ALL CHECKS PASSED) before refitting low-z windows with tracks; compare vertical slabs on full-z slabs, since band-local vertical slabs only span the window.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/BANDS.md, docs/SPIRAL_STUDY.md, docs/units/U3-tracks.md

**Geometry and segmentation (L050-L133).** Registration between scans, mesh audits, surface tracing, winding counts, umbilicus and spiral fitting. The recurring failure: surfaces that leave the sheet while numeric gates still pass (L097, L100, L101).

### L050. Mapping 2.4 um maps to the 9 um canvas: plain scaling is ~7 px off; use the offset formula
- **Trap:** Mapping canvas pixels by a plain scale N9/N2 misplaces the 2.4 um reference by several pixels; also the last canvas pixels have no source.
- **Evidence:** reg0009b label mapper c2 = (c9 + 10) N2/N9 - 10 (N = canvas extents = 20 x mesh grid, checked equal to the zarr shapes; within 2 px everywhere); reg0841 mesh fit found canvas offset o = 10 best for every segment and CHAIN VALID uses c9 = (c2 + 10) N9/N2 - 10; pairs0814 recorded the separable rule with 10.5. The declared +10 offset leaves the last ~7 canvas px of each axis without source (READ-CAL-2). Also: Plain scaling is 7.4 px off (matches an archived ~75 um warning). Formula c9 = (c2 + 10) N9/N2 - 10 with exact separable area averaging: synthetic error 0.012 px; residual median <= 0.7 px, worst 2.5 px on 0139; no flip (CT NCC 0.61-0.71 unflipped vs <= 0.012 flipped). Meshes imply an offset of 10.49-10.51 (0.37 px difference, negligible). N2/N9 per axis within 0.07 % of F = 3.897628 on 0841.
- **Fix:** Use c9 = (c2 + 10) N9/N2 - 10 for organizer canvases, verify N against zarr shapes, clamp boxes that map below 0, and count the uncovered edge pixels as invalid.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#B0841-BANK, #RCBANK-1; dominion:sib-reg0009b:logs/sib/reg0009b/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-reg0841:logs/sib/reg0841/chainvalid/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-pairs0814:logs/sib/pairs0814/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-readcal2:logs/sib/readcal2/REPORT.md

### L051. Record which inputs are measured and which are inherited from metadata
- **Trap:** Treating every spiral-fit input as measured. For PHerc0268, unit U2 delivered an axis verdict (high confidence) and an umbilicus curve of 82 control points, but the curve is a curvature centre, not an identified innermost turn, and the outward sense was inherited from the catalogue.
- **Evidence:** Two independent centre objectives disagree by 2-7 mm at mid heights (9-14 mm near the ends). The required own check (a sheet followed outward in >= 3 sections) was inconclusive, so the outward sense is not CT-confirmed. The unit also found a catalogue example inconsistent with the catalogue's own rule. Verdict: inconclusive.
- **Fix:** Record for every input whether it was measured or inherited from metadata, and carry inherited inputs as stated assumptions.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-10-14 (family period) · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/units/U2-umbilicus.md; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Spiral-fit inputs for PHerc0268: umbilicus, axis and outward sense (unit U2))

### L052. Validate geometry tile by tile before running ink, and size test patches to exceed letter height plus line spacing
- **Trap:** Running ink on a fitted patch before validating its geometry, on a patch too short to hold a letter (PoC v0/v1: fit -> snap -> render -> ink).
- **Evidence:** Only about 0.5 cm^2 of a single band window showed continuous single-sheet fibres (PoC v0; patch only 2.19 mm tall). Window seams after snapping were 8-56 vox, so no stitched sheet existed. Growth to 4.6 cm^2 left 9 of 18 tiles on-sheet (about 2 cm^2). Verdict: failed.
- **Fix:** Validate geometry tile by tile before running ink, and size test patches to exceed letter height plus line spacing; otherwise an ink null carries no information.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-10-14 (family period) · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/POC.md, poc/v1/seams.json (summary in commit message), poc/v1/layer_profile_tiles.json (summary in commit message); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Proof-of-concept patch: fit -> snap -> render -> ink (PoC v0/v1))

### L053. The stitching works mechanically, but a strip is only as good as the surfaces under it
- **Trap:** Taking a working unrolling tool as evidence that the strip it builds follows one sheet.
- **Evidence:** ringstrip (patch-to-strip unrolling) was published in the October package: 2/2 tests pass on a fresh clone (pytest, 0.39 s) and the reproduce script was checked. It unrolled five real patches into one 10,513 x 2,507 px strip. It assumes its patches lie on one winding (L155).
- **Fix:** Validate surface identity (for example with xsec cross-sections, L101) before stitching ink maps.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-10-10 (family period) · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:logs/pp/verify_ringstrip.json, logs/pp/SUBMIT_SHEET_OCT2026.md; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (ringstrip: patch-to-strip unrolling)

### L054. Cross-resolution CT NCC around 0.76-0.82 reflects scan PSF, not misregistration
- **Trap:** Treating a cross-resolution NCC below 0.80 between a mapped 2.4 um slice and the 9 um SV as a failed registration gate.
- **Evidence:** 0841: whole segments 0.763-0.770 at zero shift (best 0.768-0.778 at shift (1,0)); J windows 0.723-0.821, all best shifts <= 1.41 px. Recorded as a diagnostic, not the declared gate (which compares our 9 um render with the organizer 9 um SV and reached 0.96-0.97).
- **Fix:** Gate alignment same-resolution (our render vs organizer SV); use cross-resolution NCC only with shift search, judging the best shift, not the NCC level.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-24 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#B0841-BANK

### L055. Segments of the same scroll may be adjacent windings, not re-traces
- **Trap:** Assuming two organizer segments are two traces of one sheet.
- **Evidence:** 0841 segment 214732 lies a median 8.4 vox from w00 with only 5 % of points within 2 vox; local pitch ~8-18 vox -> may be adjacent windings (UNRESOLVED).
- **Fix:** Measure point-to-surface distance distributions and local pitch before treating segments as duplicates.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-24 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#B0841-BANK

### L056. Verify that a mesh lies on the scroll in its declared frame (CT-occupancy frame gate)
- **Trap:** Trusting a mesh's declared coordinate frame; internally consistent geometry votes do not prove the mesh is on papyrus.
- **Evidence:** 10 PHerc1447 traces (dated before the volume's own export) lie 41-91 % on zero CT and 0-19 % outside the volume; controls PHerc0139 (0-3.6 % zero CT) and PHerc0800 (0 %). Three of these had been rated HIGH by handed-1. No single z-shift fixes them (best leaves 65 % occupancy) and a 3-D translation search was degenerate. PHerc1203 raw segments were confirmed in the 9.362 um frame by implied voxel size (meta area_cm2 / area_vx2) and bbox inside the level-0 shape.
- **Fix:** Gate every mesh: FRAME-UNVERIFIED if > 5 % of vertices are on zero CT or > 1 % outside the volume; treat renders of unverified meshes as uninformative.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-handed:logs/sib/handed/REPORT.md, logs/sib/handed/h2/ct_occupancy_1447.json; dominion:sib-fl-pherc1203:logs/sib/fl-pherc1203/NOTES.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:CHANGELOG.md; dominion:sib-handed@81d525859:logs/sib/handed/REPORT.md; survey:expmap_raw.json:geometry; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:logs/pp/verify_handcheck.json, logs/pp/SUBMIT_SHEET.md; dominion:sib-pp-handcheck@2cfef810c:logs/sib/pp-handcheck/PUBLISHED.json; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (handcheck: mirror/handedness predictor)

### L057. Winding sense (up/down) needs traces spanning more than one turn; CT-only pitch-angle estimates fail
- **Trap:** Estimating the roll's winding sense from local CT sheet orientation.
- **Evidence:** Winding check F5 agreed with the organizer top flag on 36/36 PHerc0139 meshes (row spans 1.00-1.31 turns; per-mesh pair agreement 0.70-1.00). The CT-only structure-tensor pitch estimator on real PHerc0139 data split 8 positive / 8 negative per slice (a0 -60..+133 vox vs an expected ~+3 vox; scatter ~20x the signal) and gave the wrong sign for PHerc0841 at level 2; its 26-volume run was stopped.
- **Fix:** Require >= 2 frame-verified traces each with a row spanning >= 1.05 turns and >= 200 pairs at agreement >= 0.8, all agreeing on w; make no CT-only up/down claim.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-handed:logs/sib/handed/REPORT.md, logs/sib/handed/h2/spiral_sense_0139_L1.json; dominion:sib-handed@81d525859:logs/sib/handed/REPORT.md (section 12.2); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (CT-only winding-sense estimator)

### L058. Same-papyrus tests cannot separate a re-trace from windings pressed into contact
- **Trap:** Using one distance form to group re-traced segments into papyrus units.
- **Evidence:** Normal-distance rule (SAME iff >= 1000 samples within 2 vox and count[0,1) >= 2 x count[2,3)): 31 of 437 PHerc0139 pairs SAME -> 13 units. Re-traces give c01/c23 ratios of about 50-120 but seam overlaps 2-5, and a pair asserted SAME in the real-data tests came out NOT SAME (ratio 0.8, 1.2 % within 2 vox), so the distance forms disagree.
- **Fix:** Use the fail-closed union of vertex, point-to-surface and normal-distance forms (DECL-DEVLOOP-A1) for contamination/hold-out purposes and report pairs whose verdict differs between forms; over-merging only removes training material.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-contam:logs/sib/contam/proposals/PROPOSALS.md, logs/sib/contam/ASK.md, logs/sib/contam/units_0139.json; dominion:sib-contam@9dd1af44a:logs/sib/contam/proposals/PROPOSALS.md, logs/sib/contam/planted_faults_0139.json; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (3-D training-contamination checker)

### L059. Literal nearest-vertex re-trace checks miss re-traces; use vertex OR point-to-surface (CORR-RETRACE-RULE)
- **Trap:** Testing 'same papyrus' with distances to the nearest densified mesh vertex: at the official 20-vox grid with 5 x 5 densification, vertices are 4 vox apart, so true re-traces land mostly in [1,3) vox and fail the count rule.
- **Evidence:** Synthetic fault suite: the nearest-vertex form caught 4 of 200 random re-traces (1/50 and 0/50 in stress runs); an exact re-trace offset by half a dense cell scored [0, 0, 20736] and was called NOT SAME. Point-to-triangulated-surface form caught 300 of 300 with 0 false alarms on neighbouring sheets 3-20 vox away. Also: Synthetic tribunal suite: the literal vertex rule caught only 4 of 200 re-traces. Real PHerc0139 overlaps (w023/w024, w052/w053): surface form 10/10, vertex form alone 0/10, with 0/10 false alarms on neighbouring windings 5.5-15.7 vox away. PHerc0009B: 28 of 119 pairs SAME, all via the point-to-surface form, 0 via the vertex form.
- **Fix:** Same papyrus if EITHER nearest-vertex OR point-to-surface bins give >= 1000 points within 2 vox and count[0,1) >= 2 x count[2,3) (fail-closed union); compute all clearances (128-vox exclusions, halos) point-to-surface or on meshes sampled at <= 1 vox; re-check older exclusions.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-tribunal:logs/sib/tribunal/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-reg0009b:logs/sib/reg0009b/REPORT.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#CORR-RETRACE-RULE, #DECL-DEVLOOP-A1, #D3-VERDICT; dominion:sib-reg0009b@f1b3cbf19:logs/sib/reg0009b/REPORT.md; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (PHerc0009B per-segment registration and re-trace grouping (reg0009b)); dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:logs/pp/verify_tifxyz-dist.json; dominion:sib-pp-tifxyz-dist@b98504cb5:logs/sib/pp-tifxyz-dist/accuracy.json; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:logs/pp/SUBMIT_SHEET.md; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (tifxyz-dist: certified surface clearance); dominion:sib-pp-tifxyz-dist:logs/sib/pp-tifxyz-dist/accuracy.json, tools/sib/pp-tifxyz-dist/pkg/results/RESULTS.md, logs/sib/pp-tifxyz-dist/PUBLISHED.json; dominion:sib-p4-excl@0e96a9123:logs/sib/p4-excl/REPORT.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md#P4-21-RESULT; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census

### L060. PHerc0841 9.366 <-> 2.403 um registration is non-affine: a single affine fails held-out patches
- **Trap:** Mapping between the 9 um scan and the 2.4 um rescan with one affine (as the organizer meshes do).
