- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-pp-flatcheck:tools/sib/pp-flatcheck/vc-flatcheck/README.md, tools/sib/pp-flatcheck/vc-flatcheck/results/SUMMARY.md; dominion:sib-flat1@b5594d021:logs/sib/flat1/REPORT.md (FLAT-2); survey:expmap_raw.json:geometry

### L138. The official renderer reproduces the organizer surface volume essentially exactly when called correctly
- **Trap:** Assuming render differences explain poor ink results, or calling vc_render_tifxyz without the volume argument.
- **Evidence:** vc_render_tifxyz --flip-normals -n 28 on the unlevelled team w040 mesh: pooled Pearson 0.9999990 vs team SV, 99.71 % of voxels identical, none differ by > 1, offset 0; needed -v <volume>; --auto-crop omitted to keep the SV canvas. Later renders: 0.9999989 (w044), 0.9999984 (0841).
- **Fix:** Render with official vc_render_tifxyz -v <volume> --flip-normals -n <slices> at the metadata voxel size and gate with a Pearson >= 0.999 check against the organizer SV before any inference.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#C3-RUN1, #C3-R1-VERDICT, #HECATE-SCREEN

### L139. Mask model output outside render-valid pixels before display
- **Trap:** Base model maps carry output on pixels without rendered data (up to 29 % of a window, mean output 22-67 there), while reference/sealer images are zero there: a visible difference between arms.
- **Evidence:** Builder note before D1 reads; images built before the fix were withdrawn unread.
- **Fix:** Set BASE/RAW display images to 0 outside the render-valid mask (any of the n render slices nonzero) before INTER_AREA; compute CT windowing over valid pixels only.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-D1-A6

### L140. A thin slab around a mesh that runs near the sheet midline can miss surface ink entirely
- **Trap:** Thin-slab raw-CT census, per-tile stretch (2.4 um) (failed): 3 of 160 tiles were marked as rows, with 0 letters on every tile (null 21 x 0). The known-text gate was 0 of 72 tiles, so the display is uninformative.
- **Evidence:** Global display: 0 letters on all 160 tiles (1 tile marked as rows). Per-tile stretch: 3 of 160 tiles marked as rows, 0 letters on every tile; the known-text gate read 0 of 72 tiles (bar 30 %).
- **Fix:** A thin slab around a mesh that runs near the sheet midline can miss surface ink entirely. Validate the depth before building displays.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md#P4-L2-CENSUS-RESULT, logs/p4/census_l2_summary.json; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:logs/p4/census_l2s_summary.json

### L141. Bright-voxel thin slabs around the official mesh do not show ink on known text
- **Trap:** Displaying the per-pixel max of raw 2.4 um CT over +-14.4 um around the official mesh as an ink channel.
- **Evidence:** L2 (160/160 tiles, thresholds frozen on 17 known-text control tiles: T_mid 93, T_hi 203): the blind census named 0 letters on all 160 tiles and 0 of 72 known-text tiles passed (P4-L2-CENSUS-RESULT) -> uninformative. Block detector at L2S depth: held-out text recall 0.0891 at FPR 0.0321 (bar 0.90 at FPR <= 0.05) -> FAIL. Surface-following L4 faces: held-out recall 0.074 (L4-) and 0.033 (L4+) -> FAIL.
- **Fix:** Gate every raw-CT channel on known text before building target tiles; for carbon ink on Paris 4 at 2.4 um, use a trained model (P4-OWN) instead of bright-voxel slabs.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-l2:README.md, logs/sib/p4-l2/BLOCK_FREEZE.md, logs/sib/p4-l2/PREGATE_L4.json; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#P4-L2-CENSUS-RESULT; dominion:sib-p4-l2@52d6c9102:logs/sib/p4-l2/BLOCK_FREEZE.md; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census

### L142. Global display thresholds hide rows with a lower CT baseline
- **Trap:** One set of display thresholds for a whole strip; control per-tile voxel medians were 57-81 in the top rows vs 99-108 in lower rows, so top rows render darker.
- **Evidence:** Builder numbers before any read (frozen T_mid 93, T_hi 203). Also: Per-row median of the 2.4 um slab voxel median rose from 68 (first row) to 101, and the L2 output mean from 52.7 to 80.1 across rows; a row-baseline variant (L2S) was built and its stretch domain recorded per tile.
- **Fix:** Add a per-tile linear 1-99 % stretch variant (over mesh-valid pixels with CT > 0) as its own material with its own gate and null; report gate numbers per row band.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-12-A2; dominion:sib-p4-l2:logs/sib/p4-l2/STATUS.md

### L143. Percentile contrast stretches must exclude zero (out-of-scan) pixels
- **Trap:** A per-tile 1-99 % stretch computed over all mesh-valid pixels lets no-data zeros set the low percentile and changes the display.
- **Evidence:** The raw-CT E1 rebuild (DECL-P4-5-A1) recomputed the stretch over mesh-valid pixels with slab mean > 0: 33 of 60 PNGs changed (e.g. one tile's p1 moved from 20.11 to 37.19); all 4648 re-downloaded level-3 chunks matched the original manifest sha256. The superseded tiles stay on the branch and are not to be read.
- **Fix:** Mask no-data before computing display statistics, and keep superseded displays clearly marked so no reader sees them.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-5-A1; dominion:sib-p4-tiles-b:README.md, logs/sib/p4-tiles-b/e1a1/REPORT.md

### L144. Thin surface ink deposits need depth-calibrated displays
- **Trap:** Using a thick slab mean that averages a 10-20 um deposit away.
- **Evidence:** The research dossier recorded the organizers' finding that Paris 4 ink is visible in 2.4 um raw CT as 10-20 um bright surface deposits; the E2 display (+-53 um mean) is insensitive to it; the L2 thin-slab census read 0 letters on 160 tiles with its known-text gate failing.
- **Fix:** Calibrate the display depth on known text (ink may be offset from the mesh midline) before any target read.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:CHANGELOG.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:logs/p4/census_e1_provisional.json; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census

### L145. A one-layer shift of the inference window measurably degrades a reproduced map
- **Trap:** Treating the layer window (START_LAYER/END_LAYER) as unimportant.
- **Evidence:** Running the official 2.4 um model one layer off the organizer window (flipped-frame layers 1..62 instead of 0..61) cost about 0.03 in r vs the organizer map (0.972 instead of 0.99999) and 0.005 in AUC. Start 0 with 62 layers matched the organizer's production setting, although the optimized_inference README suggests START_LAYER=1, END_LAYER=63.
- **Fix:** Pin the layer window explicitly and verify it by reproducing an organizer map before production; the 9 um official infer uses the centre 17 of 31 render slices (select_layer_indices centre crop).
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-chain2um:logs/sib/chain2um/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-fl-pherc1203:logs/sib/fl-pherc1203/NOTES.md

### L146. Derive px_per_mm from the mesh's median 3-D edge length, not from nominal voxel values
- **Trap:** Cutting 2 x 2 cm tiles from a prediction canvas using the nominal 1 px/voxel scale.
- **Evidence:** 2.4 um inner strip: median 3-D edge 19.978 vox over 56.4 M edges gives px_per_mm 417.131 (nominal 416.67), tile T = 8343 px, 9 x 21 grid, 160 of 189 read-eligible (623.27 cm2); area cross-check +1.1 % vs mesh meta. 1.129 um L1: 443.622 (nominal 442.87), T = 8872 px, +0.5 %. Known-text control 2.4 um: 415.04 px/mm (T = 8301 px).
- **Fix:** Compute grid geometry from the tifxyz mesh (canvas/grid ratio, median edge, per-axis values) and cross-check summed tile area against the mesh's own area.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-tiles-a:logs/sib/p4-tiles-a/REPORT.md, logs/sib/p4-tiles-a/m2a/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-p4-tiles-b:README.md

### L147. Official inference centre-crops slices, a half-voxel shift from the surface
- **Trap:** Assuming organizer surface-volume inference sees the same depth window as a -n 31 render path.
- **Evidence:** READ-CAL-2 noise maps came from the organizer SV path, whose official inference centre-crops slices 6..22 (centre 14 vs surface 13.5), a half-voxel shift relative to the D1 render path.
- **Fix:** Record which depth window each inference path uses and keep it identical across arms being compared.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-readcal2:logs/sib/readcal2/REPORT.md

### L148. Mineral red inks survive carbonisation and are high-Z; organic lakes are invisible to a density channel
- **Trap:** Assuming a title in a different ink will appear in carbon-ink model outputs or in slab means.
- **Evidence:** Physics reasoning recorded: HgS, Pb3O4/PbO, Fe2O3 survive 300-400 C and attenuate far more at 78 keV; a 5-30 um layer is diluted by a +-53 um mean; lead-bearing black ink has been reported in Herculaneum papyri.
- **Fix:** Use a thin-slab maximum (+-15 um) with thresholds from a known-text control and an in-sheet vs gap-slab test; disclose the organic-lake blind spot.
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-6

### L149. Disclose small coverage gaps in a tile record instead of patching the output
- **Trap:** Silently filling pixels that no model window covered, which changes the declared pipeline output that the blind read and the manifest hash refer to.
- **Evidence:** o5w2: about 1.4 % of mesh-valid pixels got no window and were written as 0 (coverage_of_valid 0.98584); o5w1 coverage_of_valid 0.98657. Both were disclosed and left unchanged, and the tile hashes matched the stage manifest.
- **Fix:** Record coverage_of_valid and valid_fraction per tile, compare valid_fraction to the manifest value, and leave gaps as declared output.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-o5w2:README.md; dominion:sib-o5w1:README.md

### L150. Surface-following face extraction can absorb or leak bright deposits
- **Trap:** Finding recto/verso faces by run-length of voxels above T_mid around the mesh.
- **Evidence:** L4 unit tests: faces found within 1 slice and ink planted 10 um outside recovered (+88 u8), but a deposit brighter than T_mid is bridged into the sheet run, and when the deposit lies nearer the mesh than the sheet it is taken as the sheet (7 % / 21 % of ink px), leaking ink into the other face. Control face thickness median-of-p50 28.8 um.
- **Fix:** Unit-test face finders with deposits on both sides and nearer than the sheet; report leakage rates with the channel.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-l2:logs/sib/p4-l2/STATUS.md, logs/sib/p4-l2/PREGATE_L4.json

### L151. A contact print keeps the canvas (u, v) orientation: do not mirror offset maps
- **Trap:** Mirroring offset (contact-print) maps left-right, as if viewing the facing face from its own side.
- **Evidence:** On the flattened canvas both windings share (u along the spiral, v along the axis) at the contact, so a contact print keeps (u, v) and reads in its true direction in canvas coordinates; the earlier declared mirror was amended.
- **Fix:** Read verso/offset maps un-mirrored in canvas coordinates; disclose the derivation.
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-26-A2

### L152. A grid tiler on small canvases discards most of the surface; use cover tiling
- **Trap:** Cutting fixed 2 x 2 cm grid tiles from ~11.7 cm2 FL-4 canvases.
- **Evidence:** Under the first FL-4 kit the grid tiler kept only one cell of each ~11.7 cm2 canvas; DECL-FL-4-A2 replaced it with cover tiling plus a whole-segment window.
- **Fix:** Choose the tiling scheme from the canvas size; check the fraction of valid area that ends up in tiles.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4v-14:README.md

### L153. Render large segments in pieces; pieces match the full canvas to within one grey level, not byte for byte
- **Trap:** Requiring byte-identical inference outputs across different crop origins, or rendering whole 40-60 cm^2 segments on a small disk.
- **Evidence:** PHerc0139 FL-2 gate: pieces of <= ~12 cm^2 with the crop origin on the 64-px inference stride grid reproduced w050's full-canvas tiles with 3-6 of 1,140,624 px differing by at most 1 grey level, ink_score equal, Pearson 1.00000 (0 of 4 tiles byte-identical). In contrast, re-computing the same tile with identical code and model gave byte-identical PNGs across sessions (own-model repro tiles).
- **Fix:** Crop on the inference stride grid and compare pieces with a +-1 grey-level tolerance; require byte identity only for identical inputs and crops.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-pairs0139c:logs/sib/pairs0139c/fl2_gate/STATUS.md, logs/sib/pairs0139c/STATUS.md

### L154. The PHerc0139 title strip holds no 2 x 2 cm tile under the template tiler
- **Trap:** Assuming the known-text title segment can serve as a gate under an unchanged 2 cm tiler.
- **Evidence:** The organizer title segment's 9.362 um canvas is 1780 x 5360 px (1.67 x 5.02 cm, 7.20 cm^2); the template tiler keeps only whole 2 cm (2136 px) cells, so 0 tiles; no other of 38 organizer PHerc0139 segments intersects its bounding box (+-50 vox).
- **Fix:** Check segment height against the tile size before choosing gate material; declare a strip tiling (full-height cells, padded) if a short strip must be used.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-pairs0139c:logs/sib/pairs0139c/fl2_gate/ASK.md, logs/sib/pairs0139c/fl2_gate/STATUS.md

### L155. Unrolled strips are readable layouts, not isometric flattenings, and assume one winding
- **Trap:** Placing many grown patches on one strip by azimuth and height hides that a patch spanning two windings overlaps itself.
- **Evidence:** ringstrip: two synthetic patches overlapping in azimuth unroll with a continuous line (> 90 % bright); five PHerc0268 2 x 2 cm patches at r/R 0.70 unrolled into one 10,513 x 2,507 px strip whose ink_9um map is uniform speckle because the surfaces jump layers.
- **Fix:** Use strip unrolling only for maps already rendered on verified single-sheet patches; verify the surfaces first (xsec).
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-03 · **Sources:** ringstrip:HEAD:README.md

### L156. Resample mesh columns to the render scale before rendering
- **Trap:** Column spacing was assumed to be 20 vox on meshes whose real spacing was larger, so text would have been compressed sideways ("squeezed renders").
- **Evidence:** Recorded in the project's private log; no public numbers (main docs/LESSONS.md #4, labelled VERIFIED (record)).
- **Fix:** Resample columns to the render scale before rendering, and check the render aspect against the mesh arc length.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-09..2026-10-14 (approx.) · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#4

### L157. Pick ink depth from the local layer peak, not the global profile peak
- **Trap:** A per-strip "band-matched depth" used the global CT-profile peak, which picked a neighbouring sheet in 18 of 50 strips.
- **Evidence:** m7-centred PHerc0268 meshes peak at layer 31-33; the ink-face window starts at about layer 21-23 (d = -2...-4); on the PHerc0343 control a 3-layer outward misalignment roughly halves the strokes. The recipe picked d = +1 after sweeping -15..+15 on its own meshes; d -3..+3 is unvalidated on PHerc0268.
- **Fix:** Measure the mean-CT layer profile per render and align the ink window to that render's sheet centre; sweep depth on a control first.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#5; pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/FL_SEARCH.md, docs/PIPELINE.md

### L158. Never average recto and verso maps or stretch each ink image on its own
- **Trap:** Averaging forward and reverse maps mixes recto and verso, and a per-image contrast stretch turns noise into "ink" (the withdrawn v0 image).
- **Evidence:** Convention verified on the recipe's PHerc0343 letters: inside the letter boxes 12.4 % of pixels have p > 0.55 vs 0.4 % outside (31x) on the reverse map; the forward direction gives 0 %. The PoC v0 ink image averaged forward and reverse and was withdrawn (SUPERSEDED_CLAIMS S3). The fixed-scale display reproduces the public PHerc0343 control letters (release fig. 3).
- **Fix:** Use only the reading-face map: the order that reproduces the PHerc0343 control letters on this render frame (for the villa PHerc0268 pipeline with outward normals, the reverse order; on --flip-normals renders, official FORWARD; see L135); display on a FIXED absolute scale, p 0.40 -> 0.70 (METHODS 7, scripts/pipeline/overlay.py); validate every display change on a positive control.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#3, docs/SUPERSEDED_CLAIMS.md#S3, docs/METHODS.md#7; pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/FL_SEARCH.md; pherc0268:a0774a8:commit-message

### L159. Mirror exactly the CT chunks a mesh touches before rendering; streaming is fetch-bound
- **Trap:** Rendering winding-scale meshes with vc_render_tifxyz streaming from S3.
- **Evidence:** Mirrored: 5.5-5.8 CPU-s/cm2, 1.56-1.74 s/cm2 wall with 4 threads, 0.86 MB/mm2 output; streaming 11-25 s/cm2. --pyramid 0 is bit-identical at L0; 66-layer profiles vs an independent trilinear sample r = 0.9996. Peak RSS grows ~2.2 MB per present chunk (full windings 2-3.5 GB). The 41701aa build over-fetches on winding-scale meshes.
- **Fix:** Mirror the exact chunk list first (crop_and_chunks + mirror), render with --pyramid 0, and verify 200 random profiles against a trilinear sample (r >= 0.99).
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/PIPELINE.md

### L160. Render only the layers the ink model reads
- **Trap:** Rendering 66 layers for every region when storage or CPU is tight.
- **Evidence:** One single-depth villa ink map needs only ~17 layers (33+d-8 ... +17); a d -3..+3 sweep needs layers 22..44.
- **Fix:** Render the layer window the chosen depths need; keep only the CT layers the panels need (KEEP_RENDER=0).
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/PIPELINE.md, tools/fl/batch_ink.sh

### L161. Padding thin strips with extra real rows does not restore ink recall
- **Trap:** Fixing short strips by rendering 2 extra node rows each side and scoring only the target rows.
- **Evidence:** Pre-registered P13 arm: recall 0.52 against a bar of 0.7 (r 0.86); exploratory extrapolated padding ~ real padding (recall 0.50). 20-row strips: recall 0.63 (CI 0.49-0.72), E 18, r 0.89, 'sees ink, narrowly'. Also: RESULTS 1: P13 recall 0.517 [0.397, 0.616], r 0.858, E 26.3 (fix bar recall >= 0.7, r >= 0.8 not met).
- **Fix:** Render strips with generous real context (or stitch taller strips) and still validate on a positive control.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/FL_SEARCH.md, poc/ctrl343_strips/DECL.md, poc/ctrl343_strips/eval.out; dominion:main:docs/RESULTS.md#1

### L162. Margin fill restores sensitivity but raises off-letter strong pixels; measure its no-ink floor
- **Trap:** Reflect-filling the margin restores in-box strong ink (F13 recall 0.646) but doubles strong pixels outside the letters (1.35 % vs 0.67 % full context at the same pixels; up to 3.56 % vs 1.25 % on one strip) and misses the stricter fix bar (recall >= 0.7, r >= 0.8).
- **Evidence:** RESULTS 1 (F13 E 10.7 vs P13 26.3; CI [0.499, 0.768] spans both bars). Also: Exploratory fill arm on PHerc0343: in-box strong 14.4 % vs 15.4 % full surface, box AUC 0.703 vs 0.709, but strong ink outside the boxes 1.35 % vs ~0.6 %, concentrated near filled edges. Fill no-ink floor on +8-vox displaced PHerc0343 strips: 0.23-0.67 %.
- **Fix:** Use the fill as a mitigation, not a cure; always report the out-of-letter rate with it and run the positive control in the exact geometry.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/FL_SEARCH.md, poc/mass_fill/DECL.md; dominion:main:docs/RESULTS.md#1

### L163. Know the renderer's blank margin before cutting strips
- **Trap:** vc_render_tifxyz gives border nodes no central-difference normal and does not render the last cell, so a strip render carries all-zero rows: at least 30 at the bottom; 30 at the top where node row 0 is invalid, otherwise 10. A 260 px (13-row) render is valid on at most rows 10-229.
- **Evidence:** METHODS 3 (VERIFIED on the renders at villa 41701aa; the renderer has changed since, 208 files, and the margin is unverified there).
- **Fix:** Measure the blank margin of your renderer version before inference; re-verify after any renderer upgrade.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/METHODS.md#3

### L164. Some crops fall outside the scanned volume; absent chunks still cost a round trip
- **Trap:** Screening crops without checking CT chunk existence.
- **Evidence:** 9 mass-run crops lay outside the scanned volume (CT chunks absent on S3). Absent chunks still cost ~0.10 s vs 0.19 s per request in snap.
- **Fix:** Check chunk presence (occupancy at a coarse level) before scheduling render/ink.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/FL_SEARCH.md, docs/PIPELINE.md

## Part 2. Lessons: ink, validation and reading

**Ink models and training (L165-L195).** Which public checkpoints transfer, CPU training and fine-tuning, depth order, precision, provenance and hold-outs. Recurring finding: AUC on training or adjacent papyrus overstates transfer. On Paris 4 a cross-scroll model was blind, while a small CNN trained on the scroll's own labels with a certified exclusion zone passed every control (L176, L183, L184).

### L165. Hecate 9.6 um screened out on PHerc0841
- **Trap:** Assuming the newer distilled official checkpoint (Hecate 9.6 um) beats the base model on unseen papyrus.
- **Evidence:** Official hecate.py (stride 32), renders at 9.6 um (--scale 0.975625, -n 16), on 0.066 cm^2 of held-out 0841 labels: Hecate forward 0.678 / reverse 0.470; base forward 0.576 / reverse 0.634; bar 0.75 not met.
- **Fix:** Screen new checkpoints with pixel AUC on held-out labels in both orders before spending reads; never transfer a depth-order convention between checkpoints. Note the screen rested on one segment and 0.066 cm^2.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#HECATE-SCREEN, #DECL-HECATE; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (HECATE-SCREEN); logs/d1/hecate_screen_summary.json sha256 6b90169e..., RULES.md (HECATE-SCREEN), RULES.md (DECL-HECATE); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Hecate 9.6 um zero-shot screen on PHerc0841)

### L166. Score depth order explicitly, because the wrong order drops every model toward chance
- **Trap:** Comparing ink models on a held-out scroll without fixing the depth order and the evaluation set. Reference measurement for the master-model bars: 600 held-out PHerc0343P crops at 8.64 um.
- **Evidence:** Pixel AUC in forward depth order: public dense 9 um model 0.7605 (0.7694 averaging depth windows); public 8 um model 0.7499 per crop; Hecate 9.6 um (resampled) 0.7309; base ink_9um 0.6539. Reverse order on the same crops: dense 0.5847 (0.6135 averaging depth windows), 8 um 0.5361, Hecate 0.5509, base 0.5352.
- **Fix:** Score depth order explicitly, because the wrong order drops every model toward chance. Pseudo-labels from another model also cap any held-out AUC, so the bar must be set against that ceiling.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-10-10 (family period) · **Sources:** dominion:fl4t@a250ae8c2:logs/fl7/baseline_dense/PHerc0343P_20250511003658/summary.json, logs/fl7/baseline_hecate/PHerc0343P_20250511003658/summary.json, logs/fl7/baseline_8um/PHerc0343P_20250511003658/v8in_crops_fwd.json, logs/fl7/baseline_8um/PHerc0343P_20250511003658/v8in_crops_rev.json; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Public ink models on a held-out 8.64 um scroll (reference))

### L167. Fine-tuning the 9 um base model on nearby same-scroll papyrus did not make unseen text legible
- **Trap:** Expecting a short same-scroll fine-tune with reference-map teacher labels to sharpen the base model's 9 um maps into readable letters.
- **Evidence:** D3 FOLD-0841: 288 fold-A tiles >= 144 vox from J, 2000 steps (lr 2e-5, batch 8, 4 fold-A + 4 replay), arms FA/NULLA/REVA/CTRL; 24 sealed reads: C_all = C_net = 0 for all 8 arm-states, FA named 0 letters on 72 panels, p_max 1 -> NOT PASSED; every reader named 3-13 letters on the known-text canary.
- **Fix:** Do not spend sealed decisions on short fold-out fine-tunes from reference-map teacher labels at 9 um; look for stronger supervision or higher-resolution input.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#D3-VERDICT, #DECL-D3-A1; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (D3-FEAS-RESULT), RULES.md (DECL-D3-A2), LEDGER.md (D3 FOLD-0841 row); logs/d1/d3_summary.json sha256 fb8d31c0..., LEDGER.md

### L168. The 3-D stem of the 9 um ink model is the CPU bottleneck
- **Trap:** Optimising the 2-D encoder/decoder (most FLOPs) for CPU speed.
- **Evidence:** Profile of ink_9um seed42 step-075000 (34.55 M params): the 3-D stem (7,425 params, 23.9 % of FLOPs) takes 55 % of fp32 inference time and 60 % of a training step; it reaches only 79 GFLOP/s vs 330 GFLOP/s for the 2-D encoder. AMX helps the stem least (1.68x).
- **Fix:** Any further CPU speed-up must come from the stem (requires changing official model code) or from caching encoder features (see the frozen-encoder lesson).
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-amx:logs/sib/amx/REPORT.md, logs/sib/amx/profile_split.json; dominion:sib-amx@872d7dd78:logs/sib/amx/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-chain2um@1c4fb1444:logs/sib/chain2um/REPORT.md; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (AMX bf16 speed and equivalence on CPU)

### L169. Do not use --tta-mirror with the base ink_9um checkpoint: it lowers forward AUC below the regression bar
- **Trap:** Running official inference with --tta-mirror (the C2 chain) as the default.
- **Evidence:** w040 crop (y0 2560, x0 4096), inside supervision: with TTA forward AUC 0.97795 (fails >= 0.987), reverse 0.56648; without TTA forward 0.99347, reverse 0.58142. Fresh segment w044 without TTA (C2-NT): forward 0.99960, reverse 0.58558 -> PASS.
- **Fix:** Use C2-NT: official infer CLI, both orders, batch 4, --no-compile, CPU, NO --tta-mirror. Note the reverse-order margin is only 0.014 (base reads slightly bright in both orders).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#C3-R1-VERDICT, #C3-NT-R1-VERDICT; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:LEDGER.md (row C3-R1); logs/c3/c3_r1_results.json sha256 1473c540..., LEDGER.md (row C3-R1), RULES.md (entry C3-R1-VERDICT), logs/c3/audit_r1.json (field audit)

### L170. A fidelity gate on training papyrus validates the plumbing, not the model's ability on unseen text
- **Trap:** Reading a pass of the fidelity gate on a base-trained segment as evidence that the 9 um chain generalises to unseen text (C3-NT-R1: no-TTA base chain on a never-mapped PHerc0139 segment).
- **Evidence:** Forward AUC inside the supervision mask 0.99960 (bar >= 0.987); reverse-order AUC 0.58558 (bar < 0.60), a margin of only 0.014. The chain became the validated 9 um base-map chain, but the segment was base-trained, so the pass shows fidelity only. The later D1 result (L196) bore this out.
- **Fix:** Use a fidelity gate on training papyrus to validate plumbing only; test generalisation on held-out, never-trained text.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:LEDGER.md (row C3-NT-R1); logs/c3/c3_nt_r1_results.json sha256 9a430680..., LEDGER.md (row C3-NT-R1), RULES.md (entry C3-NT-R1-VERDICT), logs/c3/audit_nt_r1.json (field audit)

### L171. A frozen-encoder feature cache is exact and makes decoder-only training ~14x faster
- **Trap:** Re-running the whole 9 um model for every training step of a head-only recipe on CPU.
- **Evidence:** Cached encoder skips (6 tensors, 1,008,640 values = 4.04 MB/tile fp32, 2.02 MB bf16) reproduce the full model bitwise (max |logit diff| 0, also after re-batching). Decoder-only training step is 14.6x (fp32) / 13.3x (bf16) faster than a full step; 8.3x / 7.7x with a 3x3-tile letter-context block. Storing features in bf16/fp16 costs at most 1 grey level. LC384-SOFT smoke: 0.360 s/step frozen vs 7.67 s/step unfrozen (21x).
- **Fix:** For head/context recipes, cache encoder features once (fp16 cache is acceptable) and train the decoder only; verify bitwise identity of cached vs full output first.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-amx:logs/sib/amx/cache_path.json, logs/sib/amx/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-dev-lcsoft:logs/sib/dev-lcsoft/bench_unfrozen.json

- **Trap:** Treating ref9 >= 150 (ink) / <= 100 (blank) as equivalent to human ink labels for fine-tuning.
- **Evidence:** LABEL-EQUIV on 288 fold-A tiles (overlap 64,273 px, only segment 214732): agreement 0.8095, Cohen's kappa 0.6139; 306 PRIMARY tiles: 0.7966 / 0.5927; disagreement mostly teacher-ink where human-blank.

- **Trap:** Planning to fine-tune on 0841 human labels outside the sealed windows.

### L174. Base ink_9um depth-order convention: forward = render slices 7..23 ascending of an -n 31 render
- **Trap:** Guessing which depth order is the text order, or transferring an order convention between checkpoints.

### L176. A cross-scroll ink model can be completely blind on a new scroll: gate it on that scroll's known text first
- **Trap:** Assuming the public PHerc.1667-iteration-5 ink model (trained on PHerc1667 only) would transfer to the PHerc. Paris 4 2.4 um volume and computing title-search tiles with it.
- **Evidence:** PHerc.1667-iteration-5 at card geometry (62 slices, 256 px, stride 128, clip(0,200)/255, fp32) on the Paris 4 2.4 um surface volume. Stage batch o2s1 (10 tiles, 2 valid blind sessions, verified 12/12): all 3 known-text gate tiles were rows N with 0 letters, so the gate failed 0/3 (P4-O-STAGE-O2S1-RESULT) and the 13-tile batch is uninformative. On a known-text gate tile the prediction mean was 139/255 (p about 0.55) with std 52: the model does not separate ink from papyrus at this geometry. A numbers-only input re-normalisation test found only a small affine correction (a = 1.152, b = -0.065), so the domain shift was not a simple intensity offset.
- **Fix:** Before any target tile, read at least 3 known-text gate tiles of the target scroll as their own stage batch; stop the model route at a 0/3 gate. The programme then moved to a model trained on the scroll's own labels (P4-OWN), which passed.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-o5w1:README.md; dominion:sib-o5w3:README.md; dominion:sib-o5w1:logs/sib/o5w1/STATUS.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#P4-O-STAGE-O2S1-RESULT, #DECL-P4-14-A3; dominion:sib-ckpt-screen-b:logs/sib/ckpt-screen-b/STATUS.md, logs/sib/ckpt-screen-b/p4o/renorm_test.json, README.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md#P4-O-PROVENANCE, #P4-O-STAGE-O2S1-RESULT; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (P4-O-PROVENANCE), RULES.md (P4-O-PROVENANCE-2), RULES.md (P4-O-STAGE-O2S1-RESULT); logs/p4/census_o2s1_summary.json, logs/p4/census_o2s1_summary.json

### L177. Prove the trainer bitwise before any real training
- **Trap:** A new trainer that generalises an earlier one can silently change sampling, losses or resume behaviour.
- **Evidence:** d2_train.py reproduced the D3 trainer's per-step losses and final weights bitwise for arms CTRL, FA, NULLA and REVA; identical configs gave bitwise-identical weights (fp32, 1 thread); paired arms shared a chained digest of (patch, z offset, rotation) draws; runs killed after step 3 resumed from local state and from remote shards alone with bitwise-equal final weights (26/26, later 29/29 tests). Also: D2 arms passed on synthetic data: crash after step 7, resume from the step-5 checkpoint -> max abs weight difference 0.0; NULL derangement 0 fixed points (96/96 labels differ); batch images identical to P384 at every step while labels differ; REV inputs the exact depth-reverse of P384 with identical labels and RNG; 0 held-out ids loaded (19-id allowlist).
- **Fix:** Before GO, run a short synthetic smoke of the exact arm config with a hard-exit-and-resume test, a pairing check in separate processes and a tamper test of the hold-out check.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-trainer:logs/sib/trainer/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-d2-null:logs/sib/d2-null/smoke.json, logs/sib/d2-null/holdout_check.json; dominion:sib-d2-rev:logs/sib/d2-rev/smoke.json; dominion:sib-d2-p128:logs/sib/d2-p128/smoke_result.json

### L178. A 384 px model is not usable by the official 128 px inference; rotations waste more of large patches
- **Trap:** Rebuilding the base network with a 384-px patch config and expecting the base weights to load.
- **Evidence:** A 384-configured build differs from the base 128 build in 146 state keys (34,546,498 vs 47,871,298 params), so a strict load of the base ink_9um weights fails. Also: Building the base model at patch_size 384 changes parameter shapes (146 state keys differ from the 128 build), so official 128-tile inference cannot load a 'full' 384 model's context; a 'stitched' forward keeps official inference at the same CPU cost. Rotation augmentation on 384 px patches ignores 11.4 % of pixels vs 3.8 % at 128 px.
- **Fix:** Use stitched 128-px forward passes for 384 px patches (or build a gated 384-tile inference path) and account for rotation-lost pixels.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-trainer:logs/sib/trainer/REPORT.md, logs/sib/trainer/param_diff_384.json; dominion:sib-d2-p384:logs/sib/d2-p384/param_diff.json

### L179. Check gate segments against the ink model's actual training list
- **Trap:** Using known-text segments as 'held-out' gate material without checking the model's training config.
- **Evidence:** The ink_9um training list in villa 41701aa configs/aligned21_hybrid_3d2d.json includes PHerc0139 w016 w017 w028 w029 w035 w039 w040 w041 w043 (native9 w035 w039 w040 w041 w044), PHerc0814 46527, PHerc1667 and PHercParis4 segments; w016 and w017 have no 9.362 um mesh so their proximity cannot be checked; held-out PHerc0139 segments were ranked by fraction of vertices within 4 / 10 vox of any training vertex (0 / 0 for the chosen ones). w028 was once missing from a base-training list and had to be added.
- **Fix:** Read the training config and model card, compute vertex proximity of candidate gate segments to every training mesh, and exclude recorded re-traces of chosen segments.

### L180. The 2.4 um canonical ink model silently runs in bf16 on CPU
- **Trap:** Running the official ink_canonical_2um inference code 'unchanged' and believing it is fp32: its predict_fn always wraps the forward in CPU bf16 autocast. In contrast the official 9 um infer CLI autocasts only on CUDA (infer.py:748), so on CPU it is fp32.
- **Evidence:** chain2um pinned the semantics with tests/sib_chain2um_test_official_semantics.py (3 passed): exact fp32 needs a nested torch.autocast('cpu', enabled=False) inside the model wrapper. amx: the 9 um official CLI is bitwise deterministic across two fp32 runs (identical map sha256s, both orders); bf16 had to be forced with a wrapper (infer_bf16.py).
- **Fix:** For any official inference code, grep for autocast before running; to get fp32 on the 2.4 um canonical model, nest autocast(enabled=False). Record the precision of every map.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-chain2um:logs/sib/chain2um/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-amx:logs/sib/amx/REPORT.md

### L181. Allowlists must fail closed: the trainer silently ignored allow_ids for some source kinds
- **Trap:** Trusting that an allowlist passed to the trainer restricts what is loaded.
- **Evidence:** D2 P384 pairing check on synthetic data: an allowlist of 34 of 40 patches loaded all 40 because allow_ids is ignored for the 'pairs' and 'd3_pool' source kinds.
- **Fix:** Write an explicit synthetic test that the loaded id set equals the allowlist for every source kind, and add a guard that raises when an allowlist is given to a kind that does not support it.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-d2-p384:logs/sib/d2-p384/pairing_check.json, README.md

### L182. Apply hold-outs in the freeze record; a dry-run allowlist overlapped the DEV hold-out segments
- **Trap:** Assuming a training pair allowlist already excludes evaluation (DEV) segments.
- **Evidence:** An independent recomputation of the D2 pair filter reproduced the 329-patch dry-run allowlist exactly and found 121 of the 329 patches lie on DEV hold-out segments; a provisional check dropped 121 of 564 gated PHerc0814 patches.
- **Fix:** Recompute the pair filter independently and pin the hold-out list (with hashes) in the pair-freeze record before any training step; stop and ask if the freeze lacks the hold-out.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-d2-p128:logs/sib/d2-p128/holdout_check.json; dominion:sib-dev-distft:logs/sib/dev-distft/STATUS.md

### L183. A small CNN trained from scratch on the scroll's own labels detects its ink where a cross-scroll model failed
- **Trap:** Concluding from a failed cross-scroll checkpoint that the 2.4 um Paris 4 volume carries no learnable ink signal.
- **Evidence:** P4-OWN: 3-D-to-2-D CNN, 232,697 params, random init, slices 23-84 of the 2.4 um surface volume, masked BCE + soft Dice at output stride 4, 2500 steps, trained only on a certified zone T (>= 1.2 mm 3-D from a never-trained zone X). Held-out pixel AUC F1 0.9418, F2 0.9415, F3 0.9401; label-deranged NULL 0.4972 / 0.5074 / 0.5240; S1 pooled AUC 0.978 (0.9781) on 6 organizer-labelled known-text tiles inside X; G1 blind legibility gate passed (sigma2t 46/72 = 63.9 %, block 58/72 = 80.6 %, bar 30 %).
- **Fix:** Train on the target scroll's own organizer labels, exclude the evaluation zone plus a 3-D margin from training, and pass held-out folds + a deranged-label NULL + a blind legibility gate before reading any target map.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27..2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-own-lead:README.md; dominion:sib-p4-excl:README.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#P4-OWN-G1-RESULT; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (P4-OWN-G1-RESULT), logs/p4/g1_own.json; RULES.md (P4-OWN-G1-RESULT), logs/p4/g1_own.json, RULES.md (P4-OWN-S1-COLM1-AUC)

### L184. Train on the target scroll itself, with a certified 3-D exclusion margin around the prize region
- **Trap:** Assuming prize rules forbid any training on the scroll you want to read, and settling for cross-scroll models that do not transfer.
- **Evidence:** P4-OWN was trained only on patches whose every mesh point is >= 1.2 mm (3-D) from the excluded title zone. On the never-trained adjacent known-text column it separated the organizers' labelled ink at pixel AUC 0.978 (per tile 0.96-0.98), and a blind read found writing on 5 of 6 tiles (7-11 letters). Fold held-out AUC 0.942 / 0.941 / 0.940 against 0.497 / 0.507 / 0.524 for the label-deranged NULL. Held-out legibility gate G1: 46/72 = 63.9 % (sigma2t) and 58/72 = 80.6 % (block) against a 30 % bar. Only with these controls is the expected end-title null (0 of 24 tiles with writing) interpretable.
- **Fix:** Recipe that worked on CPU: 3-D-to-2-D CNN of 232,697 parameters from random init, 256/192 px, output stride 4, batch 16, 2500 steps AdamW cosine, 4000 patches with >= 2 % ink, masked BCE + Dice; 3 contiguous folds + 3 seeds + 1 label-derangement NULL (no fixed point); write each training patch's minimum distance to the exclusion zone into the manifest and freeze RECIPE.md by hash before any training step.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-23, #METRIC-HASH-45, #P4-OWN-S1-COLM1-AUC, #P4-OWN-G1-RESULT; paris-4:gifted-bell-gavnl5:README.md, SUBMISSION.md, results/census_own_s1x_summary.json

### L185. A patch cap can bind entirely on ink patches and empty the non-ink sampler pool
- **Trap:** Freezing an ink-first patch cap and a balanced 8-ink/8-rest sampler without checking how many patches qualify.
- **Evidence:** With 45,262 ink 64-px cells (feasibility bar 2000), all 4000 kept patches had core ink >= 2 %, so the non-ink pool was empty and every batch came from the ink pool (single-pool branch); non-ink pixels still dominated within patches. The qualifying-patch count was not recorded because the manifest step was re-run with --manifest-only after a crash; the deterministic kept list is verified on every rebuild.
- **Fix:** Count qualifying ink and non-ink patches before freezing the cap and the sampler; record the counts.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-own-lead:logs/sib/own-lead/p4own/RECIPE.md, logs/sib/own-lead/p4own/feasibility.json

### L186. At ink cells the sheet faces shift together: crackle beats relief, and the signal looks like displacement, not deposit
- **Trap:** Expecting carbon ink to appear as added thickness (relief) at the sheet face.
- **Evidence:** At model-ink cells face + sits +3.0 um higher and face - 2.2 um lower while thickness is unchanged (-0.2 um); F5+ crackle at the + face (AUC 0.656) beats the earlier mesh-slab crackle channel (0.584) but stays below the 0.70 bar. Physics reading graded UNCERTAIN by the lane.
- **Fix:** Do not build title searches on face height or thickness; if pursuing crackle at a face, declare block-level aggregation first and confirm which face is the ink face with a depth-sign test.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-purple-mo:logs/sib/p4-purple/mo/REPORT.md

### L187. Make training overlap mechanically impossible: carry each tile's 3-D distance to the labelled segments
- **Trap:** Letting a tile that lies near (or on another winding near) a labelled training segment become a candidate.
- **Evidence:** Every Paris 4 census tile carries its minimum 3-D distance to the 8 labelled segments' meshes; a tile closer than 1.2 mm can never become a candidate (DECL-P4-2); census summaries report n_labelled_adjacent.
- **Fix:** Compute and store the 3-D distance per tile at census time and filter before reading, not after.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** paris-4:gifted-bell-gavnl5:SUBMISSION.md, results/census_own_s1x_summary.json

### L188. Run the Grand Prize TimeSformer through the organizers' code and scale-match the voxel size
- **Trap:** Feeding a 7.91 um-trained model native data of another voxel size, or copying a scale factor between scans.
- **Evidence:** The organizer-hosted GP TimeSformer (37,959,696 parameters) expects (B,1,26,64,64); variant B rescales the layer stack trilinearly by voxel/7.91: 1.0923 at 8.64 um, 1.1836 only at 9.362 um (an erratum). fp32 vs bf16 autocast Pearson 0.999926. CPU cost about 1 h 50 min per segment.
- **Fix:** Compute the factor per scan; window 64, stride 32, fp32, Hann blend; record model sha256 and attribution in every manifest.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-FL-4, #DECL-FL-4-A1, #DECL-FL-4-A4-E1

### L189. Public ink models produce no text-like structure on organizer sheets of PHerc0800 and PHerc1203; a null is not blank papyrus
- **Trap:** Reading an absence of ink in public-model maps on a new scroll as evidence that the papyrus is blank.
- **Evidence:** orgsec-ink on 26 organizer segments (PHerc0800 6, 8.64 um; PHerc1203 20, 9.362 um), both directions: fraction above 0.5 was 0.018-0.060 and 0.012-0.158, maximum pixel never above 0.90, 1-3 mm blobs, no rows, forward and reverse unrelated; ink_9um vs Grand Prize TimeSformer agreement r 0.134 (control 0.097), 0.31 (0.17), 0.20 (0.11).
- **Fix:** Report public-model nulls as 'no transfer demonstrated' and test model transfer on known text of the same protocol before scanning unread scrolls.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-02..2026-10-03 · **Sources:** orgsec-ink:HEAD:README.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (FL6-RESULT), RULES.md (FL6-RESULT-A1); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Official-model screen on organizer-published segments (PHerc0800, PHerc1203)); dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:packages/orgseg-ink/results/agree_PHerc0800_i1_ink9um_vs_gp.json, logs/pp/SUBMIT_SHEET_OCT2026.md, logs/pp/verify_orgseg-ink.json; survey:expmap_raw.json:tools-infrastructure

### L190. Validation on the training scroll overstated transfer
- **Trap:** Validating a from-scratch master ink model (8.64 um, federated CPU training on pseudo-labels) on its training scroll and expecting the result to transfer.
- **Evidence:** On the held-out scroll (600 crops): common init global_r0 pixel AUC 0.5756; round-1 averaged model 0.5793 (AP 0.1667, tile AUC 0.575); round 2 0.5778 (AP 0.1649, tile AUC 0.572). Bars 0.90 / 0.50 / 0.85: failed.
- **Fix:** Measure on a held-out scroll, not the training scroll. A from-scratch CPU model after two rounds sat far below public pretrained weights on the same crops (L166), so start a pipeline from the strongest public model.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-09..2026-10-10 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:logs/fl7/global_r1.eval.json, logs/fl7/global_r2.eval.json, logs/fl7/global_r0.eval.json, RULES.md (E2E-1-RESULT)

### L191. Fine-tuning on pseudo-labels produced by another model can pull a stronger model toward the labeller's errors
- **Trap:** Fine-tuning the decoder and head of a public dense 9 um model for 2000 steps on 8.64 um pseudo-labels produced by a weaker model, expecting a gain.
- **Evidence:** Held-out pixel AUC on isolated crops: 0.698 at step 0 (unchanged public weights; AP 0.297, tile AUC 0.626), 0.634-0.676 at steps 250-2000, never above step 0. Full-map score of the kept base weights on the held-out segment: AUC 0.760, AP 0.408, tile AUC (p95) 0.688.
- **Fix:** Evaluate step 0 first and keep the base if no step beats it; pseudo-labels can pull a stronger model toward the labeller's errors.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (FL7-A1-RESULT); logs/fl7/dense_ft/eval_0.json, RULES.md (FL7-A1-RESULT); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Fine-tune of a public dense 9 um model on 8.64 um pseudo-labels)

### L192. CPU-trained from-scratch ink models at 8.64 um stalled far below a public baseline
- **Trap:** Training a new ink model from scratch on CPU with pseudo-labels and federated averaging.
- **Evidence:** Master model (EdgeBank + UNet3D; 18 PHerc0009B shards of organizer 2.4 um predictions rescaled 3.6x as pseudo-labels; 12 federated clients x 2 fp32 epochs): held-out PHerc0343P pixel AUC 0.579, AP 0.167, tile AUC 0.575; round 2: 0.578. Public dense_native 9 um base: 0.760 / 0.408 / 0.688. Fine-tuning its decoder (2000 steps, 0.25 s/step) gave 0.634-0.676 vs base 0.698 on isolated crops: no gain. Bars 0.90 / 0.50 / 0.85 unmet.
- **Fix:** Start from the strongest available baseline, measure on the held-out scroll after every few hundred steps, and stop rounds that do not improve.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-FL-7-A1, #E2E-1-RESULT, #FL7-A1-RESULT

### L193. Public villa ink models give no coherent signal on verifiable PHerc0268 surfaces
- **Trap:** Assuming models trained on other scrolls transfer to PHerc0268 at 8.64 um.
- **Evidence:** On the w161 strip inter-model r is 0.07-0.46 vs 0.61-0.67 on the PHerc0343 control; on gate-ON tiles p > 0.55 is 1.55 % vs 7.2 % on the control; ring patches reach 5.3-5.6 % on a raised baseline (median 0.39 vs 0.29) with blob texture (a texture response). The best public model (dense_native) has AUC 0.76 on the held-out PHerc0343P shard. No stroke rows on any validated PHerc0268 surface.
- **Fix:** Require inter-model agreement, sheet specificity and face specificity before any reading; build or fine-tune a model validated on held-out 8.64 um data before searching PHerc0268.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/FL_SEARCH.md

### L194. Hecate is ~42-47x slower than a villa ink map on CPU
- **Trap:** Including Hecate in a CPU ensemble because the recipe used it.
- **Evidence:** Measured ~1,198 px/s per 4-CPU box (~42x a villa map, fp32 vs fp32); in batch_ink ~5 s per 64x64 patch (~65 min per native Mpx, ~47x one villa run). The protocol admitted Hecate only if its CPU cost was < 2x villa's.
- **Fix:** Drop Hecate on CPU; use villa hybrid_3d2d seeds 42/43 and dense_native.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/PIPELINE.md, tools/fl/batch_ink.sh

### L195. PHerc0268 has about half the CT sheet contrast of PHerc0343: sensitivity shown on the control does not carry over
- **Trap:** Reading a PHerc0268 null as 'no ink' because the pipeline sees PHerc0343 letters.
- **Evidence:** PHerc0268 CT sheet amplitude is about half of PHerc0343's (sheet contrast ~0.42x); m7 is clean on 27-38 % of core nodes vs 87 %; nodes snapped to PHerc0268 m7 sheet centres show a 0.75 % CT peak (d = -1) vs the recipe's CT peak of 1.044 over the mean (an earlier '~7 %' was max/min). Sensitivity on tall strips is demonstrated only for PHerc0343-strength ink.
- **Fix:** State in every null that weaker ink is not excluded; calibrate sensitivity with a contrast-matched control.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/FL_SEARCH.md, docs/POC.md

**Inference validation (L196-L256).** Positive controls, planted faults, injection-recovery, displaced copies and face specificity: how to tell ink from texture, artefact and chance, and what a null does and does not exclude. Key failures: the blank-margin normalisation bug (L249, L252) and nulls without a measured sensitivity (L208, L210, L211).

### L196. The base 9 um model detects unseen-scroll ink at pixel level (AUC ~0.73) but its maps are not letter-legible
- **Trap:** Taking a respectable pixel AUC on an unseen scroll as evidence that letters can be read from the map.
- **Evidence:** D1 on PHerc0841 J1-J5: base forward AUC 0.733 pooled (per window 0.692-0.774), RAW slabs 0.50-0.53; REF ladder (official 2.4 um reference) C_all 16.0, C_net 11.37 of S' = 20 (p 1/5001), sigma_crit 0.30 mm; all 18 model-arm readers (BASE, RAW, CHANCE, both mirror states) named 0 letters on 180 J panels: C_net 0, p_max 1 -> FAIL. Same readers named 5-10 letters on the base map of base-trained 0139 w044. Base map vs reference r 0.27-0.50; DoG letter-scale std 10-12 vs canary 14.9.
- **Fix:** Never claim letters from a map without a sealed blind read; treat AUC ~0.73 as 'finds ink, does not resolve strokes'; use a base-trained canary to separate display failure from weak maps.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#TEXT-ORDER-D1, #D1-REF-RESULT, #D1-VERDICT; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:LEDGER.md (row D1 KTLB-3R); logs/d1/d1_model_summary.json sha256 22b2a0fa..., RULES.md (entry D1-VERDICT), RULES.md (entry TEXT-ORDER-D1), LEDGER.md (row D1 KTLB-3R); logs/d1/audit_d1.json

### L197. Plant real faults before trusting a pre-read gate
- **Trap:** Pipeline faults (window offset, mirror, swapped depth order, off-by-one slice, wrong voxel size, re-traced training papyrus) produce plausible-looking images that readers cannot detect.
- **Evidence:** Synthetic suite: each fault caught by its own check 40/40 with 0/40 clean false alarms. REAL-TRIB-1 on official CT renders of 12 PHerc0139 windows: clean 12/12, each real fault 12/12 by its own check only. Slices [1:32] of a -n 33 render equal the -n 31 render exactly, so off-by-one faults were made from [0:31] and [2:33]. Paris 4 tile checks: 7 planted manifest faults and 5 pixel faults each caught 200/200, 0/200 clean false alarms.
- **Fix:** Build fault injectors for every known failure mode, run them on real renders, and require each fault to fire only its own check before any reader sees an image.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-tribunal:logs/sib/tribunal/REPORT.md, logs/sib/tribunal/faultsuite.json, logs/sib/tribunal/real_trib1.json; dominion:sib-tribunal@a11610163:logs/sib/tribunal/REPORT.md (Round 1, Measured results); logs/sib/tribunal/faultsuite.json, logs/sib/tribunal/faultsuite.json (retrace_at_20vox.caught_by_literal_vertex_rule_alone), logs/sib/tribunal/real_trib1.json (clean.passed_current), logs/sib/tribunal/real_trib1.json (clean.passed_preregistered_rule); dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:CHANGELOG.md

### L198. Publishing the failure modes (the radial-gate blind spot, row-score insensitivity) is the durable output of a null push
- **Trap:** Treating a null First Letters push as producing nothing worth publishing.
- **Evidence:** Three tools were packaged with tests and their honest results: xsec (cross-section viewer), ringstrip (ring-unrolling stitcher) and orgseg-ink (CPU pipeline for public ink models on organizer segments, with its nulls). orgseg-ink published its row-score calibration: only 1.8 % of known-text tiles exceed the junk 99th percentile. xsec showed that synthetic on-sheet and layer-jump patches both score median |cos| > 0.95 on the radial gate, so the gate cannot tell them apart.
- **Fix:** Publish the failure modes (the radial-gate blind spot, row-score insensitivity) with tests; they are the durable output of a null push.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-10-03 (family period) · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:packages/orgseg-ink/README.md, packages/xsec/README.md; survey:expmap_raw.json:first-letters

### L199. A fault drill or planted-fault gate counts only if every case is built and fails its own check
- **Trap:** Accepting 'all planted faults caught' when some faults were never planted, or when every faulty copy fails an earlier, unrelated check.
- **Evidence:** Factory: the first fault drill passed vacuously because every copy failed file_layout first (stray __pycache__); fixed to require a clean baseline plus a failure of the named check, then 6/6 faults were rejected by their intended checks. Contam: 9 of 11 planted-fault cases were built (all 9 caught) but 2 patch cases were never built because R was placed on the strip bbox centre and missed the strip, so all_caught = false.
- **Fix:** Assert that the clean baseline passes, that each fault case was actually materialised, and that the named check (not another) rejects it.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-factory:logs/sib/factory/fault_drill.json; dominion:sib-contam:logs/sib/contam/planted_faults_0139.json, logs/sib/contam/ASK.md

### L200. A shifted-CT control shows whether an NCC alignment bar measures alignment
- **Trap:** An NCC >= 0.8 gate could pass patches for texture reasons rather than registration.
- **Evidence:** PHerc0814 pairs: 564 of 1502 patches passed (0.375; median zero-shift NCC 0.791); with the CT shifted by +-5 px the best NCC had median 0.577, p95 0.700, max 0.790 and 0 of patches reached 0.8. The second half passed 235 of 545 (43.1 %). Five small 2026 segments (0.2-0.3 cm^2) gave 0 candidate 384 px patches at >= 90 % valid.
- **Fix:** Run a non-gating shifted control with every alignment gate and report its distribution; budget for only about 40 % of patches passing.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-pairs0814:logs/sib/pairs0814/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-pairs0814b:logs/sib/pairs0814b/REPORT.md

### L201. RAW slab means carry no ink signal at 9 um, so RAW arms lack a working attention control
- **Trap:** Including raw CT slab displays as a reading arm expecting visible ink.
- **Evidence:** RAW-F AUC 0.526, RAW-B 0.502 against 0841 labels; RAW readers named 0 letters anywhere including the canary.
- **Fix:** Drop RAW arms unless a pixel-AUC screen shows signal; always include a canary that works in every arm's display.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#TEXT-ORDER-D1, #D1-VERDICT

### L202. Mineral-pigment (high-Z) ink is ruled out on the traced Paris 4 surfaces, with injection-recovery limits
- **Trap:** Assuming a red/gold/blue title would be missed because carbon-ink models ignore metal pigments, or reporting a pigment null without a sensitivity.
- **Evidence:** 0 DENSE-HOTSPOT tiles on 1.129 um (60) and 2.4 um (160) target tiles and both known-text controls (64, 171), at every offset from -60 to +60 um; max 2.4 um f_in per offset 0.38-0.46 vs bar 0.8. Injection of a 3 x 2 mm glyph with 0.4 mm stroke into 20 real control regions per voxel size gave detection limits (recovery >= 0.8, sigma 1 voxel) Hg/Pb/Au 0.05-0.1 um, CuO 0.5 um, Fe2O3 0.5-1 um, Egyptian blue 2 um; 0/40 false positives (0/180 in the extended panel).
- **Fix:** Pair any channel null with injection-recovery into real control CT and state the thickness limits; remaining gaps are organic dyes, untraced surfaces and depths beyond +-60 um.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-highz:README.md, logs/sib/p4-highz/REPORT.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#P4-CHANNELS-RESULT-1, #DECL-P4-6-A3, #DECL-P4-16; dominion:sib-p4-highz@68030b270:logs/sib/p4-highz/REPORT.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md#P4-CHANNELS-RESULT-1; dominion:sib-p4-highz-c2@79f496987:logs/sib/p4-highz-c2/STATUS.md; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md (P4-CHANNELS-RESULT-1); survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-pigments

### L203. Raw CT slab means do not show carbon ink to blind readers even next to known text
- **Trap:** Hoping a raw-CT slab projection reveals ink invisible to ink models.
- **Evidence:** Raw 2.4 um CT +-53 um slab mean at 9.6 um, 160 tiles on a Paris 4 inner strip: 0 positives, rows Y on 8 tiles, N0 19 x 0 and 1 x 1 letters; including 120 tiles adjacent to labelled known-ink segments.
- **Fix:** Do not expect raw-CT displays to show carbon ink at these resolutions; raw-CT search makes sense only for physically different (dense) ink.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#P4-E2-CENSUS-RESULT, #DECL-P4-5; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:logs/p4/census_e2_summary.json; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census

### L204. Model-free raw-CT channels did not detect known carbon ink on Paris 4 at 2.4 um
- **Trap:** Assuming the Paris 4 ink, reported by the organizers as bright 10-20 um surface deposits in the 2.4 um volume, can be found with simple bright-voxel or surface measures on raw CT.
- **Evidence:** On known text (the control strip, or the 120 labelled-adjacent tiles of the title strip): +-53 um slab mean 0 letters on 160 tiles (E2); raw 1.129 um slab 0 rows Y on 60 tiles (E1); on the control strip: +-15 um thin-slab max with global thresholds and with per-tile stretch: known-text gate 0 of 72 tiles (bar 30 %); depth calibration STOP at 1.129 um (robust z 1.122 < 3) and 2.4 um (z 1.94 at -31.2 um); reader-free block detector recall 0.089 at FPR 0.032 (bar 0.90 at <= 0.05); surface-following slab recall 0.074 / 0.033; crackle texture AUC 0.584 [0.565, 0.603] (bar 0.70); 9 morphology features, best AUC 0.656.
- **Fix:** Gate every channel on known text before reading any target. For carbon ink, use an ink model whose training data do not overlap the target region (own model with an exclusion zone, or an eligible cross-scroll model that passes its own gate).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-17-A2, #P4-L4-PREGATE-RESULT, #P4-L2-CENSUS-RESULT, #P4-L3E-CALIB-RESULT, #P4-L3-CALIB-RESULT, #P4-W-DETECTOR-L2S-RESULT, #P4-CHANNELS-RESULT-1, #DECL-P4-17-A1; dominion:sib-p4-l2@52d6c9102:logs/sib/p4-l2/PREGATE_L4.json; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census

### L205. Crackle texture energy carries real but weak ink information: not an independent ink channel
- **Trap:** Using DoG texture ('crackle') energy from raw 1.129 um CT as an independent carbon-ink detector.
- **Evidence:** Pre-registered gate (16 known-text tiles drawn by fixed seed from 64): pooled pixel AUC 0.584 [0.565, 0.603] vs the official 1 um prediction, bar 0.70 -> FAIL; rot-90 sanity 0.485; 15/16 tiles above 0.5, best 0.659. The DoG (sigma 1.5 / 6 px) peaks at a 35 um period with amplitude transfer 0.13 at 10 um. The reference is a model prediction, not ground truth. Also: Gate against official 1 um predictions on known text (ink = pred >= p90, background <= p50, 50 um boundary excluded): pooled AUC 0.584 [0.565, 0.603], bar 0.70; rot-90 sanity 0.485. Numeric row-structure screen (2-D power spectrum, 3-9 mm periods): every material gate failed or could not be evaluated.
- **Fix:** Drop the channel at these scales; any other sigma/slab/statistic needs a new declaration before computation (none was tried after the result).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-crackle:README.md, logs/sib/p4-crackle/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-p4-crackle@f679ccd9c:RULES.md (P4-CHANNELS-RESULT-1); logs/sib/p4-crackle/gate.json; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md (P4-CHANNELS-RESULT-1); dominion:sib-p4-crackle@f679ccd9c:logs/sib/p4-crackle/REPORT.md; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-pigments; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#P4-CHANNELS-RESULT-1, #DECL-P4-9, #DECL-P4-8

### L206. A positive control that measures the planted quantity but stays near chance shows the channel's floor
- **Trap:** Assuming a colour-agnostic relief/thickness channel can detect a title deposit because it measures height correctly.
- **Evidence:** Morphology gate on the 2.4 um known-text control (1,351,721 ink / 6,986,386 background 19.2 um cells): 0/9 tests passed; relief and thickness AUC 0.48-0.53, rot-90 nulls 0.47-0.53. A planted 10 um deposit was measured as 7.3 / 6.4 um, yet its glyph AUC was 0.60 / 0.58 (0.68 / 0.65 at 20 um) against a 0.90 bar.
- **Fix:** Run a planted positive control before any target data; if it recovers the physical quantity but not the classification bar, the limit is natural face-height variability, so a relief-only title below about 20 um is under the per-cell detection floor; aggregation at block level would need a new declaration.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-purple-mo:README.md, logs/sib/p4-purple/mo/REPORT.md, logs/sib/p4-purple/mo/posctl.json; dominion:sib-p4-purple-mo@5d805a05f:logs/sib/p4-purple/mo/REPORT.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md (DECL-P4-17-A1 'Also recorded'); survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-pigments

### L207. The same frozen detector can be sensitive on one material and blind on another: report sensitivity per material
- **Trap:** Assuming a detector validated at one voxel size or display transfers to another volume of the same scroll.
- **Evidence:** Gold thin-layer ridge detector: on the 2.4 um strip 12/12 injected letters recovered at >= 0.05 um Au-equivalent (papyrus density 1.5; 0.02 um at 0.5) and 0/12 at 0.01 um; on the 1.129 um L1 strip best 3/12 at any thickness (INSENSITIVE), because the L1 build's per-slice clip plus 2x mean and the unsharp mask's dark lobes blunt the ridge statistic. Injected E1 Z_max 77-117 overlaps the natural E1 range (max 130.5).
- **Fix:** Run injection-recovery separately on every material/display you score, and report 'insensitive' per material rather than one family verdict; model the actual reconstruction/display chain (clipping, binning, unsharp masking) in the injection.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-pig-gold:README.md, logs/sib/p4-pig-gold/REPORT.md, logs/sib/p4-pig-gold/injection/summary.json; dominion:sib-p4-pig-gold@973fe81fd:logs/sib/p4-pig-gold/REPORT.md; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-pigments

### L208. Insensitive is not absent: a clean strip from a detector that cannot see the plausible layer means nothing
- **Trap:** Reporting 'no ochre title' because the title strip scored like the control, when injection-recovery shows the detector cannot see the plausible paint thickness.
- **Evidence:** FE (ochre) stroke matched filter: 0/12 injected letters recovered at 2, 5, 10 and 20 um in both electron-density regimes on all four materials; mu-regime limit 20 um (C, E1, E2) and 10 um (C2). Papyrus-minus-gap contrast is only 15.0 / 12.4 grey levels against voxel noise SD 36-43; natural surface structure already scores ~9 sigma (median tile) to 14-16 sigma (max). Strip maxima 14.63 / 14.04 vs control maxima 14.23 / 16.16; 0 strict hotspots.
- **Fix:** Always pair a null with a measured detection limit per material and regime; label the verdict INSENSITIVE where the limit exceeds the plausible thickness (ochre 5-10 um), and say exactly what is excluded (here only mu-regime ochre >= 20 um on the traced surface).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-pig-fe:README.md, logs/sib/p4-pig-fe/REPORT.md, logs/sib/p4-pig-fe/summary.json; dominion:sib-p4-pig-fe@6b00f9bd1:logs/sib/p4-pig-fe/REPORT.md; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-pigments

### L209. A low literature prior for a coloured title justifies cheap controlled screens, not a heavy search
- **Trap:** Building many pigment-specific searches on an owner or folk prior drawn from later codex practice (rubrication, gold, purple).
- **Evidence:** Dossier: no coloured Herculaneum title is published; the standard catalogue (118 certain, 30 uncertain titles) reports none; titles are written by the text scribe; no mineral pigment is reported on any Herculaneum papyrus. Honest prior for a visibly coloured title about 2 % (1-5 %, UNCERTAIN); for a dense high-Z ink about 2-4 %. Gold memo: no Greek roll of the 3rd c. BC-1st c. AD with gold writing known. All pigment lanes returned null, insensitive or incomplete.
- **Fix:** Separate attestation by period and book form before weighting a prior; give low-prior hypotheses only cheap screens with known-text controls and measured limits.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-research:logs/sib/p4-research/DOSSIER.md; dominion:sib-p4-pig-gold:logs/sib/p4-pig-gold/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-p4-research@b234b9450:logs/sib/p4-research/DOSSIER.md (section 2.4), logs/sib/p4-research/DOSSIER.md (section 2.1); survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-pigments

### L210. An analytic detection limit is not an exclusion; a lane without injection-recovery has no verdict
- **Trap:** Quoting a modelled sensitivity as if a pigment had been ruled out.
- **Evidence:** Red-pigment lane: only steps 1-2 ran (memo, frozen params); the analytic 2.4 um model predicts pessimistic limits of 1.491-1.705 um HgS and 1.11-1.269 um PbO (PSF sigma 2 voxels; optimistic < 0.1 um), explicitly 'not to be quoted as ruled out'; 0 CT reads completed. Coverage of Hg/Pb came instead from the separate density screen.
- **Fix:** Only an injection-recovery into real control CT gives a usable limit; keep analytic predictions labelled as such and route coverage claims to the channel that actually measured them.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-pig-red:README.md, logs/sib/p4-pig-red/ADDENDUM-1.md, logs/sib/p4-pig-red/detlim_model_2p4.json; dominion:sib-p4-pig-red@38e0b0c51:logs/sib/p4-pig-red/STATUS.md, logs/sib/p4-pig-red/detlim_model_2p4.json; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-pigments

### L211. Run the positive control first, on enough material, and with cell-level ink labels
- **Trap:** Running a single-tile positive-control gate (held-out PHerc0139 known text) on too little material and without cell-level ink labels.
- **Evidence:** Wave-1 gate: rows Y on 1 of 4 held-out tiles, max 1 letter (bar 10). Wave-2 gate on fresh held-out cells, read before any census: rows Y on 0 of 8, max 0 letters: NOT SENSITIVE. Pooled waves 1-2: 12 held-out tiles from 3 segments, rows Y 1 of 12, max 1 letter. The pipeline never showed it could make one legible row visible on held-out text.
- **Fix:** Run the positive control first, on enough material, with cell-level ink labels. Without labels, 'reader/model insensitive' and 'these cells are blank' cannot be told apart.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (FL2-WAVE1-RESULT); logs/fl2/wave1_result.json, RULES.md (FL2-WAVE2-GATE); logs/fl2/wave2_gate_result.json, RULES.md (FL2-WAVE2-GATE); dominion:sib-pairs0139c@be6d4f134:logs/sib/pairs0139c/fl2_gate/STATUS.md

### L212. Dropping the positive control to save time left every later read of this arm without meaning
- **Trap:** Dropping the positive-control gate to save time (Grand Prize TimeSformer arm on held-out PHerc0139: two declared variants, native layers and layers rescaled to the model's 7.91 um training voxel; at most 16 windows per variant under the block brief; a variant to be chosen only if sensitive).
- **Evidence:** The precision check passed (fp32 vs reference bf16 autocast, Pearson 0.999926 on a test crop), but the gate was stopped by DECL-FL-4-A1 (owner: PHerc0139 gate dropped) and never read. The surface defect it might have exposed was found only a day later.
- **Fix:** Never drop the positive control to save time: every later read of that arm is without meaning.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-pairs0139c@be6d4f134:logs/sib/pairs0139c/fl4_gate/STATUS.md; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Grand Prize TimeSformer gate on held-out PHerc0139)

### L213. Derive pre-read thresholds per scan protocol; 9 um margins do not transfer to 2.4 um
- **Trap:** A slice-lag threshold calibrated at 9.362 um was reused at 2.399 um, where adjacent slices are about 4x closer and far more alike.
- **Evidence:** At 2.4 um the slice margin ranged 0.0229-0.0682 (9.362 um: 0.126-0.217); the 9 um-derived SLICE_MARGIN 0.042 raised a false alarm on clean data (11/12) and even 0.02 leaves only a 1.15x margin (pre-registered need >= 3x), although faults were caught 60/60.
- **Fix:** Calibrate every pre-read threshold on clean data of the same protocol (for example clean p1 / 3, about 0.0076 here) or compare lags of about one 9 um slice (+-4 slices at 2.4 um).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-tribunal:logs/sib/tribunal/REPORT.md, logs/sib/tribunal/real_trib2/gate_2p4um.json

### L214. Clearance thresholds must include the render slab half-depth and interpolation margin
- **Trap:** Keeping mesh nodes at >= 144 vox from sealed points is not enough when every rendered sample reaches out by the slab half-depth and pixel interpolation.
- **Evidence:** CHAIN VALID prep on PHerc0841: a node threshold of 168 vox gave a fail-closed minimum of 143.83 vox in 5 blocks after growing by the -n 63 slab half-depth (8 vox) plus 5.2 vox interpolation; raising it to 172 gave 144.07 vox; benchmark renders made from the 168 mesh were retro-checked at >= 145.8 vox and deleted.
- **Fix:** Check clearance on the grown footprint of every rendered sample (point-to-surface, fail-closed), not on mesh nodes, and re-check any render made before a threshold change.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-reg0841:logs/sib/reg0841/chainvalid/REPORT.md

### L215. A +-60 um dense-pigment sweep closes mineral inks only at CT-detectable thickness
- **Trap:** Searching raw 2.4 um CT for dense (metal-based) ink deposits near the mesh.
- **Evidence:** Frozen DECL-P4-6 screen at 9 offsets (-60..+60 um, 15 um steps) over 160 E2 tiles (parent + hzw1 40 + hzw2 48): 0 DENSE-HOTSPOT tiles at all offsets against a Bonferroni bar from 171 control tiles (P4-F-SWEEP-RESULT). Also: 0 DENSE-HOTSPOT at all 9 offsets (-60 to +60 um, 15 um steps) on 160 + 60 tiles (Bonferroni bar from control p99.89, f_in >= 0.8); title-zone max f_in 0.37-0.45, largest component 0.81 mm vs control 0.96-1.42 mm. Detection limits: Hg/Pb/Au ~0.1 um, CuO 0.5, Fe2O3 0.5-1, Egyptian blue 2 um.
- **Fix:** Report the detection limits with the null; organic and low-Z colourants and carbon ink the models miss remain untested.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#P4-F-SWEEP-RESULT; dominion:sib-hzw1:README.md; dominion:sib-hzw2:README.md

### L216. Dual-energy CT cannot see organic or lake colourants: a null means 'untestable'
- **Trap:** Running a 78/137 keV dual-energy search for a purple or lake-dye title and calling a null 'absent'.
- **Evidence:** Frozen on the control strip: known carbon ink vs blank AUC 0.483; injection recovery >= 0.8 at <= 20 um only for CuO, gold and orpiment; NOT detectable: Tyrian purple (0/50/90 % Br loss), purpurissum, alumina and gypsum lakes, carbon ink, red ochre, cinnabar, lead white. 137 keV covers only 3.01 % of the strip. The one-shot application found 1 hotspot in 11,674 patches (rate 0.0001 vs control FPR 0.0215), with z p99 2.0-2.3 vs 3.2-3.5 on control: the z scale did not transfer.
- **Fix:** Record such hypotheses as 'untestable with published data'; the only CT route for a purple deposit is a colour-agnostic deposit channel at a calibrated ink depth; ask the organizers for XRF/hyperspectral if the hypothesis matters.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#METRIC-HASH-40, #P4-DE-RESULT; dominion:sib-p4-purple:README.md, logs/sib/p4-purple/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-p4-purple-de:README.md

### L217. A null far below the control false-positive rate signals a calibration-transfer problem
- **Trap:** Reading a target-region hotspot rate that is hundreds of times below the control FPR as strong evidence of absence.
- **Evidence:** One-shot dual-energy application: 11,674 patches used, hotspot rate 0.0001 against control FPR 0.0215 (about 200x below); target z p99 2.0-2.3 against 3.2-3.5 on control rows, so the z scale did not transfer exactly.
- **Fix:** Report such a null as conservative and state that it does not demonstrate the method's sensitivity in that region; check the z distribution of the target against the control before interpreting rates.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-purple:logs/sib/p4-purple/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4-purple-de:README.md, logs/sib/p4-purple/de/title_zone.json; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md (P4-DE-RESULT); survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-pigments

### L218. A null counts only when an in-batch positive control on comparable, never-trained text passes in the same session
- **Trap:** Reporting a title-zone null without an in-batch positive control on comparable, never-trained text (own model, expected end-title area census).
- **Evidence:** Seed S1: rows on 0 of 24 tiles of the expected title area, while 5 of 6 in-batch known-text control tiles read as rows with >= 5 letters. Seed S2: rows on 0 of 24 tiles of the same area, with 6 of 6 control tiles read clearly. Null, and informative.
- **Fix:** Count a null only when an in-batch positive control on comparable, never-trained text passes in the same session; agreement across independently seeded models guards against one model's blind spot.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27..2026-10-03 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (P4-OWN-S1X-RESULT); logs/p4/census_own_s1x_summary.json, RULES.md (P4-OWN-S1X-RESULT), RULES.md (P4-OWN-S2X-RESULT); logs/p4/census_own_s2x_summary.json, RULES.md (P4-OWN-S2X-RESULT), RULES.md#P4-OWN-S1X-RESULT, #P4-OWN-S2X-RESULT, #P4-OWN-S1-XR1-RESULT; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census

### L219. State the scope of every null: the own-model title-slot null is a carbon-ink null only
- **Trap:** Reading 'no legible carbon ink in the expected end-title region' as 'there is no title'.
- **Evidence:** The Paris 4 own-model null explicitly does not exclude non-carbon ink, a flaked title or its offset onto the facing winding, the blank end of the roll, or an initial title at the beginning of the roll; it was also read before the held-out legibility gate. Also: Two independently seeded own models read 0/24 slot tiles at tile scale and 0 positive slot windows at 4 x 4 cm, while the adjacent known-text column read 5/6 and 6/6 tiles and 46-56 counts per window (N0 thresholds 5 and 18.12). This excludes body-text-like carbon writing in the slot at 2.4 um, nothing else.
- **Fix:** Name the untested alternatives with the null: non-carbon ink, other depth, physically missing rows, other positions (initial title), offset onto the facing winding.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#P4-OWN-S1X-RESULT, #P4-OWN-S2X-RESULT, #P4-OWN-SLOTW-RESULT; paris-4:gifted-bell-gavnl5:README.md

### L220. An internal body-text gate separates 'blank' from 'the model does not respond here'
- **Trap:** Expecting the outermost windings to provide a body-text positive control for an initial-title search.
- **Evidence:** 138 tiles, 0 rows Y, 1 letter total; internal body-text gate FAIL -> UNINFORMATIVE (not a null); a canvas direction conflict was flagged.
- **Fix:** Check that each material carries its own positive control before reading; record failures as uninformative.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-15

### L221. A brief that allows for sparse and ornamented writing, plus a passing known-text gate, makes a null informative for that material
- **Trap:** Reading title-scale windows with a body-text brief, or without a gate (block windows on official 2.4 um predictions).
- **Evidence:** Block brief allowing sparse and ornamented writing. Gate PASS: all 6 known-text control windows read as written blocks (6-7 lines, 6-25 letters), and exactly those 6 were the positives. All 8 target windows and the blank window read as no block (0 lines, 0 letters, 0 marks). Rotated-null counts (letters + marks) ranged 0-4.
- **Fix:** Use a brief that allows sparse and ornamented writing plus a passing known-text gate; the null is then informative for that material and says nothing about ink the model does not respond to.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md#P4-W1-RESULT, logs/p4/census_w1_summary.json; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:logs/p4/census_slot_summary.json, RULES.md#P4-OWN-SLOTW-RESULT
