### L222. Exactly-zero tiles in official predictions are blanks, not 'no ink'
- **Trap:** Counting tiles whose prediction is 0 over the whole mesh-valid area as ink-free evidence.
- **Evidence:** In one official-prediction strip tile set, 11 eligible tiles were exactly 0 over their whole mesh-valid area and byte-identical PNGs (other strips: 14, 12 and 10 blanks).
- **Fix:** Detect byte-identical all-zero tiles and mark them blank (no prediction) for gates and censuses.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-inner:logs/sib/p4-inner/STATUS.md

### L223. The linear attenuation model is optimistic: anchor detection floors to the control's undetected carbon ink
- **Trap:** Quoting ideal-model pigment thickness limits as the real sensitivity.
- **Evidence:** The same linear grey model predicts that 10-20 um soot carbon ink would be detectable at 2.4 um, yet the known-text control's real carbon text gives no letter-scale bright structure. Conservative floors anchored to an undetected 20 um soot layer: Au ~0.13 um, HgS ~0.34 um, Pb oxides ~0.3 um, CuO ~1.3 um, Fe2O3 ~2.2 um, Egyptian blue ~6 um (As ~2 um, Tyrian purple ~6-18 um, purpurissum ~8 um, lakes ~12-14 um in the extended panel).
- **Fix:** Report both ideal and conservative floors and treat the floor as the honest limit.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-highz:README.md, logs/sib/p4-highz/REPORT.md

### L224. Bright voxels in carbonised papyrus CT are compact grains, and 'gap' slabs are neighbouring papyrus, not air
- **Trap:** Reading bright-voxel clusters as pigment, or using slabs at +-60-120 um as an empty-space baseline.
- **Evidence:** 3-D morphology (1000 whole chunks per material): components >= 64 vox hold 82-88 % of bright voxels, median lambda3/lambda2 0.50-0.51, planar < 2 %, centroids within +-15 um of the surface 11.0-13.7 % vs 11.2 % for a uniform population; 87-99 % reach 255 (inclusions, sand or ash). The +-(60-120) um slabs hold neighbouring papyrus (mean 70-83), so a depth-uniform bright population gives f_in about 0.19-0.20, which is where every strip sits.
- **Fix:** Model the depth-uniform baseline before choosing bars; test layer-likeness (planarity, depth concentration) before calling a bright population ink.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-highz:logs/sib/p4-highz/REPORT.md

### L225. Compare strip peak scores with the weakest injected positive to dismiss over-bar tiles, and call it post hoc
- **Trap:** Tiles that pass an area/in-sheet rule are taken as candidates even when their scores are far below what any real layer of the target material would produce.
- **Evidence:** Gold on the 2.4 um strip: 8 tiles passed the non-excluding area and in-sheet rule, all with Z_max <= 88; the strip maximum anywhere was 93.6, against a minimum injected Z_max of 154.5 for a 0.1 um gold layer (density 1.5). The E2-vs-control excess (75 % vs 45 % of tiles with any hot area) was strip-wide and concentrated in known-text and labelled-adjacent tiles, consistent with carbon-ink deposits.
- **Fix:** Store per-tile peak scores and the injected-letter score distribution; a physical-consistency comparison can retire over-bar tiles, but disclose it as post hoc and do not let it replace the frozen rule.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-pig-gold:logs/sib/p4-pig-gold/REPORT.md

### L226. Volume edges outside the control domain produce artefact hotspots
- **Trap:** Applying a registered two-volume method where one volume's lower end / cylinder edge lies outside the region used to calibrate it.
- **Evidence:** Dual-energy application: rows near the lower end and cylinder edge of the 137 keV volume had z > +T on 33-96 % of patches (p ~1e-103), a drift artefact; rows inside the control domain had rates 0.012-0.023, consistent with the FPR.
- **Fix:** Restrict application to the calibrated domain or flag edge regions in advance; report drift artefacts rather than fixing them after seeing target numbers.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-purple:logs/sib/p4-purple/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4-purple-de:README.md

### L227. Labels taken from a model prediction measure agreement with that model, not ground truth
- **Trap:** Scoring a new channel's AUC against the official ink prediction (ink >= p90, background <= p50) on a control segment that has no human ink labels, and reading the AUC as ink detection accuracy.
- **Evidence:** The known-text control canvas has no human ink labels (listing check), so the morphology gate used the official 2.4 um prediction (ink >= pooled p90 211.5, background <= p50 33.5, 50 um exclusion). Best cue crackle at the + face AUC 0.656 [0.636, 0.675]; per tile 0.604-0.724, 16/16 above 0.5.
- **Fix:** State in the result that the AUC is agreement with a model; prefer human labels or injected positives where available; do not tune a channel to mimic the model.
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-purple-mo:logs/sib/p4-purple/mo/REPORT.md

### L228. A saturated plateau defeats a ridge statistic
- **Trap:** Assuming a thin-layer ridge detector's recovery rises monotonically with layer thickness.
- **Evidence:** Gold injection on the 2.4 um strip: the frozen rule recovered only 6/12 at 1 um for papyrus density 0.5 because the saturated plateau has no ridge, although those layers produce a disc-mean Z >= 109, far above anything on the strip.
- **Fix:** Test the full thickness range in injection and add a plateau/area statistic (disc mean) alongside ridge statistics for bright layers.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-pig-gold:logs/sib/p4-pig-gold/REPORT.md

### L229. Initial titles exist: search both ends of a roll
- **Trap:** Searching only the end-title slot.
- **Evidence:** The title-expert lane verified that PHerc. 1497/1583 carries an initial title on its outer layer as well as final titles; 6 recto initial titles are attested, 12-25 cm outward of col. 1 in the initial agraphon; their rarity is ascribed to loss of the outer turns. The register cell for an initial title was re-weighted from 0.01 to about 0.045.
- **Fix:** Plan the outer end as a second search region from the start; quarantine the expected text from readers.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-25

### L230. A statistically informative channel can still be blind at reader level
- **Trap:** Treating a statistically significant pixel correlation as proof that blind readers could see the corresponding text in that channel.
- **Evidence:** Offset channel (verso-mode maps of the facing winding): median r 0.120 vs null p95 0.039 (Mann-Whitney p 4.6e-7) = INFORMATIVE at pixel level; yet in the verso census readers did not see known text through the facing winding, no window became a candidate, and the channel was closed as weak / reader-insensitive. The null excludes only a strong offset.
- **Fix:** Always include a reader-level positive control (known text seen through the same channel) and state the null as 'excludes only a signal far stronger than body text' when it fails.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-30..2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#P4-OFF-CORR-RESULT, #P4-OFF-VW-RESULT; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (P4-OFF-VW-RESULT); survey:expmap_raw.json:fine-tuning; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md#P4-OFF-VW-RESULT; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census; dominion:sib-p4v-10:README.md; dominion:sib-p4v-02:README.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md (P4-OFF-CORR-RESULT, P4-OFF-VW-RESULT); dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md#P4-OFF-CORR-RESULT

### L231. A resumed stale checkpoint can make a reproducibility gate pass vacuously
- **Trap:** Running a 'repro' recompute after a code change while the inference tool silently resumes bands computed under the old code.
- **Evidence:** After a code change, p4-excl's repro gate first reported PASS, but infer.py had resumed a band checkpoint made under the old own_common.py (resume_band 7), so no band was recomputed under the new code. The PASS was corrected; a fresh recompute with the checkpoint moved aside (resume lines 0) gave the identical png sha256 and a genuine PASS, repeated after the next code change.
- **Fix:** For any repro gate, move checkpoints aside, assert 'resume lines: 0' in the log, then compare png sha256.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-excl:README.md, logs/sib/p4-excl/STATUS.md

### L232. Do not assume the first text you confirm is the roll's first column
- **Trap:** Placing an initial-title search band relative to whichever text block you happen to confirm first.
- **Evidence:** Own-model searches found text-like column clusters in each successive search region, so the predicted initial-title band moved each time; much of the searched area was NO-DATA (missing public CT). Positions are withheld for prize review.
- **Fix:** Keep mapping until an OBSERVED blank band is found (NO-DATA is not blank) before fixing an initial-title band; the literature places initial titles 12-25 cm before column 1 (PHerc. 1497/1583).
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-25

### L233. An automated row-structure score did not detect known text on 9 um maps
- **Trap:** Using line periodicity (3.5-8 mm pitch) of ink maps to find text automatically.
- **Evidence:** Row score on 112 known-text PHerc0139 tiles vs 144 cross-winding PHerc0268 tiles: only 1.8 % of known-text tiles exceed the junk 99th percentile; fibre and crush periodicity score as high as text. The score passes its synthetic test. Also: Calibration: 112 known-text tiles p25/p50/p75/p90 = 7.5/10.1/13.9/17.6; 144 cross-winding junk tiles p50/p90/p99 = 11.0/17.3/28.1; only 0.018 of positives exceeded the null p99 (bar 0.25): NOT SENSITIVE.
- **Fix:** Calibrate any automatic text detector on known text vs real junk of the same scale before use; publish the failure.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-02..2026-10-03 · **Sources:** dominion:fl4t:README.md, tools/fl4/rowscore.py; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#FL5-ROWSCORE-RESULT; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (FL5-ROWSCORE-RESULT), logs/fl4t/fl5_rowscore_calibration.json; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Row-structure score calibration); orgsec-ink:HEAD:README.md

### L234. Implausible ink fractions and forward/reverse disagreement are void signatures
- **Trap:** Reading structure into maps where the model marks half the area as ink or both orders disagree.
- **Evidence:** FL-4 ring1: the 2023 GP TimeSformer marked 46-59 % of each patch as ink (frac >= 128 0.4439 on one patch) -> maps void. Ring2-4 ink_9um maps were uniform speckle on non-flat renders (e.g. 0.185 of a map >= 0.5). PHerc0800 6/6 and PHerc1203 20/20 organizer-segment maps showed no row alignment and forward and reverse were unrelated; a two-model agreement check on one PHerc0800 segment was barely above its controls (FL6-AGREE-RESULT).
- **Fix:** Pre-declare plausible ink-fraction ranges and require forward/reverse and two-model consistency checks against controls before any map is triaged.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-02..2026-10-03 · **Sources:** dominion:fl4t:README.md, logs/fl4t/ring1/i102/gp_forward.json, logs/fl4t/ring2/i4/ink9um_forward.json; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-FL-4-A8, #DECL-FL-4-A9

### L235. Two-model agreement with rotation controls is a cheap ink-feature check
- **Trap:** Taking diffuse blobs on one model's map as ink-like features.
- **Evidence:** On a PHerc0800 organizer sheet, ink_9um vs GP 0.5 mm-smoothed Pearson r 0.134 against rotation/flip controls up to 0.097: barely above control. Across 6 PHerc0800 and 20 PHerc1203 organizer segments the ink_9um maps were speckle or 1-3 mm blobs, no row alignment, forward and reverse unrelated; raw-density views showed fibre weave, cracks and edge drift off-sheet, no letter shapes.
- **Fix:** Use rotated/flipped controls for any agreement statistic; agreement near the control means no shared features.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-02 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#FL6-AGREE-RESULT, #FL6-RESULT, #FL6-RESULT-A1, #FL6-RAWDENSITY-RESULT; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (FL6-AGREE-RESULT); logs/fl4t/sv0800_i1_agree.json, RULES.md (FL6-AGREE-RESULT); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Two-model agreement test on a PHerc0800 sheet)

### L236. A model-free channel is a useful cross-check, but at 8.6-9.4 um it showed no letter-scale contrast here
- **Trap:** Hoping a model-free raw-density view of organizer sheets (PHerc1203, PHerc0800 at 8.6-9.4 um) shows letters that ink models miss.
- **Evidence:** 6 sheets (4 PHerc1203, 2 PHerc0800): the layers showed fibre weave with cracks, voids and 1-3 mm blotches aligned with fibres or cracks, and no rows; the organizer segments drift off-sheet at their edges. The raw-density channel yielded no candidate.
- **Fix:** Keep a model-free channel as a cross-check, but do not expect letter-scale contrast from it at 8.6-9.4 um.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-03 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (FL6-RAWDENSITY-RESULT); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Raw-density view of organizer sheets)

### L237. Calibrate every metric on a known positive and a known negative; keep failed tools
- **Trap:** A "stroke vs blob energy" index scored the control letters 0.28 and a known-negative strip 0.62, and the script was deleted, so the claim could not be audited.
- **Evidence:** The index scored the PHerc0343 control letters 0.28 and a known-negative strip 0.62, the wrong way round; the claim was withdrawn (SUPERSEDED_CLAIMS S13). The script was deleted, so no output survives to audit, which is exactly the failure.
- **Fix:** Calibrate every metric on a known positive AND a known negative before using it; keep failed tools and their outputs.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-09..2026-10-14 (approx.) · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#8, docs/SUPERSEDED_CLAIMS.md#S13

### L238. A narrow pass sizes one setting; it is not a certificate
- **Trap:** 20-row control strips passed the "sees ink" rule narrowly, at d = +1 on one scroll, and the pass was first treated as certifying the 20-row geometry beyond the control.
- **Evidence:** RESULTS 1 (Z20 recall 0.625 [0.495, 0.719]); S9.
- **Fix:** A passed sensitivity bar sizes what that geometry shows on the control at that depth and sheet contrast; it does not carry over to another scroll, depth or contrast without a control run there.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-09..2026-10-14 (approx.) · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#10, docs/RESULTS.md#1, docs/SUPERSEDED_CLAIMS.md#S9

### L239. Take validity from the CT, never from ink p > 0
- **Trap:** Villa ink maps are non-zero over the blank margin (about p = 0.31), so p > 0 is not a validity mask.
- **Evidence:** METHODS 4; stripqc.score.load_arm and tests/test_margins_patchgrid.py.
- **Fix:** Take validity from the CT (render / ctlayers > 0).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-09..2026-10-14 (approx.) · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#13, docs/METHODS.md#4

### L240. Seam agreement between two meshes is a CT response, not proof of ink
- **Trap:** Ink-model maps of two independent meshes agreed at the same 3-D points (r 0.43-0.50, p about 0.01-0.03 by direction); the agreement persisted under the margin fill but failed face specificity.
- **Evidence:** Two independently fitted surfaces were matched point to point within 4 vox; their ink maps agreed at shared 3-D points (r 0.43-0.50, p 0.01-0.03 by direction) against a circular-shift null (B's columns shifted 200 ... W - 200 px in steps of 25). The agreement persisted under the margin fill but failed face specificity (stripqc.seam docstring; private record; METHODS 9).
- **Fix:** Agreement validates the pixel-to-3-D mapping and shows a reproducible CT response. Both maps read the same CT, so certifying ink needs face specificity and a displaced negative control.
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-10-09..2026-10-14 (approx.) · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#16, docs/METHODS.md#9

### L241. Check the margin geometry before any metric near a strip edge
- **Trap:** The margin artifact sits at fixed rows inside the strip edges (bands peak about 30-50 px inside the valid edge), so any metric or threshold evaluated there inherits it.
- **Evidence:** Natural-experiment band rows and the band/middle ratios before and after the fill (results/margin_artifact/, release fig. 1-2).
- **Fix:** Check the margin geometry (stripqc.margins) before computing any metric or threshold near a strip edge.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-09..2026-10-14 (approx.) · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#18, results/margin_artifact/natural_experiment_PHerc0268.json

### L242. Run the half-spacing displaced control first in any surface audit
- **Trap:** Auditing grown surfaces with a statistic that cannot tell a sheet from the gap beside it.
- **Evidence:** W3 peak audit of grown PHerc0268 surfaces: ON-PEAK 0.145 and 0.155 vs copies displaced by +0.5 x spacing 0.145 and 0.157 (difference -0.001 against a 0.30 bar); 67 % of vertices OFF_LAMINA and 19 % NO_PEAKS on surfaces and controls alike; the audit stopped after 2 of 78 surfaces by its own rule.
- **Fix:** Declare a displaced-copy control with a sensitivity bar and stop as soon as it fails.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-E2E-4, #VC3D-AUDIT-RESULT; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:logs/unr/vc3d_audit/summary.json; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Identity audit of 78 VC3D-grown PHerc0268 surfaces (DECL-E2E-4))

### L243. A hop detector is interpretable only alongside its unshifted-control false-alarm rate
- **Trap:** Reading a higher hop-detection rate as better sheet-identity tracking (3-D sheet-likeness operator for ORD-3, ORD3-S3, PHerc0268).
- **Evidence:** The operator sharpened what it accepted (sheet centring 0.935 on accepted cells, passing 0.90) but accepted less: CLEAN minimum within 0.28 mm 0.157 (2-D ridge 0.275). It separated the sheet from neighbours no better (margin 0.06-0.08). Hop detection rose to 0.60 (from 0.30) while the control false-alarm rate rose to 0.40 (from 0.05): uninterpretable. Verdict: failed.
- **Fix:** Report hop detection only beside the unshifted-control false-alarm rate; a detection gain that comes with an equal false-alarm gain is no gain.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (ORD3-S3-RESULT); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (3-D sheet-likeness operator for ORD-3 (ORD3-S3))

### L244. Forward/reverse agreement is not ink validation
- **Trap:** Reading a gold overlay from a model that fails its held-out bars.
- **Evidence:** On the end-to-end strip the forward and reverse maps agreed at r 0.982 (controls 0.102) although the model's held-out AUC was 0.58; p_fwd max 0.505; 11 pixels (0.01 %) exceeded the declared 0.5 threshold.
- **Fix:** Label such output MODEL OUTPUT, not ink, and write the held-out numbers beside every map.
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-E2E-1, #E2E-1-RESULT

### L245. Proposed snap QA thresholds pass a half-winding error
- **Trap:** Gating snapped meshes with frac_rejected <= 0.2, p90 < 8, median |off| <= 3.
- **Evidence:** A half-winding (+12 voxel) shift passes three of the four thresholds, and the shift-0 controls fail frac_rejected. A winding with frac_already_on ~0.17 and frac_rejected ~0.4 is the measured 'not on the papyrus' baseline (B16u s500 w022-w060: frac_already_on 0.16-0.22, frac_rejected 0.37-0.45).
- **Fix:** Catch half-winding errors with frac_already_on, the pre/post on-sheet fraction and an independent check (CT overlays, winding-gap consistency); calibrate any threshold on a positive control (a mesh known to sit on the papyrus) before use.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/PIPELINE.md, docs/POC.md

### L246. An on-sheet tile gate works as a screen but cannot certify a surface
- **Trap:** Using a CT layer-profile gate alone to declare a surface on-sheet.
- **Evidence:** tile_gate.py with --min-lt20 0.75 --require-orient 1: PHerc0343 w047 34/52 tiles ON vs +8-vox copy 5/52 and -8 copy 0/47; PHerc0268 w161 strip 6/6 vs its +/-8 copies 0/6. Thresholds were frozen on these validation pairs before any search surface was gated.
- **Fix:** Use the gate to screen; let orientation and render texture decide; freeze its thresholds on displaced-copy controls first.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/FL_SEARCH.md, poc/fl/validation.json

### L247. An ink response that is equally strong on contorted, off-sheet surface is not ink
- **Trap:** Reading blobs on a partly valid patch.
- **Evidence:** PoC v0 (w161, seed42 d -1..+1): soft blobs ~100-200 px; the excluded contorted part responded as much as the single-sheet part (mean 92 vs 83; 5.3 % vs 4.8 % of pixels above the global p95); forward/reverse r = 0.58 at d = 0; d-1 vs d+1 r = 0.88.
- **Fix:** Compare valid vs invalid parts of the same surface; demand sheet specificity before any reading.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/POC.md

### L248. Ranking strips by ink-pixel fraction surfaces artifacts first
- **Trap:** Strips were ranked by their fraction of p > 0.55, and edge bands dominated it.
- **Evidence:** results/margin_artifact/fill_test_PHerc0268_aggregate.json: the strong fraction fell 2.96-623.9x once the margin was filled. Also: The rank-1 strip by p > 0.55 fraction in the first mass pass fell from 14.3 % to 0.10 % strong once the blank margin was filled; most top-ranked strips were margin-band dominated.
- **Fix:** Rank by excess over the patch's own OFF_SHEET tiles and edges (where texture and edge artefacts live), after margin fill, and only among on-sheet tiles.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/FL_SEARCH.md, poc/mass_fill/DECL.md; dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#12, results/margin_artifact/fill_test_PHerc0268_aggregate.json

### L249. The blank-margin bug: partly blank inference patches create or suppress ink
- **Trap:** vc_render_tifxyz leaves all-zero rows at strip edges; villa ink inference normalises partly blank patches with the zeros included. This created false orange bands on PHerc0268 and roughly halved real ink on PHerc0343 (13-row recall 0.386).
- **Evidence:** RESULTS 1-3 and results/ (fill test: strong fraction fell 2.96-623.9x on 7 PHerc0268 strips; control Z13 recall 0.386 vs F13 0.646). Also: Strip renders always had 30 blank rows at the bottom and 30 or 10 at the top; ~2/3 of mass-run strips showed ink bands 30-50 px inside the valid edges. 128-px patches, stride 64, Hann blending, per-patch robust normalisation (no mask) and InstanceNorm all take in the blank rows. Natural experiment at fixed render rows (release code): ink 0.163 vs 0.049 with a 30- vs 10-row top margin on 24/29 strips (260 px) and 0.190 vs 0.029 on 6/7 (400 px) (dominion:main:results/margin_artifact/natural_experiment_PHerc0268.json; first reported as 0.130 vs 0.020, 29/32, retracted R025); CT in the band rows equals the middle rows; the interior profile fits a Hann blend on the true patch grid (R^2 0.993). Re-inking 7 strips with the margin filled cut strong ink 2.96-623.9x (first reported as 3-700x, retracted R024) (e.g. 12.5 % -> 0.02 %, 14.3 % -> 0.10 %) and removed the bands in 5/7.
- **Fix:** Fill the blank margin by reflection for the models only (batch_ink RENDER_FILL=reflect; scoring and overlays keep the original valid pixels) or mask normalisation; always look at ink vs distance-from-valid-edge before believing a strip.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#11, docs/RESULTS.md#1, #3, docs/SUPERSEDED_CLAIMS.md#S11, #S12, results/margin_artifact/natural_experiment_PHerc0268.json; pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/FL_SEARCH.md, poc/mass_fill/DECL.md, poc/mass_fill/compare.out, poc/ctrl343_strips/eval.out; pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5@6c989b9:docs/FL_SEARCH.md (PHerc0268 repository); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (PHerc0268 mass ink run (separate repository))

### L250. A fixed display threshold hides ink that the model still ranks correctly
- **Trap:** On 13-row strips the p scale compresses (99th percentile of p 0.690 -> 0.620), so a fixed threshold (p > 0.55) or fixed display (0.40-0.70) loses much of the ink even though the ranking survives (box AUC 0.670 vs 0.709 on the same pixels).
- **Evidence:** RESULTS 1: matched-rate recall 0.595 vs fixed-threshold recall 0.386 for Z13.
- **Fix:** When geometry changes, check ranking metrics (AUC, matched-rate recall) as well as fixed thresholds before declaring ink lost or absent.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/RESULTS.md#1, results/control_strips_rerun/results.json

### L251. A displaced copy is not automatically an ink-free negative
- **Trap:** The models read layers S..S+16 (-6.5 to +9.5 vox at d = +1); a copy moved +8 vox outward still holds the original sheet's CT peak (+2.5 vox) in its window. With the fill (FD8) it shows a weak letter-located signal (recall 0.032, in-box strong 1.38 % vs 0.39 % outside).
- **Evidence:** RESULTS 1 and METHODS 2 (D8 recall 0.002; FD8 recall 0.032).
- **Fix:** Check the model's depth window against the displacement; displace by a full sheet pitch or use a window that excludes the sheet for a clean negative (not run here). Treat FD8-type controls as a conservative floor.
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/RESULTS.md#1, docs/METHODS.md#2

### L252. Where the villa defect lives: robust normalisation over blank voxels
- **Trap:** All three checkpoints declare robust_mad normalisation; villa calls normalize_robust(patch) with mask=None, so median/MAD/percentiles include blank voxels. Only entirely empty patches are skipped (nonempty flag); partly blank patches are normalised with zeros; InstanceNorm2d and convolutions also see zeros.
- **Evidence:** METHODS 4 (VERIFIED against villa 41701aa; infer.py and normalization.py byte-identical on villa main 5432721, 14 Oct 2026).
- **Fix:** Fill the input (measured mitigation) or patch villa to normalise over valid voxels only (normalize_robust(..., mask=patch > 0, use_mask=True); INFERENCE, untested; InstanceNorm would still see zeros).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/METHODS.md#4, docs/RESULTS.md#5

### L253. Depth does not explain the opposite sign between scrolls
- **Trap:** It was plausible that the mass-run depth (d = -2) caused false bands. At d = -2 the control Z13 recall is 0.428 (ratio 1.109 to d = +1) and the edge band 0.37 % vs 0.75 % full context: suppression, not bands.
- **Evidence:** RESULTS 1 (pre-registered decision 6, report only, original run).
- **Fix:** Run the positive control at the mass-run depth too; the sign difference (bands on PHerc0268, suppression on PHerc0343) remains unexplained.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/RESULTS.md#1, #3

### L254. A displaced copy of the mesh (+/-8 vox, half the sheet spacing) is the decisive no-ink control
- **Trap:** Accepting a residual that survives margin fill as ink without checking whether it follows the sheet.
- **Evidence:** PHerc0343 no-ink arm: strips displaced +8 vox have in-box strong 0.3 %, recall 0.00, r 0.22 (the arm works). On PHerc0268 the largest residual after fill persisted 8 vox off the sheet (ratio 0.64 against a bar of <= 0.2), including a tile flagged by the audit: a volumetric texture response, not surface ink.
- **Fix:** Pre-register a displaced-copy arm for every candidate; require its strong fraction <= 0.2x the original's.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/FL_SEARCH.md, poc/mass_fill/DECL.md

### L255. Test face specificity: real ink sits on the reading face, texture shows on both
- **Trap:** Treating reverse-map ink that also appears in the forward map as ink.
- **Evidence:** Face-specificity metrics: share of reverse p > 0.55 pixels with forward p < 0.40, and r(fwd, rev). PHerc0343 letters: 0.99 / 0.07 and 0.72 / 0.24. Under fill, the only same-sheet seam pair still agreed (r 0.50, p 0.01) but failed face specificity (share 0.45 / 0.37); the only face-specific PHerc0268 strip had 0.26 % strong pixels and 4x more strong pixels in the forward map.
- **Fix:** Run INK_DIR=both and require share >= 0.5 and r(fwd, rev) < 0.3 in the candidate region.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/FL_SEARCH.md, poc/mass_fill/DECL.md

### L256. Push a known-letters control through the identical pipeline before reading any null
- **Trap:** Building a batch render-ink-overlay pipeline and reading PHerc0268 outputs without proving the pipeline sees ink.
- **Evidence:** batch_ink.sh on the PHerc0343 control reproduces the earlier maps byte for byte; 12.4 % of pixels inside letter boxes vs 0.4 % outside (31x); forward 0 %. The later strip-geometry control (DECL-FL-STRIP) exposed that 13-row strips do not see ink (recall 0.39).
- **Fix:** For every geometry/pipeline change, re-run the control in the same geometry and report recall, E (in/out ratio) and r against the full-context reference.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/FL_SEARCH.md, poc/ctrl343_strips/DECL.md

**Blind reading and evaluation (L257-L296).** AI blind readers: displays, key sheets, sealed-output harnesses, reader nulls and calibration. Reader namings are mostly idiosyncratic until calibrated (L269, L270), and an uncalibrated read is uninformative (L293).

### L257. Blind readers cannot tell reference maps from their mirror images: handedness cannot be fixed by reader votes
- **Trap:** Deciding scan handedness by asking blind readers which of a mirrored pair shows normal writing.
- **Evidence:** HANDED-1: all 12 votes UNSURE (windows chosen by coverage had no writing). HANDED-R2 (human-label-chosen windows): A 7, B 1, none 4. HANDED-R3B: A 5, B 13, none 6. Pooled decided votes A 12 : B 14; readers still named 2-3 letters per window on the side they picked.
- **Fix:** Choose test windows by human-label ink density, not coverage; if votes stay ambiguous read both mirror states as separate declared arms; treat inability to discriminate mirror states as evidence the namings are not real letter perception.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:LEDGER.md, logs/handed/handed_r3b_scorer_output.json, RULES.md (HANDED-R3B), RULES.md (HANDED-R3-VOID), RULES.md (entry HANDED-R3B); logs/handed/handed_r3b_scorer_output.json, RULES.md (entry HANDED-R3B); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (HANDED-R3B: larger handedness re-test (8 fresh windows)); dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#HANDED-1, #HANDED-R2, #HANDED-R3B

### L258. Blind LLM readers named almost no letters in official 0139 reference maps at 9 um-canvas scale without calibration
- **Trap:** Assuming a vision LLM can read official high-resolution reference ink maps once resampled to the 9 um canvas.
- **Evidence:** Picker on 33 candidate 2 x 2 cm windows (1/2 scale): w053 22 of 24 windows 0 letters, w024 all 0, firm namings 0; HANDED-1: 0 letters in all 4 windows; archive: 0 of 14 reference letters confirmed.
- **Fix:** Calibrate the display/prompt/reader on known text before any sealed decision (see the key-sheet K_D2 lesson); keep SG bars unchanged and record 'SG infeasible at current display'.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#RCPICK-1, #HANDED-1; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (entry RCPICK-1); logs/readcal/picker1_counts.json (selected: []), RULES.md (entry RCPICK-1); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (READ-CAL bank picker (RCPICK-1))

### L259. Agent harness silently resamples images larger than 1068 px per side
- **Trap:** Showing a 2136 x 2136 px image to a vision subagent: letters were still named 12/12 but centre coordinates came back in a shrunken frame (fitted scale 0.966 x / 0.964 y; centre error median 57.5 px, max 82 px) because the harness resampled the image by an unknown method.
- **Evidence:** Synthetic test with 12 font-rendered Greek capitals: 1068 px image -> centre error median 0.7 px, max 2.5 px, scale 1.000; 2136 px image -> median 57.5 px, scale 0.966/0.964.
- **Fix:** Cap every image shown to a picker, sealer or reader at 1068 px per side (e.g. a 2 x 2 cm window at 9.366 um shown at 1/2 scale by INTER_AREA); never rely on the harness to downscale.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#HARNESS-COORD, #DECL-READCAL-A1, CHANGELOG.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (entry HARNESS-COORD), RULES.md (entry HARNESS-SEALED-TEST); survey:expmap_raw.json:reading-calibration; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (HARNESS-COORD), logs/harness_jobs.tsv

### L260. A perception test needs material known to contain the thing perceived
- **Trap:** Choosing windows for a perception test (HANDED-1, reader handedness) by map coverage alone, so they may hold no writing.
- **Evidence:** 3 readers on 4 mirrored pairs (bar >= 10 of 12 votes for one state): A 0, B 0, no vote 12; every answer 'unsure' and no letters named. Verdict AMBIGUOUS.
- **Fix:** Use material known to contain the thing perceived (for handedness: windows chosen by human-label ink density).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (entry HANDED-1); logs/handed/handed1_scorer_output.json; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (HANDED-1: reader handedness test (coverage-chosen windows))

### L261. A suggestive lean in a small vote is not a decision
- **Trap:** Treating a suggestive lean in a small vote as a decision (HANDED-R2, label-chosen windows).
- **Evidence:** Votes A 7, B 1, unsure 4 against a bar of >= 10 of 12: AMBIGUOUS, so both mirror states stayed as separate reading arms. Readers named 8, 10 and 12 letters on the side they judged normal. The larger re-test HANDED-R3B went A 5, B 13, none 6 (L257): the lean did not hold.
- **Fix:** Keep the pre-declared bar, and read both states as declared arms until it is met.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (entry HANDED-R2); logs/handed/handed_r2_scorer_output.json, logs/handed/handed_r2_scorer_output.json; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (HANDED-R2: reader handedness re-test (label-chosen windows))

### L262. A seal made by readers measures what readers perceive, not ground truth
- **Trap:** Treating a seal made by readers as ground truth (D1 sealed benchmark construction, PHerc0841).
- **Evidence:** Three sealed-output sealers produced a consensus seal of S' = 20 letters (9 firm) over five held-out windows of the organizers' official reference maps, committed by hash before any project render of those windows existed; small-seal regime, so p_max < 0.005 was required. An earlier picker check at the unoriented display, before the key sheet existed, named 15 (3 firm). Two text-free blank windows were confirmed by a fresh picker (rows N, 0 letters).
- **Fix:** Treat recall against a reader-made seal as a consistency measure, not accuracy against ground truth.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (entry JPICK-1), RULES.md (entry SEAL-J-D1); logs/d1/jseal_summary.json, RULES.md (entry SEAL-J-D1); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (D1 sealed benchmark construction)

### L263. A placebo-controlled exemplar arm is the right design for testing whether prompting improves reading; it remains untested here
- **Trap:** Assuming a prompting change (an exemplar arm) improves reading without a placebo-controlled test (READCAL-2 reader-acuity programme).
- **Evidence:** Builder deliverables only: display and sheet builders for six arms (30 unit tests), a measured noise spectrum of blank base maps, a candidate bank under same-papyrus exclusions, and scoring glue reproducing the D1 sigma_crit. No reader, picker or sealer ran, so no read was made.
- **Fix:** Test prompting with a placebo-controlled exemplar arm; that test remains untested here.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-readcal2@46a7c29a3:logs/sib/readcal2/STATUS.md, logs/sib/readcal2/REPORT.md, logs/sib/readcal2/REPORT.md (Deliverables); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (READCAL-2 reader-acuity programme (sib-readcal2))

### L264. Build the benchmark bank first, and record every contradiction (offsets, label semantics) as a numbered correction
- **Trap:** Starting reads before the benchmark bank exists, or silently resolving contradictions in offsets and label semantics (PHerc0841 known-text bank).
- **Evidence:** Bank: 4,147 files (3.67 GB) with a hashed manifest. 2.4 -> 9 um mapping error on a synthetic test 0.012 px; cross-resolution NCC put the real reference mapping within ~1.4 px. Only 0.248 cm^2 (< 0.5 cm^2) of reference text lay outside the exclusion shell, which forced the pooled text order. The numbered corrections changed two downstream choices, the blank source and the pooled order, before any read.
- **Fix:** Build the benchmark bank first, and record every contradiction (offsets, label semantics) as a numbered correction.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-24 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (B0841-BANK), logs/bank0841/summary.json; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (PHerc0841 known-text bank)

### L265. A First Letters submission gate needs far more than reader agreement
- **Trap:** Treating a handful of agreeing namings as a prize-ready result.
- **Evidence:** Declared SG 0-14: USABLE arm on a sealed same-protocol benchmark; >= 12 letters agreed by >= 2 of 3 fresh readers with >= 8 firm and agreed - null p99 >= 10 over >= 40 empirical-null tiles; opposite order <= 2; +-1 slice re-confirmation >= 80 %; second lineage and independent re-trace each reproduce >= 50 %; copy test vs training patches; >= 128 vox + 64 px clearance from training; 0 mesh crossings and >= 93.1 % low-distortion quads; >= 2 rows, letter heights 2-4 mm; handedness and rotation checks. SG-FEAS never passed even on reference maps.
- **Fix:** Use a gate like SG 0-14 and calibrate it on known text before attempting a discovery read.
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-09-24 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-SG, #DECL-EMPNULL, #READCAL-FREEZE

### L266. Builders who never view, uuid file names and a scorer-held key keep displays blind
- **Trap:** Folder names such as /A/, /B/, /D2/, /blank/, /J/ in image paths shown to readers.
- **Evidence:** DECL-D1-A5 disclosure: the image paths of the HANDED-1/-R2/-R3B and PROBE-1/2/3 briefs contained folder names for mirror state or display (/A/, /B/, /D2/, /D1Q/, /N2/), visible to readers, and the J-seal blank picker's paths contained 'blank'. No brief said which state was correct and every reader of a probe saw the same names, so no result depended on them, but the audits had not noticed. From D1 on, every reader and canary image lives in one flat folder under a random uuid name, and only the key maps uuids to window, kind, order and state.
- **Fix:** Put every reader image in one flat folder under random uuid names, written in shuffled order with equal mtimes; keep the uuid->arm map in a scorer-only key (0400).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-tiles-a:logs/sib/p4-tiles-a/REPORT.md, README.md; dominion:sib-p4-tiles-a@b59df7ec7:logs/sib/p4-tiles-a/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-p4-tiles-b@58981e078:logs/sib/p4-tiles-b/REPORT.md; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-D1-A5, #D1-VERDICT

### L267. A font-rendered Greek key sheet shown first makes blind readers agree beyond chance (K_D2 display, fable model)
- **Trap:** Prompting readers with text alone; or trusting a single passing cell without fresh-material replication.
- **Evidence:** PROBE-2 (paired, same windows): one cell met >= 5 agreed with p < 0.05 (A_fable w039, 5 agreed, p 0.031); because windows were reused it lifted nothing. PROBE-3 on fresh windows: A_fable 10 agreed at w044, p 0.0005 -> REPLICATED; independent auditor PASS on all three probes. D1 REF ladder later: fresh fable readers recovered ~80 % of a 3-sealer seal on unseen 0841 reference maps.
- **Fix:** Freeze D* = key sheet (24 Greek capitals with lunate sigma, DejaVu Serif Bold, 1068 px) as first image + 2 x 2 cm window at 1/2 scale; P* = configs/briefs/k_d2_task.txt; reader model fable only. Replicate any lift on fresh material before relying on it.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#PROBE2-RESULT, #PROBE3-RESULT, #AUDIT-PROBES, #READCAL-FREEZE, #D1-REF-RESULT; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (entry PROBE2-RESULT); logs/readcal/probe2_results.json sha256 0e4b3fec..., RULES.md (entry PROBE2-RESULT), LEDGER.md (row READ-CAL PROBE-2); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (READ-CAL PROBE-2: font key sheet (paired re-read))

### L268. Calibrated legibility falls smoothly with blur: maps need an effective blur of <= ~0.30 mm to be read
- **Trap:** Not knowing how sharp a model map must be before spending blind reads on it.
- **Evidence:** D1 REF ladder on unseen 0841 reference maps (fresh fable readers, K_D2 display, S' = 20): summed mean C_net 11.37 at sigma 0, 8.44 at 0.15 mm, 6.42 at 0.30 mm, 4.30 at 0.45 mm (all p <= 4/5001); sigma_crit = 0.30 mm; blank namings 0.
- **Fix:** Estimate a candidate model's effective blur (sigma_eq vs the 2.4 um reference) before reading; candidates much blurrier than 0.30 mm are unlikely to be legible.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#D1-REF-RESULT, #D1-VERDICT, #DECL-DEVLOOP; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:logs/d1/d1_ref_summary.json (REF0) sha256 7c3884a2..., logs/d1/d1_ref_summary.json (REF0), logs/d1/d1_ref_summary.json (REF0 p_exact), logs/d1/d1_ref_summary.json (sigma_crit_mm)

### L269. Reader agreement beyond the identity-shuffle null is not proof of correct letters: agreed identities are dominated by simple symmetric shapes
- **Trap:** Treating agreed namings as correct letters.
- **Evidence:** PROBE-3 exploratory: 75-89 % of agreed letters per arm are mirror-symmetric capitals (O, I, T ...), matching 75-87 % of all namings; A and E never agreed in the primary arm; agreement insensitive to mirroring (A vs B 8 vs 9 opus, 11 vs 9 fable); agreed-firm 0.
- **Fix:** Score against a sealed transcription (C_net vs permutation null), require firm agreement, and report mirror-state sensitivity; treat agreement without a seal as shared perception of ink shapes only.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#PROBE3-RESULT, #PROBE2-RESULT; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:logs/readcal/probe3_results.json (field verdict) sha256 222976e3..., logs/readcal/probe3_results.json (max_agreed_in_window), RULES.md (entry PROBE3-RESULT), RULES.md (entry AUDIT-PROBES); logs/readcal/audit_probe3.json

### L270. Inter-reader agreement against a shuffle null is a usable legibility statistic, and here it showed reader namings were mostly idiosyncratic
- **Trap:** Assuming reference maps are blind-legible at some display without measuring inter-reader agreement (READ-CAL PROBE-1: display and reader-model grid).
- **Evidence:** 36 readers across 3 displays, 2 models and 2 mirror states (12 arms): at most 4 letters agreed in any window (pass needed >= 5 agreed with p < 0.05), 0 agreed-firm, every identity-shuffle p >= 0.107 (auditor correction: >= 0.117). At native 2.4 um (N2) every arm agreed on 0 letters. Recorded: reference maps not blind-legible at any tested display.
- **Fix:** Use inter-reader agreement against an identity-shuffle null as the legibility statistic; here it showed that namings were mostly idiosyncratic.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:LEDGER.md (row READ-CAL PROBE-1); logs/readcal/probe1_results.json sha256 aaa9bc22..., RULES.md (entry AUDIT-PROBES), RULES.md (entry PROBE1-RESULT); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (READ-CAL PROBE-1: display and reader-model grid)

### L271. A second benchmark needs blanks and a settled orientation, not just registered text windows
- **Trap:** Preparing a second sealed benchmark (KTLB-4P, fragment PHerc0500P) with registered text windows only.
- **Evidence:** Numbers-only builder work. CT patch registration with held-out patches frozen before reading: attempt 1 (affine) held-out median r 0.834, FAIL (bar 0.85); pre-registered attempt 2 (affine + RBF field) 0.929, PASS. Blank-window candidates (< 1 % reference ink): 0. Window certification and orientation sources were also prepared.
- **Fix:** Check early that a second benchmark has blanks and a settled orientation, not just registered text windows.

### L272. Display choice: whole 2 x 2 cm window at 1/2 scale beats full-scale tiles and native 2.4 um crops for blind readers
- **Trap:** Assuming more resolution (full-scale 1 x 1 cm tiles, native 2.4 um halved crops) helps LLM readers.
- **Evidence:** PROBE-1 (36 readers, 4 windows): agreed letters D2 6/6/6/3 per arm, D1Q 1-5, N2 0 in all arms; agreed-firm 0 everywhere; every identity-shuffle p >= 0.117.
- **Fix:** Use D2 (whole 2 x 2 cm window, 1/2 scale, INTER_AREA, 1068 px, raw 0-255) as the base display.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#PROBE1-RESULT, #AUDIT-PROBES

### L273. Never view target maps before the blind read; log every view
- **Trap:** The orchestrator looking at candidate maps before sealed reads exist.
- **Evidence:** Readers are general-purpose agents in sealed-output mode (one audited age-encrypted write); any other tool call voids the session; every image view is logged in views.tsv; the orchestrator never views seals, sealed references or target maps before they are read; viewing after the read is allowed.
- **Fix:** Make viewing rules explicit and audited; schedule human viewing after the read as a cheap credibility check.
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:configs/prompt/hercules_master_v7.md, CHANGELOG.md, logs/owner/AUDIT_2026-09-30.md

### L274. Check reader prompts from transcripts, not from truncated displays
- **Trap:** Concluding that a brief was truncated from a shortened terminal display.
- **Evidence:** An apparent truncation ('Everyt') was the orchestrator's own head -c 1500 display; transcripts showed all 30 D1 reader prompts equal to their brief files (12 exact, 18 differing only by a trailing newline).
- **Fix:** Compare transcript first prompts with brief files byte-for-byte (allowing one trailing newline) in the audit.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:CHANGELOG.md

### L275. Sealed-read harness: commit keys and briefs before any reader, never let the harness see answers
- **Trap:** Blind reads lose their value if briefs, keys or image lists can change after reading starts, or if the session running readers can see the answers.
- **Evidence:** rh-e1 ran 65 reader sessions in 8 batches and rh-e2 200 audited sessions in 12 batches, all with COMMIT A (key sha256, briefs, image manifest, builder ref) pushed and verified on the remote before any reader, fresh Opus readers whose prompt was byte-equal to the brief, answers age-encrypted to the orchestrator's public key, and a transcript audit before COMMIT B: every audited session VALID except one void attempt; 0 violations, 0 unread images.
- **Fix:** Use the two-commit protocol (A before readers, B with sealed answers, transcripts and audit), keep only the public key in the harness container, and audit prompt == brief, images read, image bytes unchanged and sealed-file sha256.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-10-02 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-rh-e1:logs/sib/rh-e1/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-rh-e2:logs/sib/rh-e2/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-rh-e1:README.md; dominion:sib-rh-e2:README.md; dominion:sib-rh-e1@a9ca62939:logs/sib/rh-e1/STATUS.md (E1 section), logs/sib/rh-e1/STATUS.md (L2S remainder section), logs/sib/rh-e1/STATUS.md (OWN_F2 / OWN_F3 section); survey:expmap_raw.json:reading-calibration; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (METRIC-HASH-30); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Remote blind-reader harness)

### L276. A research prior that is kept separate from expected text can direct where to look without contaminating blind reads
- **Trap:** Letting research priors (expected title zone, letter size, ink appearance) reach blind readers as expected text, or ignoring them.
- **Evidence:** Codicological and geometric research dossier (v4, sections 0-7): it fixed the strip orientation, estimated the expected title zone, recommended widening the readers' letter-size prior to 2-6 mm, and reported that this scroll's ink appears in 2.4 um CT as thin bright surface deposits. Its recommendations drove the thin-slab, layout, edge and further-strip tests, while expected-text material stayed in a quarantined section (L364).
- **Fix:** A research prior that is kept separate from expected text can direct where to look without contaminating blind reads.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-research@b234b9450:logs/sib/p4-research/STATUS.md; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census

### L277. If a calibration set's coordinates exist only in a lost key file, hold the papyrus out fail-closed
- **Trap:** A follow-up calibration must exclude windows already used, but their coordinates were kept only in a sealed key file outside the repo.
- **Evidence:** READ-CAL-2 builder could not reconstruct the 33 RCPICK-1 picker windows: re-running the attempt-2 rule gave 310 / 161 / 490 candidates vs the recorded 251 / 165 / 1731, so all E0 papyrus was held out and the bank was built from tier-N neighbours and PHerc0814.
- **Fix:** Publish exclusion lists (segment, y0, x0) as numbers in the repo at the time of use, separately from keys, so later calibrations can exclude exactly.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-readcal2:logs/sib/readcal2/REPORT.md, logs/sib/readcal2/ASK.md

### L278. Blank ink maps are not white noise; null models must reproduce their spectrum and blobs
- **Trap:** Exemplar and null sheets built from white noise underestimate how ink-like blank papyrus looks in model maps.
- **Evidence:** C2-NT base maps of two blank PHerc0139 windows: mean 76.8, variance 501 u8^2, 82 % of power below 0.01 cycles/px (> 1 mm); one blank has 3.8 % of pixels >= 150 (ink-like false positives). The exemplar noise reproduces the spectrum, not the blobs.
- **Fix:** Fit the null/noise model to real blank maps (2-D PSD) and also model blob statistics; never assume a blank map is i.i.d.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-readcal2:logs/sib/readcal2/REPORT.md, logs/sib/readcal2/noise_psd.json

### L279. Changing the reader model voids the reader calibration
- **Trap:** Owner instruction switched all new readers from the calibrated model (fable) to opus; the new reader's legibility on the display was unmeasured.
- **Evidence:** DECL-P4-2-A1: opus not lifted by PROBE-3; attention checks added (known-text strip must get rows = Y; positive control per phase-2 session); sealed decisions kept the calibrated reader.
- **Fix:** When the reader changes, add positive controls in every session and treat 'rows = N on known text' as reader failure; re-run calibration before any sealed decision.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-2-A1

### L280. Prompt and key sheet should cover script variants (lunate and four-bar sigma)
- **Trap:** A key sheet calibrated on one scroll showed only the lunate sigma; another scribe may write four-bar sigma.
- **Evidence:** Key sheet v2: 25 glyphs (24 capitals + four-bar sigma), deterministic render; scorer already normalises all sigma forms to one kind.
- **Fix:** Show all letterform variants in the key sheet and normalise them to one kind in scoring; never mix variants across a census and its null.
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-2-A2

### L281. Body-text census rules are blind to sparse, large or ornamented title blocks
- **Trap:** Requiring >= 5 letters in a 2 x 2 cm tile: a title of 2-6 centred lines (15-40 letters across 3-6 cm), possibly in larger calligraphic letters with dashes, flourishes or a coronis, can split across tiles below the bar; a 2-4 mm size prior can make readers skip 5-6 mm title letters.
- **Evidence:** Recorded design defect; scholarship dossier: text letters ~3 mm, titles ~3-5 mm, up to ~6 mm; decorations attested in PHerc. 172, 1027, 1457.
- **Fix:** Add a 4 x 4 cm 'block' brief (26.7 px/mm) asking for deliberate block Y/N, line count, letters 2-15 mm and non-letter marks; widen size prior to 2-6 mm; positive = block Y and letters+marks >= max(5, null p99).
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-17, #DECL-P4-12-A1, #METRIC-HASH-38

### L282. Where Herculaneum titles are: scholarly priors for title searches
- **Trap:** Searching only beside the last column, or assuming one ink colour.
- **Evidence:** Dossier: ~91 % of Herculaneum end titles stand beside the last column (Cavallo 1983), ~7 % below it; initial titles attested (PHerc. 222, 253, 1457, 1583, 1786, 1008; in 1457 ~12 cm before column 1); verso titles attested (PHerc. 339, 1491, 1670); text starts outside and ends near the core. Rubrication/coloured titles are mainly codex and later practice; Herculaneum titles read so far are mostly black ink.
- **Fix:** Keep a live hypothesis register with priors, mechanisms, tests and blind spots (location, face, depth, colourant, damage, mesh error, display/reader failure) and re-rank after each result.
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-15, #DECL-P4-6-A1, #OWNER-STANDING-ORDER-2

### L283. A 0-positive census under a gate that never passed is uninformative
- **Trap:** Reporting 0 letters on target tiles as evidence that no text is there, when the same batch also read 0 letters on known text.
- **Evidence:** In o2s1 every tile, the 3 known-text gate tiles included, was rows N with 0 letters. The record classifies the batch as UNINFORMATIVE, not a title-zone null, and tiles finishing later can only be read in a later batch under the same gate. Also: First Letters FL-2/FL-3 census: the held-out PHerc0139 positive-control gate was NOT SENSITIVE in every wave, so 0 positives on 8 tiles per scroll (FL2-WAVE1) and 4-54 stitched 4x4 cm windows per scroll (FL3-W1) mean nothing; 43 PHerc0268 FL-4 items read with 0 positives were later declared VOID because every FL-4 grow cut across windings.
- **Fix:** Pre-register the gate (here >= 30 % of gate tiles rows Y with >= 5 letters) and make the verdict on target tiles conditional on it; label a failed-gate batch void/uninformative in every summary.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27..2026-10-02 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-fl-pherc0175b:README.md; dominion:sib-fl-pherc0211:README.md; dominion:sib-fl-pherc0257:README.md; dominion:sib-fl-pherc1545:README.md; dominion:sib-p4v-02:README.md; dominion:sib-p4v-09:README.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md (DECL-FL-5); dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (FL2-WAVE1-RESULT), logs/fl2/wave1_result.json; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (FL-2 single-tile census, wave 1); dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (FL3-W1-RESULT), RULES.md (FL3-W1-RESULT); logs/fl2/fl3w1_result.json; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (FL-3 stitched-window census); dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#FL2-WAVE1-RESULT, #FL2-WAVE2-GATE, #FL3-W1-GATE, #FL3-W1-RESULT; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (FL2-WAVE2-GATE item 5); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (FL-2 single-tile census, wave 2); dominion:sib-o5w5:README.md; dominion:sib-o5w6:README.md; dominion:sib-o5w8:README.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#P4-O-STAGE-O2S1-RESULT

### L284. Session validity = transcript audit; allow exactly one re-run of a void session
- **Trap:** API rate limits (HTTP 429 'session limit') kill reader agents mid-session; re-running to get a 'complete' answer risks choosing between sealed answers.
- **Evidence:** A usage limit voided one extended-test session (0 tool calls); one re-run on the identical commit-A brief passed audit. Three sessions sealed valid answers but lost the DONE hand-back (HTTP 429) and were kept as valid under the pinned audit code. Earlier, 6 reader agents died before any tool call and were re-run fresh; an owner-side interrupt stopped 4 readers before their sealed write.
- **Fix:** Run at most ~4 readers concurrently, classify a session as void only if it sealed nothing, re-run a void session exactly once under the committed brief and disclose it; never overwrite a sealed answer.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#METRIC-HASH-44, CHANGELOG.md; paris-4:gifted-bell-gavnl5:results/own_s1x_audit.json, results/census_own_s1x_summary.json, README.md; dominion:sib-rh-e2:logs/sib/rh-e2/ASK.md, README.md

### L285. A label-scrambled NULL model measures reader hallucination on textured maps
- **Trap:** Treating 5-7 named letters on a tile as evidence of writing.
- **Evidence:** Maps from the label-deranged NULL model were read with 2-5 letters (0 firm) on all 3 candidate tiles but showed text on only 1 of 3 control tiles (1 letter) that both other seeds read as text. Reader false positives on textured non-ink maps can therefore reach 5 letters; firm letters were the stronger signal (NULL: 0 firm on every tile).
- **Fix:** Require a candidate to be positive in >= 2 of 3 independently seeded models AND below threshold in the NULL model's map of the same tile; weight firm letters; treat counts of 5-7 alone as weak.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-25-A7; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:logs/p4/g1_own.json; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census

### L286. Confirmations inside one block, read by one model family, are one result
- **Trap:** Counting confirmations of neighbouring tiles from one text-like area, read by one model family, as independent finds.
- **Evidence:** In the Paris 4 title search a candidate was found and tested; details withheld for prize review. In the extended-test design (upright tile vs the same tile rotated 90 deg, plus 48 rotated-null tiles, exact permutation over 48,620 labelings) the smallest attainable p is 1/48,620 = 2.06e-5, so a floor-level p on several neighbouring tiles adds no independent evidence. The 2026-09-30 adversarial audit noted that confirmations inside one block, read by one model family, are one result, not several, and that no human had viewed any confirmed lead.
- **Fix:** Report adjacent confirmations as one lead; before filing, add an independent reader family and the owner's or a papyrologist's viewing after the blind read.
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-09-27..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:logs/owner/AUDIT_2026-09-30.md, RULES.md#DECL-P4-25-A2; paris-4:gifted-bell-gavnl5:SUBMISSION.md, README.md

### L287. Screen builder manifests for all-zero duplicate tiles before drawing null tiles
- **Trap:** Census manifests can contain blank prediction tiles with identical bytes; nulls drawn from the batch itself can then be degenerate copies.
- **Evidence:** Paris 4 census batches: 11, 14 and 12 tiles in three batches had prediction mean 0.0 and identical bytes, kept as declared and disclosed; 2 of 18 and 1 of 18 N0 null tiles were drawn from them. An interim 3-tile manifest not flagged partial would have produced a null that is a rotated copy of a census tile in the same session; the stage rule refused it.
- **Fix:** Count unique PNG hashes and all-zero tiles in every manifest, exclude or flag them before N0 sampling, and require minimum tile counts per stage so a null is never drawn from a tiny batch.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-rh-e2:logs/sib/rh-e2/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-pairs0814b:logs/sib/pairs0814b/rh/ASK.md

### L288. Stitch tiles into 4 x 4 cm windows for the census, then re-test every window hit at tile scale
- **Trap:** Reading isolated 2 cm tiles (no cohesive context), or trusting window counts near the threshold.
- **Evidence:** Stitched 2 x 2-tile windows (2136 px resized to 1068 px = 26.7 px/mm, frozen 'block' brief) read 35-61 counts per known-text gate window. But every window-census candidate at low counts failed at tile scale: a count-9 window read 0/0/0 letters by every reader on all 4 footprint tiles; three floor-count windows (5-6) read 0 letters on all 12 tiles; a 2-window cluster gave scattered non-agreeing reads (best pair 0).
- **Fix:** Use stitched windows (stride 1, overlapping) for the census, with a known-text gate window in the batch; send each window candidate's footprint tiles through phase 2 at 53.4 px/mm with the sigma2t brief and N0 from the same material before any claim.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-25-A11, #P4-OWN-SLOTW-RESULT; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census

### L289. Census positives just above the null threshold are signals, not readings
- **Trap:** Announcing census-positive windows that were never put through a phase-2 or extended test.
- **Evidence:** Every session of the largest extended re-read was audit-valid (18/18); maps built independently by two makers were byte-identical (16/16 and 15/15 duplicate pairs).
- **Fix:** Label census hits as census-level until a pre-registered extended test (upright vs rotated, null tiles, exact permutation) passes.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-30..2026-10-03 · **Sources:** survey:expmap_raw.json:fine-tuning; paris-4:gifted-bell-gavnl5:README.md, SUBMISSION.md

### L290. Stitched windows raised reader sensitivity but did not reach legibility on held-out text
- **Trap:** Expecting stitched 4 x 4 cm windows to rescue the legibility of 9 um maps (FL-3 stitched-window gate, held-out PHerc0139).
- **Evidence:** 3 of 16 windows read rows Y, max count (letters + marks) 4, against single tiles' 1 of 12 rows and 1 letter. The declared bar (count >= 5) was not met and was not changed.
- **Fix:** Going up a scale helped but did not reach legibility: the binding limit was the 9 um maps, not the display format.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (FL3-W1-GATE); logs/fl2/fl3w1_result_gate.json; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (FL-3 stitched-window gate)

### L291. Blind-reader output was suspended in favour of owner/orchestrator triage on FL-4
- **Trap:** Continuing LLM blind reads when the material itself is unvalidated.
- **Evidence:** Under OWNER-ORDER-FL4-B the LLM blind reads were suspended; FL-4 maps went to the owner and were triaged by the orchestrator, and later geometric findings (DECL-FL-4-A8) voided the maps.
- **Fix:** Validate geometry and a positive control before investing in reading; reading cannot rescue unvalidated material.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-03 · **Sources:** dominion:fl4t:README.md

### L292. Gate reader sensitivity on known text before a census
- **Trap:** Running a census where a null could mean the readers or the maps cannot show text.
- **Evidence:** Paris 4 verso-offset census: reader-sensitivity gate PASS on the known text column (counts 61 and 43) before 133 windows were read; own-model census: the known column showed text on 5 of 6 tiles.
- **Fix:** Include a known-text sensitivity gate in the same harness and declare its pass bar before reading targets.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-03 · **Sources:** paris-4:gifted-bell-gavnl5:README.md

### L293. An uncalibrated blind read is uninformative: hide known letters and no-ink strips among the targets
- **Trap:** Read #1: blind readers missed both hidden positives (max confidence 0.35; 1 of 6 positive reads letter-like); there were no hidden negatives and one control was downscaled without adjusting the stated glyph size. Read #2 reached AUC 0.875-0.900, but colour alone reaches 0.975 on the same control strips.
- **Evidence:** First blind read: readers missed the hidden PHerc0343 controls. Calibrated read: 3 readers, 29 coded strips = 8 control letter strips + 5 displaced no-ink strips + 16 tall PHerc0268 strips; readers separated letters from no-ink at AUC 0.875-0.900 (colour-only baseline 0.975; reader confidence vs strong-pixel fraction Spearman 0.878-0.918).
- **Fix:** Use hidden positives AND colour-matched hidden negatives in the SAME format, per-reader AUC, and a colour-only baseline before reading anything into the unknowns.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/FL_SEARCH.md; dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#17, results/blind_read/read1_uncalibrated_controls.json, results/blind_read/colour_baseline.json, docs/RESULTS.md#4

### L294. Report nothing from reads whose calibration failed
- **Trap:** Reads of the unknown PHerc0268 strips could be read as evidence either way.
- **Evidence:** RESULTS 4: reads of the unknown strips are not reported, whatever they showed, because the calibration showed colour response, not letter recognition.
- **Fix:** Fix in advance that unknown reads are reported only if the controls show letter recognition beyond a colour baseline.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/RESULTS.md#4

### L295. Readers are AI agents: say so and keep coarse ROC caveats
- **Trap:** Blind readers were Claude sub-agents, not papyrologists, and 13 control images give coarse ROC steps.
- **Evidence:** The three blind readers were Claude sub-agents limited to the coded image files, returning letter-like yes/no, letter-row yes/no and a 0-1 confidence; images were re-encoded identically (JPEG q 88), coded in a fixed hash order, and shown to each reader in a different order. Read #2 had 8 hidden positives and 5 hidden negatives, so each reader's AUC rests on 13 control images (0.875, 0.900, 0.900) (METHODS 8; RESULTS 4).
- **Fix:** Disclose reader type; use enough controls for a meaningful ROC; re-encode all images identically (JPEG q 88) and code them in a fixed hash order so format leaks nothing.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/METHODS.md#8, docs/RESULTS.md#4

### L296. Forms flagged by every reader can sit on known artifact zones: test them physically before any claim
- **Trap:** Promoting a form that all blind readers flagged to a letter candidate.
- **Evidence:** Two PHerc0268 forms were flagged by all 3 calibrated readers; both overlap blank-margin artifact zones. Pre-declared physical tests (before any data): depth stability r >= 0.5 at adjacent depths; face specificity (share >= 0.5, r(fwd,rev) < 0.3); >= 2 of 3 models at >= 2x their strip-wide fraction; +8 and -8 vox displaced copies <= 0.2x; margin-fill persistence r >= 0.6. Survival would make an ink candidate, not a legible letter. Details are withheld for prize review.
- **Fix:** Check every flagged form against the artifact map (edges, margins, seams) and run displaced/forward/fill/depth/model tests before naming it.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/FL_SEARCH.md

**Statistics and pre-registration (L297-L349).** Declarations, code hashes, nulls, bars and multiplicity. Many bars failed because nobody checked them against the reference object or the null was invariant to its own transform (L300, L301, L309, L325).

### L297. Declare before data, pin code by hash, and keep an append-only hash-chained log
- **Trap:** Editing scoring code between declaration and scoring.
- **Evidence:** METRIC-HASH-0 onward: every file used by a declared bar is sha256-listed; any change needs a new METRIC-HASH entry before next use; the D1 audit found one unhashed harness file (jobs.py) and hashed it. Also: RULES.md is append-only; each entry carries the sha256 of the previous one and `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m hercules.records.rules_append verify` recomputes the chain; METRIC-HASH entries list 'sha256 path' lines checkable with sha256sum -c; blind batches use commit A (keys, jobs, briefs) before any reader and commit B sealed. The research-log README sums it up: declaring bars before reading the data kept a long run of null results honest.
- **Fix:** Hash scorer, display builder, harness and crop pickers before use; record the hash in the decision log; let the auditor compare hashes.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:VERIFY.md, configs/prompt/hercules_master_v7.md, README.md, RULES.md#METRIC-HASH-0, #D1-VERDICT, #METRIC-HASH-17; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Append-only decision log integrity)

### L298. A 128-vox clearance from training traces excludes all papyrus; contamination is a same-papyrus question
- **Trap:** Excluding every pixel within 128 vox (3-D) of any base-training trace: adjacent windings lie 20-40 vox apart, so 100 % of w024, w047 and w053 was excluded and no window remained. A 128-vox clearance between test windows likewise covered 22-54 % of each labelled segment and left 1 window.
- **Evidence:** RCBANK-1 builder defect; HANDED-R3-VOID: only 1 window qualified at 256/128/64 px grids.
- **Fix:** Use a KD-tree same-papyrus test (>= 1000 vox^2 within 2 vox normal and 6 vox Euclidean) plus a 64 px in-plane halo; at 9 um the base model sees about +-8 vox of depth, so memorised ink lives on the same papyrus, not adjacent windings. Keep 128 vox only for submission pixels vs training patches.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#RCBANK-1, #DECL-READCAL-A2, #HANDED-R3-VOID, #DECL-HANDED-R3B

### L299. Pre-registration with defaults and forking limits keeps an AI-run programme honest
- **Trap:** Deciding bars after seeing data, re-running until something passes, or letting unresolved decisions drift.
- **Evidence:** Every decision declared before data with bars and a default (e.g. FAIL at 24 h past its date); K6: <= 4 candidate arms + 1 reference per decision and <= 3 decisions per sealed benchmark (J used for D1, D3); VOID runs re-declared once only; the log recorded many VOIDs and corrections openly.
- **Fix:** Declare hypothesis, data, metric code hash, bars, default and consequence before any deciding data; allow one re-declaration per VOID; count decisions per benchmark.
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-09-24 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-KILL, #DECL-D1, #C3-RUN1, #DECL-C3-R1

### L300. A gate bar above the reference's own score can never pass
- **Trap:** Writing an absolute AUC bar (>= 0.90) for a chain-validation gate without checking what the reference map scores on the same pixels.
- **Evidence:** GATE-E2E-0139 as written: our fp32 chain reproduces the organizer map (r 0.99999) but scores AUC 0.888 against labels - and the organizer's own map also scores 0.88798 there, so the 0.90 bar is unreachable; CHAIN VALID stayed blocked. The control was also not the declared window set (undefined 'team text-window overlaps'). Also: P4-N extension: seam residual 2.40 vox (p90 6.72); the official mesh scored 2.40 vox (p90 6.70) against its own continuation one row inside itself; the literal bar FAILED. Off-sheet fraction of a mesh tile was 22.3 % counted on every 4th vertex vs 37.5 % from a 40-sample estimate (about 2.3 standard errors apart).
- **Fix:** Before freezing a bar, measure the official or reference object on the same metric and set the bar relative to that baseline; size repairs from full counts, not 40-sample estimates.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-chain2um:logs/sib/chain2um/REPORT.md, logs/sib/chain2um/proposals/DECL-CHAIN-ORDER-proposal.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:CHANGELOG.md; dominion:sib-chain2um@1c4fb1444:logs/sib/chain2um/REPORT.md; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (2.4 um ink chain reproduction on CPU); dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#P4-N-RESULT, #DECL-P4-22; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (P4-N-RESULT); survey:expmap_raw.json:fine-tuning; dominion:sib-tracer:logs/sib/tracer/p4n/REPORT.md, logs/sib/tracer/ASK.md, logs/sib/tracer/p4-24/REPORT.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md#P4-N-RESULT; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census

### L301. Reproduce archived bar values under your written metric definition before declaring the bar
- **Trap:** C3 bars (forward AUC >= 0.987, reverse < 0.60) were copied from the archive but paired with a different AUC definition (blank = every valid label-0 pixel). Under that definition even the organizers' own team SV scores 0.9807, so the gate could never pass; the run was VOID.
- **Evidence:** Inside the organizers' supervision mask (hf native9 w040_supervision_mask; ink = 255, blank = 0 inside mask) the archive numbers reproduce to 3-4 decimals (team SV 0.99659/0.49633); with all label-0 pixels as blank: team SV 0.9807/0.4563, our render 0.9549/0.4254 with TTA. Also: Archive: PHerc1203 held-out r 0.964, PHerc0846A 0.946; ours, plain Pearson over whole 48x256x256 blocks including air and gaps, 0.879 and 0.844. The archive's '(-4, -4) px on one segment' for PHerc0009B was not reproduced on any CT-registered segment (all |d| < 2.1 px); a (+4.3, +4.3) px label-vs-map offset may be that number with the opposite sign (not verified).
- **Fix:** Record the exact metric definition (masking, filtering, block size) with every registration number, and re-derive archive claims before relying on them.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#C3-RUN1, #DECL-C3-R1; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (entry C3-RUN1), LEDGER.md (row C3 run 1); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (C3 gate, run 1 (9 um base chain fidelity, as first declared)); dominion:sib-regrescan:logs/sib/regrescan/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-reg0009b:logs/sib/reg0009b/REPORT.md

### L302. An empirical null by radius band needs a real centre: geometry-only centres fail on PHerc0139
- **Trap:** Same-radius-band null tiles were drawn around a geometry-only centre curve; on a non-circular scroll the band is ill-defined and yields almost nothing.
- **Evidence:** Null dry run on clean PHerc0139: pitch 20.875 vox along normals, but 0 of 89 candidate band tiles qualified (77 outside the +-10 % band, 12 within 192 vox of R): 4 tiles where >= 40 were needed, INSUFFICIENT. The centre curve's median normal-line miss distance was 326 vox and each segment spans about 500 vox of radius.
- **Fix:** Declare the centre source (for example the official 2.399 um umbilicus mapped to the 9.362 um volume) and the band definition before building nulls; never adjust post hoc.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-tribunal:logs/sib/tribunal/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-tribunal@a11610163:logs/sib/tribunal/real_trib2/null_dryrun/null_dryrun.json (null_set.status), logs/sib/tribunal/real_trib2/null_dryrun/null_dryrun.json (null_set.n_tiles), logs/sib/tribunal/real_trib2/null_dryrun/null_dryrun.json (centre_curve); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Tribunal: empirical-null dry run)

### L303. One whole-canvas map silently consumes every 'fresh' held-out crop of that segment
- **Trap:** Declaring a gate on a crop 'before any map of it exists' after an earlier run had mapped the organizer SV of the whole w040 canvas with the same recipe; the C2-NT gate on w040 was VOID and no w040 area remained unmapped.
- **Evidence:** C3-NT-VERDICT: numbers re-derived exactly (forward 0.99926, reverse 0.56528) but the earlier whole-canvas map already scored 0.99929/0.54503 on that crop; the orchestrator missed it.
- **Fix:** Keep a ledger of every map/render made (area, recipe) and have an auditor check freshness against ledger rows and file searches before declaring; move to a segment no model map has ever covered (w044 was used and passed).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#C3-NT-VERDICT, #DECL-C3-NT-R1, #C3-NT-R1-VERDICT; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:LEDGER.md (row C3-NT), logs/c3/audit_nt.json (field audit); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (C3-NT: no-TTA variant on the same segment)

### L304. Calibrate letter-size and line-spacing bars on known text before using them as gates
- **Trap:** Bars chosen from intuition (80 % of letters 2-4 mm, a pitch-CV bar) can fail genuine text.
- **Evidence:** On 68 official PHerc0139 label blobs only 75-78 % fall in 2-4 mm (median 2.5-3.1 mm), so B8 was revised to a median-only bar; known-text row pitch median 4.7 mm and only 58-68 % of known-text tiles meet the SG 11 pitch-CV bar. The 13 official PHerc0139 label sets hold only 4-25 isolated letters per segment (68 in total), too sparse for line spacing.
- **Fix:** Measure each geometric bar's pass rate on known-text material first and record that rate as the bar's expected sensitivity; use dense reference maps, not sparse human labels, for row statistics.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-sg:logs/sib/sg/REPORT.md, logs/sib/sg/label_survey_0139.json; dominion:sib-sg@20397b831:logs/sib/sg/REPORT.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:CHANGELOG.md (2026-09-25 19:2x sibling harvest); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Submission gate as tested code)

### L305. Report every pre-specified fit that was checked, and commit the fit before the check
- **Trap:** A pipeline that runs fit -> refit -> held-out check as one command checks a fit that was never committed, and invites picking the better-scoring iteration afterwards.
