- **Evidence:** regrescan PHerc0846A: the first check used refit iteration 2 (not committed before the check); the orchestrator then specified committed iteration 1, checked once on the same 16 pre-fixed patches; both are reported (median r 0.8439 and 0.8437, both FAIL vs 0.85), neither chosen by outcome.
- **Fix:** Split fit and check into separate commands, push the fit's sha256 before any held-out read, and report every checked iteration.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-regrescan:logs/sib/regrescan/REPORT.md, logs/sib/regrescan/ASK.md; dominion:sib-regrescan@da0a72fbb:logs/sib/regrescan/REPORT.md; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (PHerc0846A 9.362 <-> 2.403 um CT affine (regrescan))

### L306. An independent verifier that recomputes the null draw and every null image byte for byte makes a phase-2 result auditable
- **Trap:** Trusting a phase-2 re-read result that nobody recomputed independently.
- **Evidence:** A phase-2 re-read of census positives on official predictions (3 fresh readers per candidate, sessions of up to 4 candidates, 4 rotated null tiles and 1 positive control per session) was re-verified by an independent verifier, including byte-exact recomputation of the null draw and of every null image (15/15 checks). The outcome is withheld for prize review.
- **Fix:** An independent verifier that recomputes the null draw and every null image byte for byte makes a phase-2 result auditable.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-10-03 (family period) · **Sources:** dominion:sib-rh-e2:README.md; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census

### L307. When a declared model fails, a replacement is admissible only if it is chosen on old data, frozen, and checked on fresh pre-registered material
- **Trap:** Replacing a failed registration model with one tuned on the new data (PHerc0841, after the affine failed).
- **Evidence:** A smooth non-affine field, chosen by leave-one-out on old patches only and frozen before new data (REG-0841-NA), passed every pre-registered bar on 16 fresh patches: held-out median r 0.863 (min 0.563; bar >= 0.85), RMS residual 0.977 vox (max 1.47; bar <= 1.5), shifted control median drop 0.695 (15/16 clear). It also showed the organizer's canvas mapping is off by about 1.2 voxels (median), negligible at letter-matching tolerances.
- **Fix:** Admit a replacement only if it is chosen on old data, frozen, and checked on fresh pre-registered material; disclose the deviation.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (REG-0841-NA); logs/sib/reg0841na/reg0841na_summary.json (sha256 9d6779bf...), RULES.md (REG-0841-NA); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (PHerc0841 registration, non-affine model (REG-0841-NA))

### L308. Small sealed sets cap statistical power: J seal S' = 20 forced p_max < 0.005
- **Trap:** Planning a decision on 5 windows of unseen-scroll reference text without checking expected seal size.
- **Evidence:** J picker on 0841 J1-J5: 15 named, 3 firm at 1/2 scale; with key sheet + fable sealers S' = 20 (9 firm) vs archive S = 43 (11 firm). No 2 x 2 cm 0841 area outside the T shell exists (<= 1.52 cm^2 per segment), so the seal could not be enlarged.
- **Fix:** Estimate seal size with a picker before declaring; plan S' >= 30 material or accept stricter p bars.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#JPICK-1, #SEAL-J-D1, #DECL-D1-A3

### L309. A rot-90 null cannot test a max-over-orientations statistic
- **Trap:** Declaring a row-periodicity score S_row as the maximum over all orientations (normalised by the median over orientations) and using a 90-degree-rotated copy as the null. A 90-degree rotation only permutes the orientation grid, so S_row(rot90) = S_row and the null is the data itself; a gate requiring >=30 % of known-text tiles above the null p99 can never pass.
- **Evidence:** Unit test: relative difference < 1e-3 on synthetic tiles. Real gates: M1 2/86 (2.3 %), M2 2/32 (6.3 %) against a 30 % bar; control-vs-rot-90 AUC 0.500 / 0.497. On synthetic tiles with obvious planted rows the declared rule passed 0/6 (AUC 0.507) while an orientation-anchored variant passed 6/6 (AUC 0.993).
- **Fix:** Before declaring any null, check that the statistic is not invariant to the transform that defines the null, and run the full gate on synthetic positives. For row structure, anchor the orientation to the control strip's median theta* (+-10 deg) so rotation moves real rows out of the window.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-struct:README.md, logs/sib/p4-struct/REPORT.md, logs/sib/p4-struct/ASK.md, logs/sib/p4-struct/synthetic_smoke.json; dominion:sib-p4-struct@5e55f94f5:logs/sib/p4-struct/STATUS.md, logs/sib/p4-struct/REPORT.md; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-pigments, paris4-census

### L310. Measure a calibration rule's false-pass rate on layer-free profiles before trusting a pass
- **Trap:** An ink-depth calibration rule (fraction of voxels above T_hi vs depth offset; pass if peak excess > 3 robust SD within +-100 um) can pass on profiles with no ink layer, and individual control tiles 'pass' at scattered depths.
- **Evidence:** 1.129 um known-text control (826 of 960 chunks, T_hi 233): peak excess z = 1.12 < 3, STOP. Per-tile peak offsets median -6.8 um, p10 -114.7 um, p90 +102.5 um; 9 of 24 tiles would pass individually, in line with the rule's measured false-pass rate of 0.17 on flat layer-free profiles. 27 unit tests pass. Also: The declared rule passed 25/100 i.i.d.-noise sheets (family-wise error of a max over 109 offsets) and 10/10 no-ink sheet+gap profiles (the sheet body itself becomes a 'peak' when gaps set the median). Its positive test passed (a 15 um layer with 2.4 um PSF located within 2.4 um, 21/21).
- **Fix:** Before using a depth rule as a gate, simulate layer-free profiles and report the false-pass rate; require a common depth across tiles, not per-tile optima. Scattered per-tile optima (~+-100 um) indicate the real surface wanders relative to the mesh, so constant-offset slabs mix ink with interior or air.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-tiles-b:README.md, logs/sib/p4-tiles-b/l3e/REPORT.md, logs/sib/p4-tiles-b/l3e/calib_1129.json; dominion:sib-p4-depth@c6c551185:logs/sib/p4-depth/calib.json; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md#P4-L3-CALIB-RESULT; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census; dominion:sib-p4-depth:README.md, logs/sib/p4-depth/ASK.md, logs/sib/p4-depth/specificity/README.md

### L311. When a fallback rule exists, declare it before the primary rule is run
- **Trap:** Designing a new geometric rule after the declared one fails on target data.
- **Evidence:** Facing-surface geometry for the offset channel: the declared per-vertex rule failed on every tile (137 to over 27,000 self-intersections), the pre-declared regularised rule was rejected on controls (53-65 % of vertices vs 80 % required), and only the pre-declared fallback (adjacent official winding within 250 um) passed (18/36 control, 32/54 target tiles).
- **Fix:** Declare primary, regularised and fallback rules together, each with control-first gates, so a failure does not invite post-hoc design.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md (P4-26-FACING-GEOMETRY-RESULT); dominion:sib-p4-core@11b9c7d20:logs/sib/p4-core/STATUS.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md#P4-26-FACING-GEOMETRY-RESULT; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census

### L312. When ink depth is uncertain, sweep the declared offsets with a multiplicity-corrected bar instead of trusting the mesh
- **Trap:** Trusting the mesh surface as the ink depth when both depth calibrations failed to find an ink layer (dense-pigment screen, Paris 4).
- **Evidence:** The declared fallback ran the unchanged screen at 9 offsets (-60 to +60 um): 0 DENSE-HOTSPOT tiles on E2 (2.4 um, 160 tiles) and on E1 (60 tiles) at every offset, and no target-region tile crossed the multiplicity-corrected bar at any depth. The sweep was split across workers; the merged screen files were verified by sha256 against the branch (screen_dstar_E2.json 3b7c8ff0..., screen_dstar_E1.json a11e5825...).
- **Fix:** Sweep the declared offsets with a multiplicity-corrected bar instead of trusting the mesh; split a sweep across workers only with merge checks (no duplicates, offset-0 records equal to the original run).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md (P4-F-SWEEP-RESULT); dominion:sib-p4-highz@68030b270:RULES.md (P4-F-SWEEP-RESULT); logs/sib/p4-highz/screen_dstar_E2.json, RULES.md (P4-F-SWEEP-RESULT); logs/sib/p4-highz/screen_dstar_E1.json, logs/sib/p4-highz/REPORT.md (Addendum A3, panel_ext.json); dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md#P4-F-SWEEP-RESULT; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census

### L313. A strong upright-versus-rotated contrast shows orientation dependence, not necessarily writing
- **Trap:** Reading a strong upright-versus-rotated contrast as writing (extended confirmation test of a single phase-2 tile on official 2.4 um predictions).
- **Evidence:** All 18 sessions valid. Upright reads named 5-7 letters (best-pair triples 5, 5, 5); the rotated self-null named 0-1 (triples 1, 0, 0; permutation p 5e-5). The null-tile maximum triple over 48 tiles was 7, so the tile was not confirmed (L321). Verdict: failed.
- **Fix:** Treat an upright-versus-rotated contrast as orientation dependence only: a bright fibre band or fold behaves the same way. A large null of real tiles, including rotated text, is what stops such features from passing.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:logs/p4/ext1_score.json; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census

### L314. Placing dependent channels behind their gates avoided reads on displays already shown to be uninformative
- **Trap:** Running depth-dependent displays (verso face, title-scale thin-slab windows) before a calibrated ink depth or a passing known-text gate exists.
- **Evidence:** These reads were declared to run only after a calibrated ink depth d* existed or a thin-slab display passed its known-text gate. The calibration stopped with no d*, so P4-V (the verso at -d*) and the P4-W windows at L3 never ran; 70/70 target-zone and 56/56 control thin-slab windows were built but never read.
- **Fix:** Place dependent channels behind their gates; it avoided reads on displays already shown to be uninformative.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-l2@52d6c9102:logs/sib/p4-l2/STATUS.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md#P4-L3-CALIB-RESULT; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census

### L315. Pre-register a second attempt for registrations
- **Trap:** Re-running a failing registration with tweaks until it passes.
- **Evidence:** KTLB-4P registration 9.362 <-> 2.215 um on fragment PHerc0500P2 failed attempt 1 (held-out median r 0.834) and passed its pre-registered attempt 2 (0.929).
- **Fix:** Declare the retry and its bar before attempt 1 runs, and report both attempts.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-handed:logs/sib/ktlb4p-prep/REPORT.md, README.md

### L316. Verify frozen hashes before scoring, and use a deterministic resumable scorer so split work can overlap safely
- **Trap:** Splitting a long scoring job across containers without a way to prove each one ran the frozen code, or with a scorer that recomputes finished tiles.
- **Evidence:** CU sub-lane c verified all 6 sha256 values in params_freeze.json (0 mismatches) and resumed E2 after the parent's 29 scored tiles; the scorer skips finished tiles and is deterministic, so overlap with the parent was harmless (E2 160/160 and C2 101 tiles scored in one session).
- **Fix:** Ship a params_freeze.json with sha256 of every parameter and code file; each worker verifies it and stops on any mismatch; scorers write per-tile records and skip existing ones.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-pig-cu-c:README.md, logs/sib/p4-pig-cu-c/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4-pig-cu:logs/sib/p4-pig-cu/SUBSIBS.md

### L317. Allowed design iteration happens on controls only and is disclosed
- **Trap:** Swapping detector versions after looking at target data, or hiding a design change made after a pilot.
- **Evidence:** Gold: detector v1 was replaced by the thin-layer ridge v2 after a single control pilot injection showed v1 insensitive (disclosed in detector_core.json); params.json was frozen from the controls only (sha256 84ab70b9...) before any title-strip number. CU: the grain detector was frozen (params_freeze.json) after control-only checks (permutation null 0 on 7 control tiles; injected Egyptian-blue letter ~1000-1600 vs blank 0-83).
- **Fix:** Iterate freely on control material, then freeze params and code with sha256 before the first target number, and list each pre-freeze change in the record.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-pig-gold:logs/sib/p4-pig-gold/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-p4-pig-cu:logs/sib/p4-pig-cu/STATUS.md

### L318. Cut title search windows by physical column slots measured from layout, not tile ranges fixed in advance
- **Trap:** Fixing title search windows as tile-column ranges before the column layout was measured, which split the most probable slot between two hypotheses.
- **Evidence:** The red team found the register's windows mis-cut relative to the measured column pitch (~8 cm = 4 tiles) and a 91 % 'beside the last column' prior with 2.5-10 cm offsets; it also found the register summing non-exclusive locations as exclusive and double-counting the 91 % prior. Its corrections fed the window order of DECL-P4-17-A1.
- **Fix:** Measure the column layout first (validated pitch on known text), then define slots; keep location hypotheses non-exclusive in the arithmetic.
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-titulus:README.md, logs/sib/p4-titulus/REDTEAM.md

### L319. The SG 7 copy test flags genuine letters by chance at low n_eff
- **Trap:** A copy test (letter crop vs training-label patches over 24 rotations, any NCC >= 0.8 is a copy) is treated as a clean veto, but on smooth maps chance correlations exceed the bar.
- **Evidence:** Synthetic null on independent smoothed fields: every crop falsely flagged at n_eff <= 13, none at n_eff >= 30; the chance maximum grows with patch count (0.691 -> 0.743 from 100 to 1000 patches at n_eff 31).
- **Fix:** Report n_eff_median with every copy test, run the empirical null on the real patch set before the gate, and treat a flag at low n_eff as uninformative rather than as proof of copying.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-sg:logs/sib/sg/REPORT.md, logs/sib/sg/copytest_null.json

### L320. Never round a pre-registered threshold, and evaluate every condition
- **Trap:** A pre-registered rule MIN_REF_NCC = p1 - 3(1 - p1) produced 0.9998, which rounded to 1.000 and would have failed every clean record; short-circuited checks also hid secondary failing reasons.
- **Evidence:** REAL-TRIB-1 clean minimum NCC 0.999944 vs unrounded threshold 0.999777 (12/12 clean pass); the rounded rule was reported as a defect and not used. Raising MIN_REF_NCC above the 0.74-0.85 NCC of real off-by-one faults makes those faults read 'unverifiable', losing attribution to the slice check (0/12 by slice alone).
- **Fix:** Store thresholds unrounded, pass them in explicitly, have every check list all failing reasons, and keep reference-NCC floors below the NCC that genuine faults produce.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-tribunal:logs/sib/tribunal/REPORT.md

### L321. A 4-tile null manufactures leads; a rotated self-null plus >= 40 null tiles kills them
- **Trap:** Accepting a candidate that beats the maximum of only 4 null tiles at the minimum margin.
- **Evidence:** Title-search phase 2: a candidate met the bar (best pair 5 vs N0 max 4; auditor: WEAK). Extended test: 48 rotated null tiles (triple scores max 7, P99 7) -> median candidate triple 5 < 7: NOT confirmed, although upright vs rotated self-null differed strongly (p 5e-5; one row, y std 0.12-0.14 mm). Both 7-scoring null tiles were rotated labelled-adjacent text.
- **Fix:** Require >= 40 matched null tiles and agreed - P99 >= 10 (SG 1c spirit); a reproducible upright-only feature can be a fibre band or fold, so U-vs-rot90 alone is not evidence of writing; readers of one model family are not independent.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-3, #P4-B-PHASE2-RESULT, #P4-C-RESULT

### L322. Null tiles must come from the same material as the candidates
- **Trap:** Phase-2/extended-test builders drew null tiles from every census key, including raw-CT batches where readers name nothing, which would make the null artificially empty and lower the bar.
- **Evidence:** Defect found before any affected read; fixed with an explicit pool-batch list; regression reproduced earlier selections exactly.
- **Fix:** Pass explicit same-material pool batches to every null draw; never pool nulls across displays or materials.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#METRIC-HASH-32

### L323. Treat each display/checkpoint as its own material with its own known-text gate and null
- **Trap:** Pooling candidates across several displays of one volume or several iterations of one model, or interpreting a channel that cannot see known text.
- **Evidence:** Declared for L2, L2S, L3 displays and up to 6 PHerc.1667 iterations; channels failing their known-text gate (>= 30 % of non-blank known-text tiles rows Y with >= 5 letters) were recorded 'uninformative', not 'absent'.
- **Fix:** Gate first on known-text tiles of the same strip; disclose multiplicity; a candidate counts only if confirmed in its own material.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-12, #DECL-P4-12-A2, #DECL-P4-14-A1, #P4-L2-CENSUS-RESULT

### L324. Run a peak-detection threshold on the dense known-text control before declaring it
- **Trap:** A line-structure test (count text lines from peak outliers in 0.5 mm-binned prediction profiles) was declared with a threshold that sat above the profile maxima of dense body text, so it detected 0 lines on the body-text reference groups.
- **Evidence:** DECL-P4-19 validity control: threshold/profile-maximum ratios 1.081 and 1.065 in the two body-text groups, 0 lines detected, although both were strongly periodic (autocorrelation pitch 6.61 and 6.41 mm). Verdict INVALID; nothing concluded and the rule was not re-run after target numbers were known.
- **Fix:** Dry-run every detection threshold on the control groups (dense periodic profiles) before declaration; keep a validity control that must look body-like before any target decision; use autocorrelation pitch rather than peak outliers for dense text.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-tiles-a:README.md, logs/sib/p4-tiles-a/p419_profile.json; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md#P4-19-RESULT; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#P4-19-RESULT, #DECL-P4-19

### L325. Rotation-closed kernels and rotation-invariant tile scores make the rot-90 null an implementation check, not a null
- **Trap:** Using a rot-90 copy as the false-positive null for a detector whose kernel set is closed under 90-degree rotation (4-orientation stroke filter) or whose tile score is rotation-invariant (gold ridge detector). The 'null' reproduces the score exactly and adds no independent sample.
- **Evidence:** FE detector: rot-90 null max |z| difference 0.0 on both voxel families; theta is effectively p99 of the control tiles. The FE-e2 sub-lane flagged the same (rot-90 identical to z on every tile). Gold: the tile-level rot-90 null equals the unrotated control by construction. Also: p4-l2: rotating a tile with its cell lattice leaves the cell statistic unchanged, so the rot-90 flagged rate equals the overall flagged rate and a detector with high text recall must fail it. p4-highz recomputed the rot-90 null on all 455 tiles: radial statistics identical, directional peaks swapped.
- **Fix:** Treat a known-text control strip (and a virtual-glyph false-positive test on uninjected patches) as the discriminating null; report the rot-90 run only as a code sanity check.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-pig-fe:logs/sib/p4-pig-fe/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-p4-pig-fe-e2:README.md; dominion:sib-p4-pig-gold:logs/sib/p4-pig-gold/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-p4-l2:logs/sib/p4-l2/ASK.md; dominion:sib-p4-highz:logs/sib/p4-highz/REPORT.md

### L326. Pre-register a title-versus-body-text layout table before measuring
- **Trap:** Deciding after the fact whether a confirmed text-like block is a title.
- **Evidence:** A decision table was pinned by hash before any profile number: (a) text column W 5.5-7.0 cm, intercolumn 1.3-2.2 cm (or 8.8-10.8 with one invisible column), pitch 7.0-8.8 or 14.0-17.7 cm, line pitch 6.0-6.3 mm, left-aligned; (b) initial-title block W 2-5.5 cm, inward gap 9-14 cm (up to 26), open blank outward, 2-6 centred lines at 6-9.5 mm; rows scored -1/0/+1, sum >= +3 favours (b), <= -3 favours (a). Applied mechanically to the withheld candidates (details withheld for prize review), it kept the project from filing on wishful reading.
- **Fix:** Keep the layout test descriptive (it cannot make or break a candidate) but pre-register it; state that a pinned conditional probability assuming a blank surround is invalid when the surround is text-rich.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27..2026-10-03 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#METRIC-HASH-42, #DECL-P4-25-A13, logs/owner/AUDIT_2026-09-30.md; paris-4:gifted-bell-gavnl5:README.md, SUBMISSION.md; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census

### L327. Applying the candidate rule regardless of the gate adds chances; the phase-2 null is what controls them, and this was disclosed in advance
- **Trap:** Applying the candidate rule on strips whose internal gate failed (official-prediction census of three further Paris 4 strips).
- **Evidence:** The three strips gave positive rates of 1.4-6.1 % against a 20 % internal gate on each: every strip failed, so the column locator never ran. The candidate rule still produced 20 phase-2 candidates, as disclosed in advance.
- **Fix:** Applying the candidate rule regardless of the gate adds chances; disclose it in advance and let the phase-2 null control them.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-rh-e2:README.md; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census

### L328. Split a frozen screen across workers with a tile filter only, and check overlap records exactly
- **Trap:** Letting each worker re-implement or re-threshold a shared screen.
- **Evidence:** hzw1/hzw2 ran the parent's stage_off.py unchanged at a pinned commit with the frozen T_hi threshold; wrappers only filtered tiles to a column block. hzw1's offset-0 records equalled the parent's stage_b records exactly (40/40); hzw2's record keys matched the control file. The pooled 160-tile screen was then aggregated by the parent against a Bonferroni bar from 171 control tiles.
- **Fix:** Distribute frozen code by commit, filter work by tile only, and verify one shared slice (offset 0) byte-for-byte against the parent.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-hzw1:logs/sib/hzw1/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-hzw2:README.md

### L329. Freeze and hash the training recipe before the first training step
- **Trap:** Choosing architecture, patch rules, seeds or fold lists after seeing training curves or maps, which makes held-out numbers unauditable.
- **Evidence:** RECIPE.md was frozen at commit 6b5bdc5 with sha256 377784c2bd8dd8617f38ae0e054fbe37684004f6e0d105852e84e16c16a6dfb8 before any training step (METRIC-HASH-45); it lists code sha256, seeds (20260927/28/29), fold groups (77/76/76 tiles), the NULL derangement (n 4000, 0 fixed points) and the held-out tile lists. A later implementation fix was recorded as a separate amendment with old and new train.py sha256.
- **Fix:** Draft the recipe with everything label-independent fixed, fill only build-produced counts/hashes, push RECIPE.md + .sha256 before training, and record every later code change as a hashed amendment.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-own-lead:logs/sib/own-lead/p4own/RECIPE.md, logs/sib/own-lead/p4own/RECIPE_A1.md

### L330. Contiguous folds without a spatial buffer can make held-out AUCs optimistic
- **Trap:** Reading fold AUCs as fully independent when training and held-out groups are adjacent windings.
- **Evidence:** The 229 certified tiles were cut into 3 contiguous groups; windows straddling groups were excluded, but no buffer separated the groups. The recipe disclosed that adjacent windings may make the F AUCs optimistic. Holding out the densest group left F2 only 1230 training patches (about 33 passes) against 3365 (F1) and 3359 (F3), yet its AUC (0.9415) matched.
- **Fix:** Disclose fold geometry at freeze; where possible add a spatial buffer between folds, and back the folds with an independent check (here a separate never-trained zone and a blind legibility gate).
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-own-lead:logs/sib/own-lead/p4own/RECIPE.md

### L331. Define declared terms operationally and check them on the data's distribution
- **Trap:** Freezing an interpretation of an undefined declared term ('gap depths') that turns out to be degenerate on real data.
- **Evidence:** p4-depth defined gap offsets as slices whose pooled median voxel < T_mid (93); on real data the pooled median was below 93 at all 109 slices (max 91), so every slice was 'gap' and the comparison was uninformative.
- **Fix:** Write declarations with operational definitions and sanity-check them on the control distribution before the run; store per-slice histograms so an amended rule can be recomputed without new reads (p4-depth did).
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-depth:logs/sib/p4-depth/STATUS.md, logs/sib/p4-depth/ASK.md

### L332. i.i.d. synthetic sheets are far noisier than real papyrus in max-projections
- **Trap:** Building a synthetic-specificity test from voxels drawn independently from empirical class histograms.
- **Evidence:** Every synthetic no-ink cell was flagged (100 %) by both L4 faces because the max over 11 slices of i.i.d. voxels is inflated; the verdict rested on sensitivity alone (recall 0.074 / 0.033 vs 0.90).
- **Fix:** Use a spatially correlated generator, e.g. real control air/interior patches reshuffled in blocks, for synthetic specificity bars.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-l2:logs/sib/p4-l2/ASK.md, logs/sib/p4-l2/PREGATE_L4.json

### L333. Fence the target region at the byte level until the method is hash-frozen; apply it exactly once
- **Trap:** Designing a composition method while target-region bytes are reachable, or re-applying a method with new settings after seeing target numbers.
- **Evidence:** Dual-energy lane: geometry only for the title strip, no 137 keV byte fetched until the orchestrator recorded the method hash (METRIC-HASH-40 = sha256 93d04a4d... of DUAL_FREEZE.md); the bbox fence was replaced (A-1) before any 137 keV byte; the application verified all 15 frozen tool hashes, added only apply.py (pushed before any number), and was declared 'one run only; a crash is resumed, never rerun with other settings'.
- **Fix:** Design and validate only on a control; hash the frozen method into the decision log before any target byte is read; write an apply script before running it; resume crashes from cache rather than re-running with changes.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-purple-de:README.md, logs/sib/p4-purple/de/APPLY.md; dominion:sib-p4-purple:logs/sib/p4-purple/STATUS.md

### L334. In the extended test the rotated-self arm, not N0, is the strict control
- **Trap:** Relying on N0 tiles drawn from mostly blank material to confirm a candidate.
- **Evidence:** Extended-test design: U vs R = rot90(U), 18 sessions (9 U, 9 R), 8 N0 per session, 48 N0, 1 positive control per session, exact permutation p over 48,620 labelings (or 20,000 permutations, minimum p 5e-5). In one batch 46-48 of 48 N0 tiles had census < 5 letters, so criterion (i) was mostly a comparison against rotated blanks.
- **Fix:** Keep the U-vs-R agreement criterion; do not exclude text-like tiles from N0 (conservative); draw N0 only from the same material.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-25-A2

### L335. Check that an interim futility rule can actually fire
- **Trap:** Declaring an early-stop rule that is arithmetically unreachable.
- **Evidence:** With 24 tiles per fold, the declared futility stop could never trigger: after 2 folds (Y + 24) >= 0.3 x 72 = 21.6 for every Y >= 0, so G1 needed all three folds anyway. Synthetic tally tests: 22/72 PASS, 21/72 FAIL, 0/24 and 0/48 PENDING.
- **Fix:** Evaluate interim rules on synthetic counts before pinning; disclose when a rule is inert.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#METRIC-HASH-49, #DECL-P4-23-A1

### L336. A NULL control only counts if it actually runs: assign it to whoever can run it
- **Trap:** Delegating the hallucination/chance control to a worker that may be blocked, leaving positive arms without a control.
- **Evidence:** The dedicated NULL worker was blocked; own-lead ran the label-deranged NULL arm itself (2500 steps) and it scored held-out pixel AUC 0.4972 / 0.5074 / 0.5240 on the F1/F2/F3 pixels, chance level as required.
- **Fix:** Treat the NULL arm as critical path; if its worker is blocked, the lead runs it before any target map is interpreted.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-28 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-own-null:README.md; dominion:sib-own-lead:README.md

### L337. In text-rich regions, cap window candidates by footprint size
- **Trap:** Without a size rule every body-text column in a non-blank search region becomes a 'title candidate', each costing about 21 reader sessions plus maps.
- **Evidence:** In the first outward own-model search 12 of 27 targeted tiles read as rows; the adopted rule (8-connected clusters of positive windows, tile footprint <= 3 x 3 tiles = 6 x 6 cm, at most 3 candidates by maximum count) turned column-sized clusters (footprints larger than 3 x 3 tiles) into reported context instead of candidates.
- **Fix:** Pre-register the footprint cap (tools/p4/win_candidates.py, synthetic unit test: a planted 3x3 block survives, a 5-row column is dropped) before the window census.
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-25-A11-A1, logs/owner/AUDIT_2026-09-30.md

### L338. A positive-control gate must be physically able to meet the bar
- **Trap:** Choosing gate material on which the criterion cannot be met even with perfect sensitivity.
- **Evidence:** The held-out PHerc0139 title segment is only 1.67 cm tall, so the unchanged 2 x 2 cm tiler kept 0 cells; a 2 cm-wide strip of a title line holds fewer than 10 letters, so the >= 10-letter criterion was impossible there.
- **Fix:** Choose gate segments by geometry and expected letter count, and confirm they are not in the model's training list (here: not among the official ink_9um training segments).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-FL-2-E2

### L339. Without a valid surface and a declared bar, visual triage of ink maps can only report a null
- **Trap:** Visually triaging ink maps without a validated surface or a declared bar (ink_9um on normal-grid PHerc0268 patches, three winding bands).
- **Evidence:** 16 own normal-grid patches on three windings gave uniform-speckle maps and 0 candidates. The render centre layers showed fibres radiating from the seed, so the surfaces were not flat on one sheet and the null carries no weight.
- **Fix:** Validate the surface and declare a bar first; otherwise visual triage can only report a weightless null.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-02..2026-10-03 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (FL6-RESULT), RULES.md (FL6-RESULT; DECL-FL-6 item 1); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (ink_9um on normal-grid PHerc0268 patches (three winding bands))

### L340. Declare the decision rule for an agreement statistic before computing it; otherwise the number cannot be acted on
- **Trap:** Computing a two-model agreement statistic without a declared decision rule (Grand Prize model on the largest PHerc1203 organizer sheets).
- **Evidence:** Only 2 of 5 planned sheets finished before the deadline (i16, i17 and i19 did not). Agreement with ink_9um was recorded against rotation/flip controls, but no agreement threshold had been declared, and no candidate was drawn from either model. Verdict: inconclusive.
- **Fix:** Declare the decision rule for an agreement statistic before computing it; otherwise the number cannot be acted on.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-03 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (FL6-GP-RESULT); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Grand Prize model on the largest PHerc1203 organizer sheets)

### L341. Use a circular-shift null with equal n
- **Trap:** Non-wrapped column shifts drop pixels, so every shift has a different n and neighbouring shifts are correlated; the null was too wide and gave p = 0.09.
- **Evidence:** Private record; stripqc.seam.circular_null_r and its test (S5: corrected p about 0.01-0.03).
- **Fix:** Use circular shifts over the full sample (equal n) and report the effective number of independent shifts.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-09..2026-10-14 (approx.) · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#7, docs/SUPERSEDED_CLAIMS.md#S5

### L342. State exactly which data a "before any data" declaration precedes
- **Trap:** The declaration of the PHerc0268 margin-fill test was labelled "before any data" but quoted exploratory control results that had already been computed.
- **Evidence:** Private record; SUPERSEDED_CLAIMS S14. DECL-FL-STRIP (docs/prereg/) quotes no control numbers.
- **Fix:** State exactly which data a "before any data" declaration precedes; label every non-declared analysis as exploratory.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-09..2026-10-14 (approx.) · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#19, docs/SUPERSEDED_CLAIMS.md#S14

### L343. Freeze the held-out set and the evaluation code before comparing models
- **Trap:** Comparing AUCs computed on different crop sets or with different inference semantics.
- **Evidence:** The same dense_native weights scored AUC 0.698 on 600 isolated 64-px crops but 0.760 by full-map inference on the same held-out shard; rebuilding the held-out shard moved the master model from 0.619/0.201 to 0.576/0.164.
- **Fix:** Hash the held-out shard and the evaluation script; report every model under identical semantics.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#E2E-1-RESULT, #FL7-A1-RESULT

### L344. Declare the candidate rule and mandatory false-positive controls before any search data
- **Trap:** Defining what counts as a letter candidate after looking at maps.
- **Evidence:** FL_SEARCH protocol: thresholds frozen on validation pairs first; mechanical ranking; a patch is a CANDIDATE only if >= 2 of 3 independent readers report >= 10 letter-like marks in rows parallel to the fibres, on ON_SHEET tiles, persisting across d = 0..+2 and three models; mandatory controls: +8-vox displaced copy (marks must vanish), forward direction, a held-out region of the same surface. Nothing is published before the prize team's review.
- **Fix:** Copy this structure: frozen gate, fixed display scale, mechanical ranking, blind readers, three controls, then claim.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/FL_SEARCH.md

### L345. Natural experiment: compare column classes inside the same strip
- **Trap:** Edge bands could be physical or artifact; a pooled comparison cannot tell.
- **Evidence:** RESULTS 3: ink proxy 0.163 vs 0.049 (260 px strips, higher with the 30-row margin in 24/29) and 0.190 vs 0.029 (400 px, 6/7); patch-share model r = 0.61 with bands peaking at rows 71 and 183.
- **Fix:** Exploit within-strip variation of the confound (30-row vs 10-row blank top margin) at fixed render rows, then confirm with an intervention (the fill test).
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/RESULTS.md#3, docs/METHODS.md#7

### L346. Bootstrap letters, not pixels
- **Trap:** Pixel counts run to hundreds of thousands but neighbouring pixels are not independent; pixel-level CIs would be far too narrow.
- **Evidence:** RESULTS 1: recall CIs from a 13-letter cluster bootstrap, 2 000 replicates, seed 0; 13 letters settle neither the 0.5 nor the 0.7 bar for F13 or Z20.
- **Fix:** Resample the independent units (letters, strips) and report that CIs exclude strip-placement variability.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/RESULTS.md#1, docs/METHODS.md#6

### L347. Check letter-box registration robustness
- **Trap:** Scoring against letter boxes could depend on a one-node registration error.
- **Evidence:** Moving every box +-20 px (one node) in x and y, 9 positions, changed no decision (results/control_strips_rerun/box_shift_check.json).
- **Fix:** Shift ground-truth boxes by one node in each direction and confirm decisions are unchanged.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** dominion:main:results/control_strips_rerun/box_shift_check.json, docs/METHODS.md#6

### L348. Pre-register decision bars and label exploratory arms; it is what exposed the strip artifact
- **Trap:** Deciding after seeing the data whether the mass-run strips 'see ink'.
- **Evidence:** DECL-FL-STRIP fixed before any result: Z13 'sees ink' only if pooled recall >= 0.5, E >= 5 and r >= 0.6 (result 0.39 / 15 / 0.79: does not); Z20 the same (0.63 / 18 / 0.89: narrowly); padding fixes only if recall >= 0.7 (0.52: no); no-ink arm D8 f_in <= 0.2x Z13 (0.3 %: works). Arms added later (AUC, matched-rate recall, fill, extrapolated padding) are marked exploratory.
- **Fix:** Write arms, metrics and thresholds into a DECL file and commit it before running; push every arm whatever the outcome.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:poc/ctrl343_strips/DECL.md, poc/ctrl343_strips/eval.out; pherc0268:9c80b1f:commit-message

### L349. List superseded claims explicitly, the same day
- **Trap:** Letting earlier statements stand once new controls change their meaning.
- **Evidence:** In one day the FL record superseded four claims: 'every strip is too short to hold a letter row' (refuted for the 16 tall strips), 'seam p = 0.09' (understated), 'the bands are a model artifact' (now measured), 'the 16 tall strips are an informative negative' (overstated).
- **Fix:** Keep a 'superseded claims' list in the result document and cite the replacing measurement.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/FL_SEARCH.md

## Part 3. Lessons: agents, process, compute and tools

**Agents and process (L350-L401).** Running an AI orchestrator with a fleet of sibling sessions: permissions, handovers, owner orders, delegation, verification of claims and submission hygiene.

### L350. Never work around safety or permission blocks
- **Trap:** Sibling sessions blocked by their own safety checks (tile builder start, licensed mesh download, one checkpoint's inference) while the programme is under time pressure.
- **Evidence:** Each block was recorded and the task dropped or reassigned only where legitimate (e.g. one PHerc.1667 iteration dropped; organizer title-search mesh mapping stayed blocked); data-licence acceptance and account sign-ins stayed owner-only. Also: Red-pigment lane: the first numbers-only CT read (a depth histogram of 400 random control chunks from the public bucket) was refused by the session's auto-mode safety check, which said it would keep refusing; the lane created no sub-sibling (that would be a route around), recorded ASK-1 and stopped with params.json frozen so a fresh session could resume steps 3-4 unchanged. Those steps never ran.
- **Fix:** Log the refusal verbatim in ASK.md, keep the design frozen and resumable, and ask the owner to relaunch with appropriate permissions.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-10-15 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#27; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-4-A1, #DECL-P4-14-A2, #DECL-P4-15, #OWNER-LICENSE-EDUCELAB-1, #OWNER-STANDING-ORDER-1; dominion:sib-p4-pig-red:README.md, logs/sib/p4-pig-red/ASK.md, logs/sib/p4-pig-red/STATUS.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:configs/prompt/hercules_master_v7.md, CHANGELOG.md, logs/owner/HANDOFF.md, logs/owner/INBOX.md

### L351. Read-only Explore agents cannot run sealed-output mode; a custom Read-only agent type cannot be loaded mid-session
- **Trap:** Planning to use a tool-less 'blind-reader' agent type or the read-only Explore type for sealed reading.
- **Evidence:** The 'blind-reader' type was 'not found' mid-session and Explore agents refuse to write; the sealed-output harness with a general-purpose agent passed its live test (12/12 letters on a planted synthetic image, 0.7 px coordinates, decoys untouched).
- **Fix:** Use general-purpose agents in sealed-output mode and contain their wider tool set by a post-hoc transcript audit (only the listed Reads, each <= 2 times, one sealed write, hand-back) plus a planted-decoy-file test per harness configuration.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#D0-CONFLICTS, #HARNESS-SEALED-TEST, #DECL-HARNESS, CHANGELOG.md

### L352. Verify against the artifact before reporting; never round a range outward
- **Trap:** Four quantitative claims were retracted in one day, a message was reported delivered when it was not, and "3-700x" was reported where the data said 2.96-623.9x.
- **Evidence:** "The margin fill cut strong ink 3-700x on all 7 strips" was rounded up from 2.96-623.9x (S11); the natural-experiment numbers 0.130 vs 0.020 (29/32) came from an unshipped scratch script and the release code gives 0.163 vs 0.049 (24/29) (S12); a stroke-energy index was withdrawn after failing calibration (S13); and a message reported as delivered had started a new session (S16) (docs/SUPERSEDED_CLAIMS.md).
- **Fix:** Verify against the artifact, label every result (VERIFIED / MEASURED / INFERENCE), and never round a reported range outward or a claim upward.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-10-15 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#20, docs/SUPERSEDED_CLAIMS.md#S11, #S12, #S13, #S16

### L353. Parallel agent fleets burn budget; prefer one detached command per job
- **Trap:** A fleet of sibling sessions (118 registered 25 Sep-2 Oct and 52 more on 9 Oct) burned a large compute and usage budget, and many workers asked for confirmation instead of acting.
- **Evidence:** 118 sibling sessions were registered 25 Sep-2 Oct and 52 more in the 9 Oct fleet (release LESSONS 31; experiment map, Sibling fleet operation). The 9 Oct dispatcher created 0 of 72 triggers, and when usage credits ran out on 10 Oct only 17 of 72 survey positions had finished (register OPS-16).
- **Fix:** Prefer ONE detached command per compute job that pushes its own results; no supervising turns; get the design right before launch.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-10-15 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#31, results/experiments/experiment_map.json

### L354. "Sent" is not "delivered"
- **Trap:** A scheduled-message trigger aimed at an existing session started a NEW session; success was reported from the API response alone.
- **Evidence:** The claim "The introduction message reached its destination" was withdrawn: the trigger had started a new session instead (SUPERSEDED_CLAIMS S16; release LESSONS 33).
- **Fix:** Verify delivery at the destination before reporting it.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-10-15 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#33, docs/SUPERSEDED_CLAIMS.md#S16

### L355. Record the evaluation of a launched run on the shared branch, not only on per-unit branches
- **Trap:** Launching long runs across a fleet and leaving their evaluation on per-unit branches (long 10,000-step spiral fits, Order 9 autopilot, PHerc0268).
- **Evidence:** Order 9 declared a 10,000-step horizon: a one-command autopilot per unit, with snapshots pushed every 1000 steps to the unit branches. No convergence or sheet-lock evaluation of these fits was found on the shared branch, so the outcome is unknown.
- **Fix:** Record the evaluation of every launched run on the shared branch, not only on per-unit branches.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-10-14 (family period) · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/BANDS.md (Order 9); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Long 10,000-step spiral fits (Order 9 autopilot))

### L356. A subagent's final answer leaks into the orchestrator context; use sealed-output mode for any blind reader
- **Trap:** Pickers/sealers/readers hand their answer back to the orchestrator, exposing seal contents (and nested agents were unavailable: a general-purpose subagent has no agent-launch tool). One READ-CAL picker had to be stopped before answering and discarded.
- **Evidence:** DECL-HARNESS-A1 defect; HARNESS-SEALED-TEST: general-purpose agent did Read + one Bash `age -r <recipient> -o <path>` heredoc + hand-back DONE, audit VALID, 12/12 letters, centre error median 0.7 px after scorer-side decryption.
- **Fix:** Brief each blind agent with one output path and the scorer's age recipient; it writes its JSON with exactly one Bash age call and returns only DONE; only scorer code decrypts (every key read logged); a code audit of the transcript voids any agent making any other tool call.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-HARNESS-A1, #HARNESS-SEALED-TEST

### L357. One unfinished freeze step in a shared metric harness blocked every dependent lane
- **Trap:** Making many recipe and screening lanes depend on a single session's freeze step.
- **Evidence:** The DEV-LOOP METRIC-HASH was never recorded because the devloop session was stopped before its freeze; as a result DIST-FT, LC384-SOFT and the official-checkpoint screens A, B and C never received GO and produced no DEV result, although all their phase-1 work passed.
- **Fix:** Finish and hash the shared evaluator/registry before spawning dependent lanes, or make the freeze a small step the orchestrator can complete itself.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-devloop:README.md; dominion:sib-dev-distft:README.md; dominion:sib-dev-lcsoft:README.md; dominion:sib-ckpt-screen-a:README.md; dominion:sib-ckpt-screen-c:README.md; dominion:sib-devloop@835cff610:logs/sib/devloop/ASK.md; dominion:sib-dev-distft@164ad62a3:logs/sib/dev-distft/STATUS.md; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (DEV-loop recipe screening)

### L358. Push the handover file before pausing a split lane
- **Trap:** A lane that splits its work with helper lanes paused (owner stop, then container restart) without pushing the promised HANDOVER.md; two helper lanes sat idle waiting for it.
- **Evidence:** pairs0139 never pushed logs/sib/pairs0139/HANDOVER.md; pairs0139b and pairs0139c each polled for 6 h (waiter v2, 10-min interval) and timed out at 2026-09-26 11:30Z with 0 segments rendered and 0 pairs built.
- **Fix:** Write and push the handover (pinned code commit, segment list, commands, gate, registry format, push rules) as the first act of a split, before any long job or pause; the parent should never hold the only copy of the plan.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-pairs0139:README.md; dominion:sib-pairs0139b:logs/sib/pairs0139b/ASK.md; dominion:sib-pairs0139c:logs/sib/pairs0139c/ASK.md; dominion:sib-pairs0139@580d5241c:logs/sib/pairs0139/ASK.md; dominion:sib-pairs0139b@4ad9cf99e:logs/sib/pairs0139b/ASK.md; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (PHerc0139 training-pair builders (pairs0139, pairs0139b))

### L359. Re-fetch the prize page and licence terms before relying on the catalogue
- **Trap:** A local catalogue of eligible scrolls and assumptions about open-source terms go stale.
- **Evidence:** Live prize page fetched 2026-09-25: PHerc1447 had been removed ('excludes those where letters have now been found'), so the eligible set is 22 while data/catalogue/eligible_products.json still listed 23; the open-source condition became 'code, data, model weights and results'. Licence lineage of the base: ink_9um checkpoint MIT (PERMITS-RELEASE), open-data bucket LICENSE.txt CC BY-NC 4.0 (BLOCKS permissive release of derived data), ink_9um labels state no licence (UNVERIFIED); overall BLOCKS. Also: Diff of scrollprize.org/prizes 2026-09-25 vs 09-24: First Letters eligible volumes 23 -> 22 (PHerc1447 removed: 'excludes those where letters have now been found'); winners must open source code, data, model weights and results; progress-prize early release includes model weights and training data. prizeEligibility.json grand-prize list still had 13 incl. PHerc1447.
- **Fix:** Fetch and hash the prize page at the start of every submission task, diff it against the catalogue, and run a licence-lineage check; derived results must carry CC BY-NC 4.0 and the owner settles licence questions with the organizers.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-sg:logs/sib/sg/REPORT.md, logs/sib/sg/licence/lineage_base_ink9um.json; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#PRIZE-CHECK-20260925

### L360. Commit and push declarations before launching any reader; run an independent auditor before recording a verdict
- **Trap:** Recording verdicts on scorer output alone, and committing an amendment after sealed answers were already written.
- **Evidence:** AUDIT-OMIT-PROBES: three probe verdicts lacked the required auditor; AUDIT-PROBES then passed all three (48/48, 16/16, 12/12 cells re-derived) but disclosed an undeclared interim decryption and a declaration committed at 03:38:03Z after answers were written (03:35-03:37Z).
- **Fix:** Order: declare -> commit+push -> launch agents -> decrypt -> fresh auditor re-derives with independently written code and checks declaration-before-data timestamps -> verdict entry. Mark lifts PROVISIONAL until the audit passes.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#AUDIT-OMIT-PROBES, #AUDIT-PROBES

### L361. A relayed instruction does not lift a direct owner stop; continuing on a new branch routes around it
- **Trap:** Treating an orchestrator's 'unblock' message as permission and re-routing the denied action through a different command (merge, archive copy, alternate checkout).
- **Evidence:** The workers declined the relayed RECIPE-A1 checkout and the merge; the merge attempt itself was denied as 'Auto-Mode Bypass', i.e. the same outcome as the first denial. Each wrote an ASK naming the two owner-side remedies (approve in that session or add a permission rule; or reassign the arm). Also: contam declined five relayed GO/resume triggers after a direct owner stop (2026-09-25 ~23:47Z); devloop held from 2026-09-26; factory held for the owner's own resume; devloop2 refused to perform the freeze on a new branch. Consequence: the DEV-LOOP freeze (FREEZE.md, hold-outs, METRIC-HASH) never happened anywhere.
- **Fix:** Treat only the owner's own message in the same session (or a permission rule) as lifting a stop or a denial; record the hold in ASK.md with exactly what is blocked and do not retry or work around denials.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-contam:logs/sib/contam/ASK.md; dominion:sib-devloop:logs/sib/devloop/ASK.md; dominion:sib-devloop2:README.md; dominion:sib-factory:README.md; dominion:sib-pairs0139:logs/sib/pairs0139/ASK.md; dominion:sib-pp-handcheck:logs/sib/pp-handcheck/ASK.md; dominion:sib-own-f2:README.md; dominion:sib-own-s3:README.md; dominion:sib-own-f1:logs/sib/own-f1/ASK.md

### L362. Keep long jobs detached and self-pushing; in-turn polling burns the account's usage
- **Trap:** Keeping AI sessions alive to babysit multi-hour CPU fits (idle containers are reclaimed and their processes die).
- **Evidence:** Order 6 required units to stay in their turn and poll status at least every 9 minutes, push every 30 minutes and keep a 100-minute send_later backup. Order 9 (owner, 2026-10-11 14:30 UTC) stopped all AI polling because it spent the account's usage: one detached command (setsid nohup autopilot.sh) runs a 10,000-step fit, snapshots and pushes meshes every 1000 steps, writes DONE, and re-running the same command resumes from the newest checkpoint.
- **Fix:** Finish the current atomic step before handling a message; run long jobs in the background with append-only outputs; resume from RESUME.md after resets; siblings in economy mode (no re-reading large files, polling >= 10 min, terse status).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/BANDS.md, tools/spiral_cpu/autopilot.sh; pherc0268:1c73a5d:commit-message; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#OWNER-STANDING-ORDER-3, #OWNER-STANDING-ORDER-4

### L363. Workers need a working tasking channel before they are created, and their outputs must be merged
- **Trap:** Creating sub-sessions with no prompt and planning to message them later; leaving sub-lane scores on their own branches.
- **Evidence:** CU parent created three sub-sessions idle; it had no tool to message cloud sessions, so they were unused until the orchestrator tasked them. They then pushed partial scores on their own branches (E1 20 tiles; C1 64; E2 160 + C2 101) that were never merged; the parent stopped without thresholds, report or verdict. The orchestrator trigger called the lane complete; its STATUS says INCOMPLETE.
- **Fix:** Create workers with their full task in the creation prompt (or verify a messaging path first); give the parent an explicit merge step with consistency checks; verify completion from the lane's own STATUS, not from a trigger.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-pig-cu:README.md, logs/sib/p4-pig-cu/ASK.md, logs/sib/p4-pig-cu/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4-pig-cu-a:README.md; dominion:sib-p4-pig-cu@d2f385f78:logs/sib/p4-pig-cu/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4-pig-cu-a@81697342c:commit message; logs/sib/p4-pig-cu/scores/E1/scores_E1.jsonl; dominion:sib-p4-pig-cu-b@ec2c9ebdc:commit message; logs/sib/p4-pig-cu/scores/C1/scores_C1.jsonl; dominion:sib-p4-pig-cu-c@d0517e207:commit message; logs/sib/p4-pig-cu-c/STATUS.md

### L364. Grade research claims by source strength and quarantine expected-text material
- **Trap:** Reading a paper containing the edited text of the final columns (and possibly title views) before judging title candidates.
- **Evidence:** The research dossier graded findings FIRM/LIKELY/UNCERTAIN, spot-checked key citations at source, and kept expected-text material in one quarantined section that the orchestrator did not read; the title-prior lane wrote no title word, author or book number. A published 1983 census of 70 Herculaneum titles places 91 % beside the last column and 0/70 above the column (95 % upper bound 4 %).
- **Fix:** Keep a single quarantined section for expected text, never shown to readers or orchestrators who design reads; use graded priors only to direct where and how to look.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-research:README.md; dominion:sib-p4-titulus:README.md, logs/sib/p4-titulus/QA.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:configs/prompt/hercules_master_v7.md, CHANGELOG.md, logs/owner/INBOX.md, RULES.md#OWNER-REQUEST-CERC54-READ, #CERC54-LAYOUT-RESULT

### L365. An independent red team of the hypothesis register finds missing channels and mismatched positive controls
- **Trap:** Letting channel builders define both the hypotheses and their controls.
- **Evidence:** The p4-titulus red team of the Paris 4 hypothesis register (v1, 2026-09-26, numbers and published text only) found: the search windows were cut by tile ranges fixed before the measured column pitch (~8 cm = 4 tiles), splitting the most probable title slot; the 'physically lost' hypothesis was under-weighted (0.10 vs about 0.25-0.30, since only about 2 mm of papyrus survives above the mesh top edge, less than one title line); location priors were summed as exclusive (they summed to 1.02, and initial and end titles can coexist); missing channels (ink offset onto the facing winding, stuck layers, a verso title at the outer end, a kollesis/final-sheet anchor); and positive controls that did not match the target (dense body text is not a sparse centred block), so a synthetic sparse-block injection control was needed.
- **Fix:** Assign an independent red-team lane to the hypothesis register early; pre-register its decision tables before the relevant measurements exist.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-titulus:README.md, logs/sib/p4-titulus/REDTEAM.md; dominion:sib-p4-titulus@265ed6cfc:logs/sib/p4-titulus/STATUS.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:logs/p4/HYPOTHESES.md (re-rank 2026-09-27 06:16Z); survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-pigments

### L366. Progress Prizes are the fastest money, but require public open-source code and the owner's approval
- **Trap:** Treating milestone prizes (First Letters, First Title, Grand Prize) as near-term income, or publishing code without approval.
- **Evidence:** Prize map from the official prizes page (fetched 2026-09-26, open pool stated $2,140,000): monthly Progress Prizes paid $1,000 each for small, well-scoped tools in the July 2026 round (best submission $20,000), with awards about 6 days after month end; a winner must make the work open source under a permissive license publicly on GitHub. Milestone reviews are slow (acknowledgement within a week, then technical and papyrological review). Three 200-216-word contribution texts were drafted; submission was left to the owner.
- **Fix:** Package validated small tools for monthly Progress Prizes; get the owner's explicit approval and scrub secrets/sealed material before making a repository public.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-research:logs/sib/p4-research/PRIZES.md, README.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-PP-1, #DECL-PP-1-A2

### L367. Infrastructure failures (rate limits, idle kills) are the common failure mode
- **Trap:** Treating void blind-reader sessions as a protocol failure rather than an infrastructure one (remote sealed-read harness, lane rh-e2).
- **Evidence:** 12 batches under one protocol: 20/20 sessions valid in the first batch and 17/17 in a later one. Exactly one session in the lane was void, killed by an API rate-limit error before any tool call; it was re-run fresh and disclosed, and the re-run was valid.
- **Fix:** Expect infrastructure failures (rate limits, idle kills); a per-session audit with a disclosed fresh re-run handles them without touching answers.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-rh-e2@586d6d75d:logs/sib/rh-e2/STATUS.md (first section), logs/sib/rh-e2/STATUS.md (P4-L section); survey:expmap_raw.json:reading-calibration

### L368. When the task text and the declaration disagree, build the declared recipe and only price the other
- **Trap:** Following a brief's wording ('unfrozen' encoder) that contradicts the frozen declaration.
- **Evidence:** LC384-SOFT: the declared frozen-encoder recipe was built; the undeclared unfrozen reading was only benchmarked (7.67 s/step, 21x the frozen 0.360 s/step).
- **Fix:** Record the conflict in an ASK file, build the declared version, and give the cost of the alternative for the orchestrator to decide.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-dev-lcsoft:README.md, logs/sib/dev-lcsoft/bench_unfrozen.json

### L369. Verify a sub-agent's pushed records before redoing its work
- **Trap:** Concluding a sub-sibling stopped at its last visible checkpoint (or at a 'session limit' status) and recomputing the remainder.
- **Evidence:** The parent believed p4-highz-c2 stopped at 151/171 tiles and finished tiles 152-171 itself; 151 was only the last 30-tile checkpoint push, and the sub-sibling completed all 171 tiles (final jsonl pushed). Every field except wall-clock time agreed in all 171 records.
- **Fix:** Check the sub-agent's branch for a final record before taking over; deterministic, frozen tools turn an accidental duplicate into a free replication check.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-highz-c2:README.md, logs/sib/p4-highz-c2/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4-highz:logs/sib/p4-highz/SUBSIBS.md

### L370. A worker that stops without its own STATUS file leaves finished and interrupted work indistinguishable
- **Trap:** Sub-lanes pushing results with only a commit message.
- **Evidence:** CU sub-lane a pushed E1 scores for 20 of 60 assigned tiles in one commit and has no STATUS file; sub-lane b scored all 64 control tiles but likewise has no STATUS; sub-lane c stopped C2 at 101 of 171 tiles and never updated STATUS to done.
- **Fix:** Require every worker to write STATUS.md with planned vs done counts and an explicit DONE/STOPPED marker before its first push.
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-pig-cu-a:README.md; dominion:sib-p4-pig-cu-b:README.md; dominion:sib-p4-pig-cu-c:README.md

### L371. Plan for account session caps and usage limits when delegating
- **Trap:** Planning sub-lanes without checking the account's session limit.
- **Evidence:** The gold lane's two planned sub-siblings hit the account session limit before doing any work, so the parent ran all injection and scoring itself; the purple lane's two sub-siblings both stopped at usage limits and were resumed; FL-4 A1 workers stopped at the 5-hour usage limit.
- **Fix:** Check available session slots before declaring a split, keep the parent able to run everything, and make workers resumable.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-pig-gold:README.md; dominion:sib-p4-purple:README.md; dominion:sib-p4v-04:README.md

### L372. A dependent lane needs a deadline and a fallback, not only a waiter
- **Trap:** Helper lanes were given a poll-and-wait script with no fallback task, so a missing upstream file cost each of them a full 6 h of idle compute.
- **Evidence:** wait_handover.sh polled every 10 min and exited 3 after 6 h (HANDOVER_TIMEOUT); pairs0139c was later re-tasked by the orchestrator as a helper (S1 maps, FL-2 gate, FL-4) only after the timeout.
- **Fix:** Give every waiting lane a short deadline (for example 1 h) and a pre-declared fallback job, and have the orchestrator re-task on timeout automatically.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-pairs0139b:tools/sib/pairs0139b/wait_handover.sh, README.md; dominion:sib-pairs0139c:README.md

### L373. Make a split build verifiable: re-run the parent's stage and compare field by field
- **Trap:** When a build is split across sessions, silent differences in environment or code make the two halves incomparable.
- **Evidence:** pairs0814b re-ran pairs0814's unchanged stage A on its two handed-over segments; every field except the timestamp, and the ref9/cov9/val9 array sha256, matched pairs0814's own outputs bit for bit; the code copy was verified against SHA256SUMS; 545 registry rows re-derived 'passed' from ncc0 and n_aligned with 0 disagreements.
- **Fix:** Pin code by sha256, re-derive the parent's first stage in the child and diff every field before producing new outputs; run the merge stage once over the union.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-pairs0814b:logs/sib/pairs0814b/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-pairs0814:logs/sib/pairs0814/HANDOVER.md

### L374. Submission kits must leave owner-only fields empty and contain no filing path
- **Trap:** An automated agent drafting a prize submission could fill identity fields, accept terms or file on the owner's behalf.
- **Evidence:** The SG submit kit generates drafts headed 'DRAFT - NOT SUBMITTED - K7' with email, name, team, hosting link and terms acceptance left empty and no network or submission code; the Title Prize form read without sign-in has an Email field plus 4 required owner-only items; its held-out validation requirement (TP-16) is honestly MISSING DATA because no ground truth exists for the title region.
- **Fix:** Generate answer sheets from named JSON fields with a guard that refuses reader text or Greek characters, mark missing data explicitly, and let the owner fill identity fields and submit in person.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-sg:logs/sib/sg/REPORT.md

### L375. Reader transcripts are ~10 MB each: run blind reads in sibling containers with a two-commit protocol
- **Trap:** Running dozens of readers on a container with ~109 MB free.
- **Evidence:** Remote harness: commit A (keys, jobs, briefs, image manifest) pushed before any reader; commit B (sealed .age answers, audits, gzip transcripts); answers encrypted to the orchestrator's age recipient; rh_verify passed all 12 checks (A0-A5, B1-B3) on the first remote census (20 reads).
- **Fix:** Use a harness sibling that never decrypts; verify code hashes, commit order, key vs eligible set, brief equality, transcript re-audit and answer==sealed-write before scoring.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-REMOTE-HARNESS-1, #METRIC-HASH-28, #P4-E2-CENSUS-RESULT

### L376. Hand-backs other than DONE are integrity events even when harmless
- **Trap:** A reader handed back 371 characters (correcting a mistyped item id in its sealed answer).
- **Evidence:** Auditor counted 0 Greek characters; the scorer dropped the mistyped N0 read as coded; recovering it changed nothing.
- **Fix:** Log every non-DONE hand-back as an integrity event; never let a hand-back correct a sealed answer; void a seal only if seal content leaks.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#HANDBACK-EVENT-P4P2-S0

### L377. Keep an owner inbox and answer every request with a status
- **Trap:** Losing owner requests in a burst of messages.
- **Evidence:** logs/owner/INBOX.md numbered every owner request (36 items) with its status, and new messages never cancelled in-flight work unless they said so; owner messages opened with 'No submission ready' plus at most 3 lines and ended with an integrity line.
- **Fix:** Keep a numbered inbox, re-read bursts, and use a fixed message format that states the integrity status.
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:logs/owner/INBOX.md, configs/prompt/hercules_master_v7.md

### L378. Sub-workers that must import code from another branch get blocked by the permission classifier: commit shared code into the recipe branch first
- **Trap:** A worker brief whose setup step is `git checkout <sha> -- tools/<other lane>/ && git reset -q ...` (optionally hiding it via .git/info/exclude) to bring another branch's reader code into the tree.
- **Evidence:** All six P4-OWN arm workers (F1, F2, F3, S2, S3, NULL) were denied that step on 2026-09-27 at about 13:13-13:15Z as 'Untrusted Code Integration'. The orchestrator's merge-based unblock (merge the base branch that carried the same reader) was denied too, as 'Auto-Mode Bypass' (14:22-14:30Z). Nothing was built or trained on those branches; they were stood down at 17:54Z and the lead trained all seven arms itself.
- **Fix:** Commit the shared code, tracked (not hidden), into the recipe branch with its sha256 listed in the frozen recipe, or have the owner grant the permission rule before dispatch. Test the worker setup step in one session before fanning out.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27..2026-10-02 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-own-f1:logs/sib/own-f1/ASK.md; dominion:sib-own-f2:logs/sib/own-f2/ASK.md; dominion:sib-own-s3:README.md; dominion:sib-own-null:README.md; dominion:sib-own-lead:logs/sib/own-lead/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-own-f3@20f5661b1:logs/sib/own-f3/STATUS.md; survey:expmap_raw.json:fine-tuning; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-FL-4-A4-A1-E1, #DECL-FL-4-A4-A2-E1, #DECL-FL-4-A4-A2-E3, logs/owner/INBOX.md

### L379. Multi-agent prompt-regeneration workflows can burn the usage budget
- **Trap:** Running a 24-agent workflow to regenerate the master prompt after each context condensation.
- **Evidence:** v8 run used 1,454,186 subagent tokens across 24 agents; only 3 completed; it was killed by the usage limit and contributed to hitting it.
- **Fix:** Retire it: after a condensation read a live handover file (RESUME_NOW.md), the newest master prompt and the log tail; refresh the prompt in one pass at most once per 24 h with a scripted diff of integrity rules.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#STANDING-ORDER-COMPACT-A2, #STANDING-ORDER-COMPACT-A1; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (STANDING-ORDER-COMPACT-A2); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Multi-agent prompt regeneration)

### L380. Check the submission text against the published package before sending
- **Trap:** Submission sheets drafted earlier drift from what is finally published (numbers re-measured on public data, claims narrowed during packaging, titles mis-copied).
- **Evidence:** Recorded mismatches: tifxyz-dist sheet said 1.6e-11 vox on-surface error, published 2.7e-12 (different mesh); 'exact minimum distance from any mesh' vs a certified [lower, upper] interval; 'agree exactly' vs <= 1e-6 vox. flatcheck sheet promised 'the full run log including failures', which the public repo does not contain, and '33 of 33' hides 8 ties. handcheck brief said 9 of 15 PHerc1447 meshes flagged; the packaged rule flags 11 of 15. The citation-rules file titled a post '$335k awarded in July'; its real title is '$33.5K awarded in July'.
- **Fix:** Generate a sheet-vs-package diff (PUBLISHED.json 'sheet_mismatch') and correct the sheet before filing; take every number from the published repo, and re-check quoted titles against the live page.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-pp-tifxyz-dist:logs/sib/pp-tifxyz-dist/PUBLISHED.json; dominion:sib-pp-flatcheck:logs/sib/pp-flatcheck/PUBLISHED.json; dominion:sib-pp-handcheck:logs/sib/pp-handcheck/PUBLISHED.json; dominion:sib-pp-flatcheck@ec5d06476:logs/sib/pp-flatcheck/PUBLISHED.json; dominion:sib-pp-handcheck@2cfef810c:logs/sib/pp-handcheck/PUBLISHED.json; survey:expmap_raw.json:geometry

### L381. Schedule gate tiles before target tiles; otherwise a failed gate throws away the target-tile compute
- **Trap:** Launching the known-text gate tiles and the target tiles of a cross-scroll model in parallel (all 8 workers started 02:42-02:43Z on 2026-09-27).
- **Evidence:** Each tile cost 2.5-3.9 h on a 4-thread CPU container. When the gate failed 0/3 at 06:52Z, the finished target tiles became uninformative, one finished tile was never read at all, one worker was killed at 1748/4356 windows (40 %), and a further assigned tile was stopped after about 12 minutes.
- **Fix:** Run the gate stage alone first and dispatch target tiles only after it passes. The record made this the rule: any other P4-O iteration must pass a gate-first stage batch (>= 3 gate tiles) before more target tiles are computed.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-o5w4:README.md; dominion:sib-o5w7:README.md; dominion:sib-p4-highz:logs/sib/p4-highz/RESUME.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#P4-O-STAGE-O2S1-RESULT

### L382. A numbers-only builder rule conflicts with computing label statistics: ask for an explicit amendment
- **Trap:** Reading label raster pixel values under a 'never read any image or map pixel' builder rule because only numbers will be reported.
- **Evidence:** p4-excl stopped and wrote an ASK: 'numbers only' limits what is reported, not what is read. It delivered the geometry-only part (coverage per tile) and asked for an amendment or reassignment for the ink lookup.
- **Fix:** When a task needs pixel values the role may not read, get a recorded amendment (read programmatically, never display/save, report aggregates only) or assign it to a role that may.
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-excl:logs/sib/p4-excl/ASK.md

### L383. Scrub a package before it goes public, and know what tools cannot set
- **Trap:** Code copied out of a research repo carries secrets, private paths, governance references, title-search identifiers and personal information.
- **Evidence:** flatcheck scrub: 0 hits in 5 categories; handcheck: 0 findings with 10 reviewed exceptions; tifxyz-dist scrub_ok. Each package was pushed as one commit on top of the owner's LICENSE-only initial commit, with no force-push. No tool could set the GitHub 'About' field; it was left for the owner.
- **Fix:** Run a category scrub (secrets, private paths, governance coupling, title-search terms, personal data) on the exact tree to be pushed, run the tests on a clean install from the published repo, and hand repository settings to the owner.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-pp-flatcheck:logs/sib/pp-flatcheck/scrub.json; dominion:sib-pp-handcheck:logs/sib/pp-handcheck/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-pp-tifxyz-dist:logs/sib/pp-tifxyz-dist/STATUS.md

### L384. Hash fingerprints are what make independent verification possible: keep them, add a verify guide
- **Trap:** Owner asked to drop hashing so the team could verify independently after submission.
- **Evidence:** Declined literally (hashes let anyone confirm files were fixed before results; removing them breaks the METRIC-HASH rule); added VERIFY.md (one-command chain check and per-entry sha256sum -c), and committed decrypted reader answers in plain text after each verdict while the repo is private.
- **Fix:** Keep sha256 fingerprints next to plain-text files; provide one-command verification and unseal answers after verdicts (never publicly before a prize embargo ends).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#OWNER-STANDING-ORDER-4

### L385. Know what a title or First Letters submission needs before the evidence exists
- **Trap:** Finding the package requirements only after a lead appears.
- **Evidence:** Recorded needs: the tifxyz mesh with a low-distortion flattening; a programmatic image with a 1 cm scale bar and letter dimensions, named after the mesh; methodology, false-positive mitigation and held-out validation; a statement that ink-model training data do not overlap the region; the owner's own sign-in on the form. The audit added: first to submit wins under the general rules, Discord registration is required, winners must open-source code, data, weights and results, and repository access is granted privately.
- **Fix:** Keep a submission checklist and a package builder ready early; never publish a prize discovery before the award.

### L386. Session permission layers refuse remote model code, third-party downloads and detached launches: plan approved paths up front
- **Trap:** First Letters pass-2 pipelines were written to run detached (setsid nohup, start dockerd, self-push loops) in fresh sibling sessions; the permission classifier refused the launch, so whole lanes produced nothing.
- **Evidence:** Not launched or held on 2026-09-30: FL-1 pass 2 PHerc0490A (regrescan), FL-2 PHerc1218 (trainer), FL-1 pass 2 PHerc0191 (tribunal), FL-1 PHerc0826 (rh-e2, 'Security Weaken' denial for detached setup_env.sh), FL-2 PHerc0175B (reg0841, held pending owner confirmation). The trainer's delete of its own test ref was also refused. Also: On 2026-09-30 the auto-mode classifier denied the detached pipeline for PHerc0846A ('Unauthorized Persistence', research lane), the self-restarting PHerc1218 pipeline (titulus lane), and the PHerc0343 pipeline (struct lane); on 2026-10-02 it denied a lane restart that fetched and ran go.sh ('Code from External'). None were retried by another route.
- **Fix:** Before a fan-out, have the owner add explicit Bash permission rules for dockerd, detached setup and git push in the sibling sessions, or run pipelines from a session that already holds them; a refused launch is recorded, never worked around.
