### L387. Reconcile a new model arm with standing data-use rules before declaring it
- **Trap:** An order to use a community checkpoint and crop code conflicted with a lane's standing official-only integrity rule.
- **Evidence:** The FL-2 gate order asked for a community dense checkpoint arm and a community title-bar crop; the lane ran official data and checkpoint only, did not read the community repository, and the arm was withdrawn by DECL-FL-2-E1. Also: A third party's public dense model arm (claimed title AUC 0.955 vs 0.814 official on its own within-scroll benchmark) was declared and then withdrawn in full, because the standing rule allowed only the project's own work and official organizer products; its download was also refused by the pilot session's classifier. The within-scroll benchmark did not transfer cross-scroll. Much later the owner overrode the rule for one release positive control only.
- **Fix:** Check standing rules at declaration time; record any override with its exact scope; demand cross-scroll held-out evidence for third-party benchmarks.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-30..2026-10-10 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-FL-2, #DECL-FL-2-E1, logs/owner/AUDIT_2026-09-30.md, RULES.md#OWNER-ORDER-RELEASE-I10; dominion:sib-fl-pherc0257@1f712d0df:logs/sib/fl-pherc0257/fl2/DENSE_FAIL.json; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (DECL-FL-2-E1); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Community dense-model arm); dominion:sib-pairs0139c:logs/sib/pairs0139c/fl2_gate/ASK.md

### L388. Per-unit idempotent markers and pushed per-tile provenance made every defect traceable after the fact
- **Trap:** Running a per-scroll fleet (First Letters material) without a central fix channel and a central quality gate.
- **Evidence:** The fleet produced 2650 official-model tiles covering all 22 eligible volumes, each verified by png sha256. Wave 1: 21 scrolls x 8 tiles = 168 tiles (PHerc0490B had none; its worker never got its environment running). Lanes hit full disks, safety-classifier refusals, background-job time limits, two pipelines running at once (one lane's two-hour window was invalidated) and a shell-variable bug that rendered an old mesh under a new name (16 tiles withdrawn; L463). A bug or flag found by one lane took hours to reach the shared kit.
- **Fix:** Keep per-unit idempotent markers and pushed per-tile provenance (they made every defect traceable), and add a central fix channel and a central quality gate.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-30..2026-10-02 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (FL3-W1-RESULT), RULES.md (FL2-WAVE1-RESULT); dominion:sib-fl-pherc0257@1f712d0df:logs/sib/fl-pherc0257/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-fl-pherc0191@edd797045:logs/sib/fl-pherc0191/fl2/STATUS.md

### L389. Only AI turns cost usage: script everything else and batch the turns
- **Trap:** Polling, status chatter and check-in turns eating the usage allowance.
- **Evidence:** The audit estimated (no cost ledger exists) 43 % of project time lost to usage limits and ~25-40 h to container reclaims, refusals and serial CPU work; every sibling stopped on 'out of usage credits' (seven-day overage) on 2026-10-10. The standing order: repeatable work as detached scripts that push their own results with watchdogs; waiters exit only on actionable events; timed check-ins only as >= 6 h fallbacks.
- **Fix:** Spend AI turns only on blind reads, code review/pinning, declarations, verification and owner messages; batch them; never skip a read or a check to save usage.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#OWNER-STANDING-ORDER-5, logs/owner/AUDIT_2026-09-30.md, logs/owner/INBOX.md

### L390. Honest odds keep the programme pointed at real routes
- **Trap:** Promising a win to match the owner's urgency.
- **Evidence:** The orchestrator repeatedly told the owner that no legitimate path produced a verified First Letters win within 24 h, gave title odds of ~2-7 % and First Letters < 0.5 % in the audit, and lowered no bar.
- **Fix:** State calibrated odds with every plan; never lower a bar for speed.
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:CHANGELOG.md, logs/owner/AUDIT_2026-09-30.md, logs/owner/INBOX.md

### L391. Lane-level numeric checks caught the grow failure a day before the central verdict
- **Trap:** Treating worker lanes as 'parameters only' compute and ignoring their anomaly reports.
- **Evidence:** The PHerc0306B lane's surface check (2026-10-01 02:40Z) and PHerc0846B's geometry check (05:48Z) showed the template grows did not follow the papyrus; DECL-FL-4-A5/-A6 confirmed the cause for all FL-4 grows about a day later, after more compute and reads had been spent on the material.
- **Fix:** Give every worker a cheap numbers-only sanity check of its inputs and route a failing check to an immediate fleet-wide hold.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-fl-pherc0306b:README.md; dominion:sib-fl-pherc0846b:README.md

### L392. A deterministic seed planner with a fixed plan cannot be 'extended' by re-running it
- **Trap:** Asking workers for 48 seeds from a template whose seed function has a hard-coded 8-entry (z, azimuth) plan, then ordering a 'new round' to extend coverage.
- **Evidence:** fl.py cmd_seeds yields at most 8 seeds; lane 0 got at most 4 grow attempts. Re-running 'fl.py seeds ... 48' returned seeds with identical seed_xyz, so a new round would only duplicate segments. Workers diverged: p4v-05 kept the 8-entry plan, p4v-15 built a 48-entry table and later a round shifted 22.5 deg; p4v-01 also built a 48-entry grid; p4v-09 extended with 7 heights x 8 azimuths on order.
- **Fix:** Declare seed plans centrally (one seeds.json shared by all lanes on a scroll) and change seed logic only through a declaration; check that a 'new round' produces new seeds before running it.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4v-05:README.md; dominion:sib-p4v-11:README.md; dominion:sib-p4v-15:README.md; dominion:sib-p4v-12:logs/sib/p4v-12/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4v-14:logs/sib/p4v-14/STATUS.md

### L393. Fresh small-context sessions beat waking long-context sessions
- **Trap:** Re-waking worker sessions that carry huge contexts.
- **Evidence:** Old lane sessions carried 480k-750k-token contexts ($48-$138 spent each); re-waking them would cost about 10x the usage of a fresh session per turn and would likely trip the usage limit again.
- **Fix:** Give each lane a fresh session with a short brief on the same branch and worker name, so outputs and paths stay unchanged.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-FL-4-A4-A1

### L394. Sibling launches must use the attached repository URL exactly, and prove a push before working
- **Trap:** Launching unit sessions with a repo URL that differs in letter case from the attached repository.
- **Evidence:** The first launch of U1-U4 (21:03 UTC) used a URL whose case did not match the attached repository and had to be archived and relaunched (21:07). The launch template then fixed: exact lower-case source_url, STEP 0 = create docs/units/<unit>.md, commit, git push -u; if the push fails call add_repo with push access and retry; continue only after the push succeeds; the orchestrator checks every new branch appears on the remote within minutes.
- **Fix:** Copy the source_url string from the attached-repository record, make the first action a pushed stub, and verify branches appear.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/FLEET.md; pherc0268:a203039:commit-message

### L395. Adversarial verification of study reports catches confident errors
- **Trap:** Building a fleet plan directly from first-pass study reports.
- **Evidence:** The six-reader spiral study was checked by adversarial verifiers and re-checked against primary sources; corrections included the lasagna group/scale pairing, 'sense unknown' (catalog gives CW), 'multiple GPUs needed' for winding inference (one suffices), a stale Paris 4 patch count (~27,399 -> 89,237), 'z_min 4500 is a Scroll 1 default' (batch-wide), and the A vs B schema. Every claim cites KEY:file:line, a URL or a unit report.
- **Fix:** Require citations to file:line for every spec claim and run an adversarial verifier per report before acting.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/SPIRAL_STUDY.md

### L396. Kernel-only benchmarks under contention mislead: measure end to end on the same window
- **Trap:** Adopting a speed patch on the strength of a kernel micro-benchmark run on a shared box.
- **Evidence:** B14's patch 0005 (RK4 adjoint combined gather) was measured as -26 % of the adjoint, but U1's end-to-end 7-step test on one window gave 0001-0003 23.55 s/step, +0004 21.93, +0004+0005 30.71 (about 40 % slower); it was retired. A '6x multithreading penalty' in flatten was also contention, not real.
- **Fix:** Benchmark candidate patches end to end, same window, same box state, several steps; check outputs are bitwise identical.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/BANDS.md, docs/PIPELINE.md; pherc0268:0d075d5:commit-message; pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/BANDS.md (Order 6), docs/BANDS.md (Order 6-A4); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (CPU spiral-fit engineering (memory, speed, settings))

### L397. Cloud sandboxes cap at ~42 concurrent; plan swarms in waves with a claim queue
- **Trap:** Launching ~100 window units at once and assuming each gets a sandbox.
- **Evidence:** 33 of 49 quarter-window units failed sandbox allocation and never started (a retry message did not revive them); at 01:17 UTC 42 sessions were running and 21 idle units messaged since 00:35 had not run a turn. The plan became 68 fitting units in two waves: merged windows for missing partners, a 30-item second-wave queue with claim files (owner first; earliest claim wins; claims expire after 3 h without a push; duplicates become replicates).
- **Fix:** Budget ~42 concurrent sandboxes; give each unit a fallback (absorb a missing partner's core); queue the rest with git-based claims.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/FLEET.md, docs/QUEUE.md, docs/BANDS.md

### L398. A broadcast Orders section plus direct one-shot triggers is how a 68-unit swarm was steered
- **Trap:** Messaging dozens of unit sessions individually, or expecting idle units to notice changes.
- **Evidence:** docs/BANDS.md carried timestamped Orders 1-9 (units re-read them at every step and check-in); direct messages used a one-shot routine bound to the unit's session (persistent_session_id + run_once_at) that wakes it if idle. Orders recorded exceptions per unit and status counts (e.g. 6-A6 status: 23 of 65 runs carried loss_start_track_dt, 8 past it).
- **Fix:** Keep one versioned orders file with numbered, timestamped orders; reserve direct triggers for unit-specific actions.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/FLEET.md, docs/BANDS.md

### L399. .gitignore '*.tif' silently dropped every tifxyz mesh from unit pushes
- **Trap:** Committing mesh folders with git add and assuming they arrived.
- **Evidence:** B16q1's snap_s500 push arrived with 210 meta.json files and no x/y/z.tif because the repo ignored *.tif.
- **Fix:** Un-ignore mesh paths (bands/**/*.tif), use git add -f for meshes, and check git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/<branch> | grep -c 'x\.tif$' equals the winding count.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/BANDS.md; pherc0268:d68b20a:commit-message

### L400. 'git checkout <branch> -- dir' keeps files deleted upstream: a retired patch came back
- **Trap:** Updating tools in unit checkouts with git checkout origin/<shared> -- tools/spiral_cpu after retiring a patch.
- **Evidence:** Units kept patches/0005 next to patches/retired/0005; setup.sh re-applied it (results identical, ~40 % slower) and fit_window.sh start refused to launch (B17q1 incident).
- **Fix:** Make installers skip any patch whose name also exists in patches/retired/, or sync tool directories with deletion (e.g. remove then checkout).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:ce7bebe:commit-message

### L401. A CPU port is a research port until it reproduces a known result
- **Trap:** Trusting PHerc0268 CPU fits from the patched villa chain without a positive control.
- **Evidence:** Both villa versions hard-code CUDA (a CPU-only torch raises AssertionError, which except RuntimeError does not catch); U1's patches (0001 shell-optional, 0002 cpu-device, 0003 trackgraph-iter, later 0004) made the fit run on CPU. The recommended gate (rerun the PHerc0343 recipe band on CPU and compare with the published w047/w048) is not recorded as done; the owner chose CPU only and parked the free-GPU worker kit.
- **Fix:** Before fleet-scale use, reproduce the reference band on the port; keep a GPU path for the reference recipe (24 GB per the recipe).
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/SPIRAL_STUDY.md; pherc0268:7b89dd1:commit-message

**Compute and operations (L402-L451).** CPU-only, ~15 GB RAM, ephemeral containers with usage caps: timing, precision, memory, disk, checkpoints, restarts and keepalives.

### L402. Long jobs need checkpoints that survive a container restart
- **Trap:** Resuming only at tile boundaries when each tile takes 3-4 h and containers are reclaimed or restarted every few hours.
- **Evidence:** dev-distft lost every PHerc.1667 iteration-2 tile to three container reclaims (0 of 108 produced). S1/S2/S3 workers each lost ~4 h of wall time to restarts; S2 lost no computed windows because its 15-min in-tile checkpoint survived, while tiles with no surviving checkpoint restarted from zero. The in-tile resume writes float32 sums every 200 windows (4-8 min) and is bitwise identical to an uninterrupted run. Also: A container restart at about 04:07Z on 2026-09-30 killed all CU jobs (saved: E2 160/160, C2 31, C1 5, E1 0; injection E2 12/12, C2 12/12, E1 8/12, C1 1/12). By contrast the dual-energy application resumed after a usage-limit stop and a restart from its block cache (623 of 1781 blocks) without recomputing any block, and the FE E1 scoring reused saved maps after a restart.
- **Fix:** Checkpoint accumulators inside each tile (every ~15 min), make the builder idempotent (skip finished tiles), keep checkpoints on persistent storage where possible, and push each finished tile immediately.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-10-15 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-pig-cu:logs/sib/p4-pig-cu/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4-purple:logs/sib/p4-purple/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4-pig-fe-e1:README.md; dominion:sib-pairs0139:logs/sib/pairs0139/runs.jsonl; dominion:sib-pairs0814b:logs/sib/pairs0814b/fl2/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-tribunal:logs/sib/tribunal/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-pairs0814:logs/sib/pairs0814/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-readcal2:logs/sib/readcal2/REPORT.md; dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#22; dominion:sib-own-lead:logs/sib/own-lead/STATUS.md, logs/sib/own-lead/RESUME.md; dominion:sib-hzw2:logs/sib/hzw2/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-hzw1:logs/sib/hzw1/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-dev-distft:logs/sib/dev-distft/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-ckpt-screen-b-s2:README.md; dominion:sib-ckpt-screen-c-s2:README.md; dominion:sib-ckpt-screen-b:logs/sib/ckpt-screen-b/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-o5w7:README.md, logs/sib/o5w7/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-ckpt-screen-c@3916ff853:logs/sib/ckpt-screen-c/p4o/PHerc.1667-iteration-4/manifest.json; dominion:sib-dev-lcsoft@cb6dcb853:logs/sib/dev-lcsoft/p4o/PHerc.1667-iteration-1/manifest.json; dominion:sib-dev-distft@164ad62a3:logs/sib/dev-distft/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-ckpt-screen-c@3916ff853:logs/sib/ckpt-screen-c/STATUS.md; p4o/bf16_check.json

### L403. Watchers and merge loops stall silently after container restarts
- **Trap:** Assuming a background merge loop keeps working after a restart.
- **Evidence:** ckpt-screen-c: the merge loop's fetch stopped merging after container restarts (merged [] while tiles existed) and had to be run by hand and restarted. Docker daemons also did not survive restarts (chain2um, flat1), so later renders failed until dockerd was restarted.
- **Fix:** After any restart, re-check every background loop's last successful action and restart dockerd; pipelines should test `docker info` even when an env-ok marker exists (the FL template re-runs setup_env.sh idempotently in that case).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-10-15 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-ckpt-screen-c:logs/sib/ckpt-screen-c/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-chain2um:logs/sib/chain2um/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-flat1:logs/sib/flat1/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-fl-pherc0257:tools/sib/fl-pherc0257/pipeline.sh; dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#30

### L404. Check for AMX before choosing bf16 on CPU: without it bf16 is ~2x slower
- **Trap:** Planning bf16 runs from a benchmark taken on a different host type. Cloud containers of the same nominal size differ (AMX Sapphire-class vs Cascade Lake without AMX or avx512_bf16).
- **Evidence:** AMX host (oneDNN brg_conv avx10_1_512_amx kernels): bf16 inference 1.60-1.74x faster at 4 threads, training step 1.83-2.06x (2.1-2.5x at 1-2 threads). Non-AMX host (chain2um): bf16 emulated at 15.54 s/tile vs fp32 8.21 s/tile, i.e. 1.9x slower. D2 hosts: the same fp32 cell ran at 148.75 s/step vs 103.98 s/step on the trainer's host (1.43x). Also: GP TimeSformer on a non-AMX 4-thread CPU: fp32 about 200 ms/window, villa bf16 autocast about 400 ms/window, so fp32 was used; fp32 vs bf16 agreement Pearson 0.999926 (max abs diff 3). On the AMX host the 2 um model ran bf16 3.8 s/tile vs fp32 5.1 s/tile, and trainer P128 steps 6.79 vs 11.94 s. pairs0814's container had no AMX flags although docs described a 2.1 GHz AMX host; bf16 at 512 px crashed natively.
- **Fix:** Run `lscpu | grep -o 'amx[a-z_0-9]*'` (or grep /proc/cpuinfo for amx_bf16/avx512_bf16) and time a few steps on each host before planning. channels_last never helped fp32 (0.85-1.01x) and gave at most ~10 % with bf16 (within noise).
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-amx:logs/sib/amx/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-chain2um:logs/sib/chain2um/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-d2-null:logs/sib/d2-null/READY.md; dominion:sib-d2-rev:README.md; dominion:sib-pairs0139c:logs/sib/pairs0139c/fl4_gate/STATUS.md, logs/sib/pairs0139c/fl4_gate/precision_check.json; dominion:sib-reg0841:logs/sib/reg0841/chainvalid/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-trainer:logs/sib/trainer/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-pairs0814:logs/sib/pairs0814/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-d2-null@45b1ccf72:logs/sib/d2-null/READY.md; dominion:sib-d2-p128@b737266dd:logs/sib/d2-p128/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-d2-rev@e627fa999:logs/sib/d2-rev/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-d2-p384@0cec61d6a:commit message

### L405. Ephemeral containers: seal keys and signing keys die with the container
- **Trap:** Creating a sealed set in one container and scoring it in another.
- **Evidence:** The seal decryption key lived only in the orchestrator container, so sealed-but-unscored answers would become unreadable if it was reclaimed; the S2, S3 and NULL weights existed only in one sibling's /work until pushed.
- **Fix:** Create, read and score a sealed set within one container lifetime, or escrow the key in an owner-provisioned store; generate signing keys per session.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#D0-CONFLICTS, logs/owner/HANDOFF.md, logs/owner/AUDIT_2026-09-30.md, CHANGELOG.md

### L406. Check the provisioned hardware before planning: the prompt assumed 8 GPUs, the container had 4 CPUs and no GPU
- **Trap:** Plan written for 8 x A100/H100, 1 TB RAM, 10 TB NVMe; actual container: 4 CPU cores, 15 GB RAM, ~30 GB free disk, no GPU, ephemeral.
- **Evidence:** Measured: base ink_9um inference 0.114 s per 128 px tile on 3 threads (~0.07 h per 2 x 2 cm window both orders, 0.28 h with --tta-mirror); ink_canonical_2um ~5.25 s per 256x256x62 tile (6-35 h per 2 x 2 cm window); normal grids for 23 volumes total 386.9 GB (790,141 objects) and cannot be synced; official VC3D apps built from villa source in 3 min 46 s on 3 cores.
- **Fix:** Measure per-tile inference time and free disk on day 0, shrink the plan (no training needing ~60 GPU-h, no 23-volume census), and re-date every decision before any deciding data exists.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#D0-CONFLICTS, #D0-HW, #DECL-FL-4

### L407. Create every prerequisite inside the job
- **Trap:** A daemon failed to start because a log directory was missing.
- **Evidence:** A daemon did not start because a log directory it needed was missing; the release records the fix as creating every prerequisite inside the job (release LESSONS 23, Operations).
- **Fix:** Create every prerequisite (directories, env) inside the job itself.

### L408. Cap caches: a CT mirror that only grows causes OOM kills
- **Trap:** A local CT mirror reached 9.4 GB on a 16 GB RAM disk and caused out-of-memory kills.
- **Evidence:** The local CT mirror grew to 9.4 GB on a 16 GB RAM disk and out-of-memory kills followed; the fix was a size cap and trim (bi_mirror.py --cap-gb) plus deleting finished work dirs (release LESSONS 24).
- **Fix:** Cap and trim the mirror (bi_mirror.py --cap-gb), delete finished work dirs, and watch RAM.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-10-15 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#24

### L409. Never edit a running bash script in place
- **Trap:** Editing a bash script while it runs corrupts the run (bash reads the file incrementally).
- **Evidence:** Bash reads a script incrementally while it runs, so an in-place edit corrupted a running job; writing a new file and renaming it over the old one leaves running instances on the old inode (release LESSONS 26).
- **Fix:** Write a new file and rename it over the old one; running instances keep the old inode.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-10-15 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#26

### L410. Check df before cloning or writing anything large
- **Trap:** The disk was nearly full; background jobs share it.
- **Evidence:** The disk was nearly full and background jobs shared it; the recorded fix is to check df before any clone or large write (release LESSONS 28, Operations).
- **Fix:** Check df before cloning or writing anything large; account for background jobs.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-10-15 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#28

### L411. The job runner must append to the compute ledger automatically
- **Trap:** Logging compute by hand.
- **Evidence:** Main container: 4 CPU cores, 15 GB RAM, 30 GB free disk, no GPU. The compute ledger holds 78 jobs, all CPU (GPU-h 0), 73 with exit code 0, the last ending 2026-09-25T02:16:21Z; cumulative CPU about 14 core-h to 2026-09-25 11:00Z. Manual logging lapsed within a day and the fleet's compute was never ledgered.

### L412. On a usage-capped, CPU-only, ephemeral platform, the binding constraint was availability, not method
- **Trap:** Planning as if method were the binding constraint on a usage-capped, CPU-only, ephemeral platform.
- **Evidence:** No complete cost ledger exists, so the total cost cannot be stated. The 2026-09-30 adversarial review estimated (not measured) that 43 % of project time went to usage limits and ~25-40 h to container reclaims, refusals and serial CPU work, while the validity machinery cost minutes. Measured: when every sibling stopped on "out of usage credits" on 2026-10-10, the DECL-E2E-3 survey had finished 17 of 72 positions (logs/owner/INBOX.md item 36).
- **Fix:** Treat availability as the binding constraint: budget usage explicitly, make every job resumable and pushed, and keep an automatic ledger of time and usage from day one.
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-10-10 (family period) · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:logs/owner/AUDIT_2026-09-30.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:logs/owner/INBOX.md (item 36); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Operating cost and failure modes)

### L413. Stream data; offload with a verified self-test; keep under GitHub limits
- **Trap:** Downloading whole volumes or deleting local copies before the remote copy is verified.
- **Evidence:** Disk doctrine: inputs stream from the official S3 bucket; outputs compact (uint8 PNG, npz); batches go to a git data branch, one commit per batch, remote tip verified before local deletion; the first push was a synthetic self-test (push, delete, fetch back, compare: identical). GitHub limits 100 MB per file and ~5 GB per repo; free disk ranged from ~0.1 to ~3 GB. Also: FL-4 PHerc0268 lane: 7 of 7 renders on 2026-10-01 failed with 'No space left on device'; FL-2 renders hitting the same error had to be rerun. The offload branch stored 1324 files / 3,391,551,719 bytes in 4 batch commits, each with BATCH.json listing path, bytes and sha256 per file, refusing key files, sealed answers, symlinks, files >95 MB and raw CT.
- **Fix:** Check free disk before each render, and move closed work to a chained offload branch (one commit per batch, per-file sha256) instead of deleting.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:configs/prompt/hercules_master_v7.md, CHANGELOG.md, RESUME_NOW.md, STATE.md, RULES.md#DECL-OFFLOAD-1; dominion:sib-fl-pherc0306b:logs/sib/fl-pherc0306b/fl4/PHerc0268/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-fl-pherc0175b:README.md; dominion:data:README.md, BATCH.json; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:CHANGELOG.md, RULES.md (METRIC-HASH-30 note), logs/offload/manifest.jsonl; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Data offload to a git data branch)

### L414. bf16 (AMX) inference is not accurate enough for ink maps; fp32 CPU inference is cheap enough
- **Trap:** Accepting a reduced-precision (bf16) ink map because its correlation with fp32 is 0.999+.
- **Evidence:** Synthetic official chain: Pearson 0.99943 / 0.99910 but only 98.18 % / 97.72 % of pixels within +-2 grey levels (bar 99.9 %), max |diff| 5 / 7. Real 2.4 um PHerc0139 control: Pearson 0.99997 but 98.41 % within +-2. PHerc.1667 iteration-4 one-tile check on a Paris 4 surface volume: 8.94 % of 59,719,609 mesh-valid pixels differ by more than 2/255 (limit 1 %), max 16/255. Precision ablation: no bf16 placement both speeds up inference and keeps 99.9 % within +-2; the 3-D stem causes most drift. Also: On an AMX host bf16 gave x1.6-1.7 inference (fp32 11.5 vs bf16 18.4-19.6 tiles/s at 4 threads) and x1.8-2.0 training speed-ups, but bf16 inference failed the +-2 grey-level bar, so inference stayed fp32; another sibling container had no AMX and no avx512_bf16.
- **Fix:** Gate any precision change for maps on a per-pixel bar, not on correlation. Run a single-tile bf16-vs-fp32 equivalence check before production tiles; on fail keep fp32 (DECL-AMX-1 was declared for training parity only; every map stayed fp32).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-AMX-1, CHANGELOG.md; dominion:sib-amx:logs/sib/amx/REPORT.md, logs/sib/amx/synth_chain_gate.json; dominion:sib-chain2um:logs/sib/chain2um/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-ckpt-screen-c:logs/sib/ckpt-screen-c/p4o/bf16_check.json

### L415. API usage limits kill reader agents mid-run; plan for re-runs without bias
- **Trap:** An owner-side interrupt stopped 4 readers after their sealed-write command but before the file existed; two D3 auditors were stopped (interrupt, then usage limit).
- **Evidence:** 12 BASE/RAW readers had written answers (4 died after the write), 6 CHANCE readers died with 0 reads/writes.
- **Fix:** Re-run only agents that saw no image, with identical brief and output path; discard any job that dies after reading images and create a new job for its slot.

### L416. Measure throughput before committing to a training programme
- **Trap:** Committing to a CPU training programme before measuring throughput (pooled-training CPU trainer, D2 infrastructure).
- **Evidence:** The trainer was built and tested on synthetic data only (26 tests passed, 0 failed): it matched the earlier fine-tune loop bitwise, was bitwise deterministic and resumed bitwise from remotely stored checkpoint shards. Measured cost per 12k-step arm, fp32, 4 threads: 39.8 h at 128 px; 346.6 h (14.4 d) at 384 px (L423).
- **Fix:** Measure throughput before committing to a training programme. Remote checkpoint shards make long CPU runs survive reclaims, at the cost of unreachable objects piling up on the remote (L420).

### L417. Gated pair building with re-derivable PASS flags (all 545 recomputed and matched) makes split work auditable
- **Trap:** Splitting a training-pair build across sessions without re-derivable pass flags (PHerc0814 pairs0814 / pairs0814b, D2 material).
- **Evidence:** Both halves finished: 149 PASS rows (36 %) in the primary half and 235 of 545 (43.1 %) in the handed-over half passed the CT-correlation and alignment gates; all 545 PASS flags were recomputed and matched. pairs0814b was later reused as a First Letters worker (23 PHerc1545 segments tiled) and as an FL-4 lane.
- **Fix:** Store every gate input with its PASS flag so a reviewer can re-derive it; that is what makes split work auditable.

### L418. Gate a costly run behind an explicit GO marker, and record whether the gate was ever released
- **Trap:** Preparing a costly run near sealed material and never releasing or retiring its gate (PHerc0841 CHAIN VALID preparation).
- **Evidence:** Meshes were mapped with the frozen non-affine field, a fail-closed exclusion clearance from the sealed benchmark was applied (L214), the inference driver was copied from the 2 um chain lane and the metrics were tested on synthetic data. The runner refuses to start without an explicit GO marker; its status stayed WAITING FOR GO and the chain run never executed.
- **Fix:** Gate a costly run behind an explicit GO marker (it prevented any accidental ink map near sealed material), and record whether and when the gate is released or retired.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-reg0841@1bdfd0bae:logs/sib/reg0841/chainvalid/REPORT.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (REG-0841-NA); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (PHerc0841 CHAIN VALID preparation)

### L419. int8 quantization of the 9 um ink model is not feasible in the pinned environment
- **Trap:** Expecting quick int8 CPU speed-ups with PyTorch quantization.
- **Evidence:** quantize_dynamic is a no-op (0 Linear vs 71 conv/deconv modules; output bitwise fp32); FX static PTQ fails (TraceError on control flow in NetworkFromConfig.forward; float(Proxy) in encoder.py:163); PT2E needs torchao, not in the freeze.
- **Fix:** Do not spend time on int8 without tracing-friendly model code or new dependencies; bf16 fidelity already fails the map bar, int8 would be worse.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-amx:logs/sib/amx/int8_feas.json, logs/sib/amx/REPORT.md

### L420. Do not store weights on git as force-pushed orphan commits
- **Trap:** Using a git ref as a reclaim-safe checkpoint store: superseded states stay on the remote as unreachable objects, and the session may be refused the destructive delete needed to clean up.
- **Evidence:** A full resume state (414,952,758 bytes in 5 shards < 90 MB) pushed in 90.3 s; final synthetic weights (138,362,143 bytes, 2 shards) fetched back byte-identical. Pushing every 24 h would leave about 55 GB of unreachable objects across 12 sessions. After the Q6 ruling the trainer refuses network remotes for weights; its delete of the test ref was refused, so the ref remains.
- **Fix:** Keep weights off git; use a store with deletion, and plan a cleanup route that does not depend on a destructive git command.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-trainer:logs/sib/trainer/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-trainer-ckpt:MANIFEST.json, README.md
