### L423. Full-forward 384-px training of the 9 um model is not feasible on CPU
- **Trap:** Planning a 12,000-step multi-arm fine-tune on 4-vCPU containers.
- **Evidence:** Median step time at batch 32, fp32, 4 threads: P384 129.16 s (17.9 days per arm), NULL 148.75 s (20.7 days), REV 147.8 s (~20.5 days), P128 18.35 s (2.55 days). Peak RSS 6.85-9.89 GB. D2 was recorded as blocked for lack of a GPU (NOT RUN if no GPU by 2026-11-15). Also: Throughput (batch 32, 4 threads): P128 11.94 s/step fp32 (39.8 h per 12,000 steps), P384 full 103.98 s/step (346.6 h, 14.4 d), 512 full 180.85 s/step (25.1 d); 12 arm-seeds = 135 session-days fp32, 83 bf16; 384 fp32 at micro-batch 8 and 512 fp32 at micro-batch 4 were OOM-killed on 15 GB. D2 never received its amendment or GO and is recorded as blocked for lack of a GPU.
- **Fix:** Use a GPU for full-forward fine-tunes, or switch to cached-feature (decoder-only) recipes on CPU; measure step time per host before committing.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-d2-null:logs/sib/d2-null/READY.md; dominion:sib-d2-p384:logs/sib/d2-p384/smoke_result.json; dominion:sib-d2-rev:logs/sib/d2-rev/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-d2-p128:logs/sib/d2-p128/READY.md; dominion:sib-trainer:logs/sib/trainer/REPORT.md, logs/sib/trainer/throughput.json

### L424. Container restarts wipe /dev/shm and stop dockerd
- **Trap:** Moving data to /dev/shm as overflow storage, or deleting regenerable data / pushing to a non-designated branch on a general delegation.
- **Evidence:** A restart cleared 109 MB of tile copies in /dev/shm (content survived on builder branches); the auto-mode safety check refused deleting a 4.9 GB docker store and the first push to the data branch; the owner then approved both with exact sentences ('I approve deleting ...', 'I permit pushing to ...').
- **Fix:** Start dockerd via setup_env.sh whenever `docker info` fails; make every RAM artefact regenerable by script; commit anything decision-relevant at once; score sealed answers promptly.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-FL-4-A4-E2, RESUME_NOW.md, logs/owner/HANDOFF.md, RULES.md#DECL-OFFLOAD-1, #DECL-OFFLOAD-1-A1, #DECL-OFFLOAD-1-A1-CORR, #DECL-OFFLOAD-1-A2

### L425. Probe split-vs-serial cost before spawning sub-agents
- **Trap:** Spawning sub-siblings for jobs that one container finishes faster than new sessions can start.
- **Evidence:** p4-crackle: about 30 s range-read fetch (17 slices, ~1.4 GB) overlapped with about 24 s DoG per level-0 tile, 60 tiles in about 35 min, so no sub-sibling was created. p4-highz: ~450-480 level-0 range requests/s (6 processes x 24 threads), ~0.6 M chunk reads in ~25 min; it split off one sub-sibling only when the work grew to ~1.4 M reads (~110 min).
- **Fix:** Measure per-tile fetch and compute first; split only when the serial time clearly exceeds spawn + briefing + merge overhead.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-crackle:logs/sib/p4-crackle/SUBSIBS.md; dominion:sib-p4-highz:logs/sib/p4-highz/SUBSIBS.md

### L426. Level-0 raw-CT scoring is network-bound: plan the split before starting
- **Trap:** Starting a level-0 scan of several materials in one container.
- **Evidence:** Level-0 scoring of four materials streams about 300 GB of range reads; one container reaches about 70 MB/s with 4 CPU cores (~28 s per level-0 tile). The 2.4 um zarr has 128^3 uncompressed u8 chunks. The morphology gate streamed ~120 GB for 16 tiles; FE E1 maps alone fetched 289,883 chunks.
- **Fix:** Estimate bytes and tiles per material up front, split by material across workers with a verified frozen code hash, and checkpoint per tile.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-pig-cu:logs/sib/p4-pig-cu/SUBSIBS.md, logs/sib/p4-pig-cu/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4-purple-mo:logs/sib/p4-purple/mo/REPORT.md

### L427. Keep shard files under 90 MB and branches under their budget
- **Trap:** Pushing training pairs or weights to GitHub as large files or repacked shards.
- **Evidence:** PHerc0814 pairs: 180 block files, 1560.9 MB in total, max 33.6 MB, each < 90 MB, pushed in batches of <= ~500 MB; repacking into 20-patch shards was skipped because it would duplicate every patch and exceed the 1.5 GB branch budget.
- **Fix:** Write one compressed file per block under 90 MB with sha256 in a registry, push in <= 500 MB batches, and record any refused push.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-pairs0814:logs/sib/pairs0814/REPORT.md, logs/sib/pairs0814/ASK.md

### L428. CPU inference cost: plan in CPU-hours per cm^2, it is large
- **Trap:** Planning a CPU fleet for a large 3-D ink model without a measured per-tile cost.
- **Evidence:** At 4 threads, fp32, window 256, stride 128, slices 23-84, forward order only: 3389-4356 model windows per tile took 2.53-3.89 h (o5w2 2.531 h for 3614 windows; o5w3 13322.9 s for 4356; o5w4 14014 s for 3389; o5w6 12614.6 s for 4356). Missing CT chunks (S3 404) were 0 to 851 per tile and were zero-filled as in the builder. Also: 2.4 um canonical model on 4 non-AMX vCPU: 8.21 s/tile, 1060.5 tiles per cm^2 per order -> about 2.4 h wall (9.6 core-h) per cm^2 per order, ~19 h wall for a 2x2 cm window in both orders. PHerc.1667 checkpoints on a 2.4 um surface volume: 4.05 s per 256-px window, ~4,356 windows, 3.3-4.9 CPU-h per 2x2 cm tile; a 108-tile grid is ~450-480 h on one worker. 9 um official model: one 2x2 cm window in both orders ~3.2 min fp32 at 4 threads. DEV screen: 624 CPU-min per 2 cm window for four checkpoints, both orders.
- **Fix:** Order tiles by prior (title zone + known-text gate tiles first), push partial manifests per stage, read each stage as its own batch; allow bf16 only after an equivalence check on one gate tile (<= 1 % of pixels differ by > 2/255).
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-chain2um:logs/sib/chain2um/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-ckpt-screen-c:logs/sib/ckpt-screen-c/ASK.md; dominion:sib-ckpt-screen-a:logs/sib/ckpt-screen-a/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-ckpt-screen-b:logs/sib/ckpt-screen-b/p4o/SUBSIBS.md; dominion:sib-amx:logs/sib/amx/REPORT.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-14-A2; dominion:sib-o5w2:README.md; dominion:sib-o5w3:README.md; dominion:sib-o5w4:README.md; dominion:sib-o5w6:README.md

### L429. np.concatenate over memory-mapped shards silently loads everything into RAM
- **Trap:** Loading a 17 GB memory-mapped patch set with np.concatenate(parts) on a ~15 GB container.
- **Evidence:** The first S1 launch (2026-09-27 13:05Z) was OOM-killed during data loading at 0 training steps (memory cgroup OOM, anon-rss 13.9 GB).
- **Fix:** Index the shards lazily (a ShardCat whose item i equals np.concatenate(parts)[i], unit-tested), keep batches/seeds identical, and record the change as an implementation amendment with the new sha256 before any training completes.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-own-lead:logs/sib/own-lead/p4own/RECIPE_A1.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#METRIC-HASH-46

### L430. Lasagna flatten on CPU: run one-thread processes in parallel, not threads
- **Trap:** Running training and inference strictly one after the other at full thread count.
- **Evidence:** F1 training at 2 threads ran 6.42 s/step (4.45 alone at 4 threads) while S1 inference at 2 threads ran about 7.9 min/tile (4.9 alone); combined throughput was 1.31x sequential, so both were kept concurrent. RAM rule used for a second concurrent trainer: MemAvailable >= peak train RSS + 2 GB (F2 VmHWM 7.4 GB, mostly shared mmap).
- **Fix:** Measure the concurrent vs sequential throughput once and adopt the faster schedule; gate extra concurrent jobs on a memory rule.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27..2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/PIPELINE.md; dominion:sib-own-lead:logs/sib/own-lead/STATUS.md

### L431. A statistic that is only logged can OOM-kill a worker; measure memory stage by stage
- **Trap:** Blaming the obvious large read (read_stack) for container OOM kills.
- **Evidence:** Builder p4o_tiles.py: boolean-index and clip copies of a 4.6 GB stack in a logged norm_mean pushed peak to about 14 GB, above the 13.36-14.3 GB cgroup limits (3 OOM kills on one worker). A separate unbounded chunk-read map OOM-killed another run at anon-rss 14.0 GB, costing ~6 h of parent compute. A banded integer-sum norm_mean (equal on 3/3 synthetic checks) cut sampled VmHWM to 6,818,616 kB. The worker's first attribution to read_stack was wrong and was corrected after a staged diagnostic with an RSS/cgroup sampler.
- **Fix:** Run an RSS + cgroup memory sampler with a stage-by-stage diagnostic before patching; avoid full-size temporary copies in logging code; bound chunk caches; a 16 GiB swapfile can bridge until a fix lands.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-ckpt-screen-b-s3:logs/sib/ckpt-screen-b/p4o/S3_NOTES.md; dominion:sib-ckpt-screen-b-s2:logs/sib/ckpt-screen-b/p4o/S2_NOTES.md; dominion:sib-ckpt-screen-c:logs/sib/ckpt-screen-c/STATUS.md

### L432. Measured CPU budget for a from-scratch 2.4 um ink CNN
- **Trap:** Picking model size and patch size without timing them on the actual 4-vCPU container.
- **Evidence:** Config A (232,697 params, RF radius 151 px): 0.50 / 1.41 / 2.70 s/step at batch 16 and patch 128/192/256; config B (550,937 params) 0.96 / 2.84 / 5.28 s/step. End-to-end tile inference 4.89 min incl. S3 reads (peak RSS 3.75 GB; S3 read 40.5 MB/s), about 7.9 min/tile at 2 threads. 2500 steps took about 2.1 h/arm at 4 threads and about 4.5 h/arm at 2 threads. The reader does not cache CT chunks, so re-maps still cost about 5 min/tile.
- **Fix:** Time candidate configs with random labels on a training-zone tile before freezing; choose the config that fits the per-arm and per-tile bars (here 20 min/tile).
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-own-lead:logs/sib/own-lead/STATUS.md, logs/sib/own-lead/p4own/RECIPE.md

### L433. Contending processes invalidate timing tests
- **Trap:** Running two timing benchmarks at once on the same CPUs.
- **Evidence:** own-lead's first timing run was declared INVALID because two timing processes contended for the CPU; it was discarded and re-run.
- **Fix:** Run timing tests alone on the container and record the thread count.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-own-lead:logs/sib/own-lead/STATUS.md

### L434. A float64 stretch on large windows OOMs: compute it from the uint8 histogram
- **Trap:** Computing a percentile stretch in float64 on 16686 px windows on a ~15 GB container.
- **Evidence:** Two window processes were OOM-killed (the float64 stretch peaked at ~9.7 GB). The same stretch from the uint8 histogram plus a LUT was byte-identical to the builder's (30/30 synthetic cases and a real window), and killed runs resumed with no duplicate windows.
- **Fix:** Use histogram + LUT stretches for uint8 data and test byte identity against the reference implementation.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-l2:logs/sib/p4-l2/STATUS.md

### L435. Inference band checkpoints fill the disk unless deleted after each committed tile
- **Trap:** Keeping per-tile resume checkpoints after the tile has been committed.
- **Evidence:** own-lead's disk hit the 5 GB free-space floor at 00:53Z; 73 stale band checkpoints (4.7 GB) were removed and run_arms.py was changed to delete infer.py's band checkpoint after each committed tile.
- **Fix:** Delete a tile's checkpoint once its outputs are committed and pushed; check df before and after large jobs and keep >= 5 GB free.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-28 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-own-lead:logs/sib/own-lead/STATUS.md

### L436. Budget memory explicitly on 15 GB containers
- **Trap:** Launching several inference or geometry jobs at once on a 4 vCPU / 15 GB container.
- **Evidence:** Five inference processes at once (2 lanes + 3 seeds, about 3.6 GB RSS each) were killed by the OOM killer; windows.py was OOM-killed beside a full-resolution label check, which was itself killed (exit 137); 5 x 5 densification of 2.401 um meshes needs about 27 GB. Also: A level-2 census was OOM-killed at 4.96 GB RSS with other jobs resident; ORD-3 tracking peaked at 7.2-7.5 GB (declared cap 3 GB); a second audit worker died with two ~4 GB chunk caches; one full 11632 x 11008 section through the ridge operator would need ~10 GB. A 1.38 GB native block fetched in 12.4 s (112 MB/s).
- **Fix:** Gate fetches on `free -m`; compute fields on tube bounding boxes only; keep one resident row; log RSS per process.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-30..2026-10-10 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#UNR-X0-SURVEY-RESULT, #ORD3-PILOTB-RESULT, #VC3D-AUDIT-RESULT, #DECL-E2E-2; dominion:sib-pairs0814b:logs/sib/pairs0814b/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-reg0009b:logs/sib/reg0009b/REPORT.md

### L437. Distributed map makers need a byte-identical reproduction gate
- **Trap:** Letting many fresh sessions produce maps with 'the same' code and model and pooling them without checking that each container reproduces a reference output.
- **Evidence:** 15 verso/forward map makers each re-made one reference forward map first; 14 matched the reference PNG sha256; p4v-13 got fb6a6900... vs 6954db7d... (same valid pixels, means differing by a relative ~4e-10), stood down, and none of its maps were used. Its own resumed and clean runs agreed exactly (0 px differ on bands 1-2). 63 duplicate map pairs from different makers were byte-identical. Also: Each helper first re-made one existing map; 63 cross-maker duplicate pairs (49 verso, 14 forward) and 16 + 15 duplicate pairs in other regions were all byte-identical. One container's map differed (mean 88.53055721 vs 88.53055724, relative ~4e-10; floating-point nondeterminism on that CPU) and all its maps were excluded.
- **Fix:** Gate every worker on a byte-identical reproduction of a reference artefact before its outputs enter a census; record CPU flags, torch build and thread count; candidate causes to test: library/AVX512 path, thread count, checkpoint resume without fsync.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-30..2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-25-A10, #DECL-P4-26-A2-E2, #P4-OFF-CORR-RESULT; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md#P4-OFF-CORR-RESULT; dominion:sib-p4v-13@6298724d7:logs/sib/p4v-13/STATUS.md; survey:expmap_raw.json:paris4-census; dominion:sib-p4v-13:README.md, logs/sib/p4v-13/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4v-10:logs/sib/p4v-10/STATUS.md

### L438. Compute spent without a read plan is lost
- **Trap:** Fanning out compute before scoping what will be read (Grand Prize inner-winding lanes on PHerc0490A).
- **Evidence:** The FL-4 kit ran on PHerc0490A in lanes fl-pilot, fl-pherc0175b, fl-pherc0483b, fl-pherc0846b, census and pairs0139c, but DECL-FL-4-A3 limited reading to PHerc0268, so the PHerc0490A outputs are not read; the dedicated fl-pherc0490a FL-4 run never started (held pending owner permission).
- **Fix:** Scope reading before fanning out compute; compute spent without a read plan is lost.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-30..2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (DECL-FL-4-A3 item 1); dominion:sib-fl-pherc0490a@e52e2c1ac:logs/sib/fl-pherc0490a/fl4/PHerc0490A/STATUS.md; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (GP inner-winding lanes on PHerc0490A)

### L439. Parallel lanes must not read a shared input while another lane is still downloading it
- **Trap:** Two lanes on the same host start together and one reads a mesh file mid-download.
- **Evidence:** S1 map helper: lane A failed in load_valid because it read lane B's in-progress curl of the same mesh x.tif; the files were later verified complete (120,307,846 B each == S3 Content-Length); the tracer verso lanes hit the same race (x.tif sha mismatch).
- **Fix:** Download shared inputs once before starting lanes and verify size against Content-Length and sha256 against the manifest.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-pairs0814b:logs/sib/pairs0814b/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-tracer:logs/sib/tracer/STATUS.md

### L440. The VC3D remote chunk cache is uncapped and fills the disk
- **Trap:** Rendering or growing on remote volumes with vc_render_tifxyz / GrowPatch fills ~/.VC3D/remote_cache until ENOSPC.
- **Evidence:** pairs0139c: the cache grew /work/docker from about 6 to 30 GB, 24 GB in about 7 min, failing all 8 render attempts at about 55 % of a 61.6 cm^2 segment; large PHerc0139 segments were estimated to need 21-40 GB vs 16 GB free; even a 15.64 cm^2 segment peaked at about 19 GB. tracer: decoded 192^3 chunks took 12-16 GB per seed region and filled the disk three times; FL-2 PHerc0813 stopped with 8 of 24 segments tiled after a disk-full render loop.
- **Fix:** Render in grid-aligned pieces of <= ~20 cm2 and delete the cache between pieces; run the render container with HOME=/tmp and XDG_CACHE_HOME on tmpfs (store growth 13 MB); check output size/completeness, never just the exit code.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-FL-2-E3, #DECL-FL-4-A4-E2; dominion:sib-pairs0139c:logs/sib/pairs0139c/fl2_gate/ASK.md; dominion:sib-tracer:logs/sib/tracer/REPORT.md, logs/sib/tracer/fl2/STATUS.md, tools/sib/tracer/dev_batch.sh

### L441. One launcher, matched by absolute path: duplicate watchdogs corrupt renders
- **Trap:** Launching a watchdog by relative path while the keepalive's pgrep matched the absolute path, so the keepalive started a second pipeline on the same work directory.
- **Evidence:** p4v-08: from 06:17:39Z to 09:47Z on 2026-10-01 two watchdog/pipeline instances overlapped on 7 segments (concurrent renders into the same zarr, rm -rf of a zarr during the other's render, duplicate infer writes); 40 tiles were excluded from the census and regenerated by a single pipeline. Other workers caught the same risk and relaunched by absolute path.
- **Fix:** Use a single launcher and a lock file (flock) per work directory; match processes by absolute path; check for an existing instance before starting one.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4v-08:README.md, logs/sib/p4v-08/fl2/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4v-02:logs/sib/p4v-02/STATUS.md

### L442. A keepalive must end inside the 7200 s background limit; the harness forbids restarting a max-timeout command
- **Trap:** Keeping a fleet alive with a background Bash keepalive that sleeps until just under 2 h and then expecting the lane to re-arm it.
- **Evidence:** At 07:58-08:01Z on 2026-10-02 every lane's keepalive (about 7150 s plus a final sleep of up to 120 s) overran the 7200 s limit and was killed; the harness told sessions not to restart a command that already had the maximum timeout, so the lanes stopped, containers were reclaimed and in-flight GP passes were lost (DECL-FL-4-A4-A2-E4). Fix: exit after 6600 s with 60 s sleeps (at most about 6660 s). Also: FL workers: a tracked pipeline task stopped at its 2 h limit with 4 of 39 segments tiled and was not relaunched; keepalives stopped at the 2 h background limit (PHerc0483A lane, PHerc1203 lane) and were not re-armed. Usage limits stopped the whole fleet on 2026-10-01 and ~08:00Z 2026-10-02, and again on 2026-10-10; a usage-limit pause also restarted an hzw worker container at 7/40 tiles.
- **Fix:** Write a marker per finished unit, push per unit, skip finished units on restart, and re-arm keepalives explicitly; plan fleet work so a simultaneous stop loses at most one unit per worker.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-02 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4v-02:README.md; dominion:sib-p4v-01:README.md; dominion:sib-p4v-08:README.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md (DECL-FL-4-A4-A2-E4), RULES.md#DECL-FL-4-A4-A2-E4; dominion:sib-pairs0814b:logs/sib/pairs0814b/fl4/PHerc0268/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-fl-pherc0483a:README.md; dominion:sib-fl-pherc1203:README.md; dominion:fl4t:README.md; dominion:sib-hzw1:logs/sib/hzw1/STATUS.md

### L443. Session count is not compute
- **Trap:** Equating session count with compute (sibling fleet: builder/trainer cloud sessions on their own branches with no access to seals, scoring or viewing; orders by one-shot triggers, decision requests through ASK.md, a RESUME.md per sibling).
- **Evidence:** The registry lists 118 sibling session entries (95 branches, created 2026-09-25 to 2026-10-02) and 52 sessions in the 2026-10-09 fleet; there are 116 worker branches, including 22 sub-sibling branches not in the registry. Fleets stopped all at once at background-time and usage limits (L389, L442).
- **Fix:** Make jobs resumable, keep each turn within known background-time limits, and budget the account's usage before scaling out; a fleet that outgrows its usage budget stops all at once.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-02 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:logs/sib/registry.json, logs/sib/registry.json (fleet_2026-10-09); dominion:refs/remotes/sib-*:git refs; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:RULES.md (DECL-FL-4-A4-A2-E4)

### L444. Idle sibling containers are reclaimed and detached jobs die with them
- **Trap:** Launching detached jobs in a sibling session and ending its turn.
- **Evidence:** Round-1 training was lost to a container restart and no umbilicus lane pushed 'done' within 85 min; until the fix, the effective fleet was a fraction of the session count.
- **Fix:** Resumable job + DONE marker; the sibling keeps its turn alive by polling in Bash calls of < 10 minutes until DONE; a backup trigger 100 minutes later relaunches dead jobs; orders come from a committed brief through a dispatcher.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-09 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#SIB-KEEPALIVE-1, #OWNER-STANDING-ORDER-6-A1

### L445. SDT bands must be aligned to the 512-working-slice tile rows and must cover the fit window
- **Trap:** Building the distance field per arbitrary 500-slice band.
- **Evidence:** The script works in whole tile rows: band z 7000-7500 computed working z 6656-7680 (1024 slices; up to 2x compute wasted). The loader refuses a fit window outside built_z_ranges_working (z_begin 6900 refused for a [6936, 7564] build). Per 100 working slices ~103 s and ~0.93 GB; whole scroll 6,975 base tiles ~3.6 h, group 1 ~101 GB.
- **Fix:** Choose [z0-64, z1+64] inside whole rows (z0 = 512k+64, z1 = 512m-64), reuse a store with --resume for bands sharing a row, and drop pyramid groups 2/3 (the fit reads group 1).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/units/U4-sdt.md, docs/SPIRAL_STUDY.md

### L446. Run villa ink inference on CPU as single-thread processes with a writable TMPDIR
- **Trap:** Running villa inference with torch.compile and workers on a 4-CPU box.
- **Evidence:** With --no-compile --num-workers 0 and one thread per process: 52.7k px/s fp32 and 83.9k px/s bf16 per 4-CPU box (model level), 57-74 s/cm2 per map end to end. torch inductor writes to /tmp even with its cache dir set. One whole-scroll uint8 map is 33.9 GB; the lean 42-map recipe is ~100 h on 60 boxes.
- **Fix:** Use single-thread processes, --no-compile, --num-workers 0, TMPDIR on a writable filesystem; budget storage for maps (not git) before scaling.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/PIPELINE.md

### L447. CPU spiral-fit memory growth is reference cycles: one gc.collect() per step holds RSS flat
- **Trap:** Blaming allocator fragmentation for steadily growing RSS in the CPU fit and trying allocator swaps.
- **Evidence:** On a 352-slice window RSS grew ~0.25 GiB/step and was OOM-killed after ~11 steps; a 640-slice window was OOM-killed while loading (~13 GiB). The Order-4 matrix (MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2, malloc_trim, jemalloc/tcmalloc, gc.collect) found Python reference cycles the generational GC rarely reaches: gc.collect() each step holds RSS flat (~6-7 GiB for 384 slices) with unchanged losses (B13, B15, B22, B23, B26).
- **Fix:** Set FIT_GC_EVERY=1 (built into fit_probe.py), MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2, CT-masked pools, windows <= 384 slices on 15 GB boxes; chunk the density supplement (sample_count_dense_spacing_density_chunk_pairs 128 avoided an OOM at step 7 on a 300-slice fit).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/BANDS.md; pherc0268:7b89dd1:commit-message; pherc0268:93f5dbb:commit-message

### L448. CPU spiral fits run ~16-34 s/step: the 30,000-step recipe is ~10 days per window
- **Trap:** Planning CPU fits with the recipe's step count.
- **Evidence:** ~29 s/step initially (3000 steps ~24 h, 30000 ~10 days per band); per-step cost hardly depends on window size (256-slice 26 s/step, 384-slice 29-34 s/step); later fits ran ~16-25 s/step; track_dt adds +0 to +27 % (median +9.5 %, n = 35) with RSS unchanged (<= 8.7 GiB). Critical path estimate at ~42 sandboxes: 18/30/78 h, paced by the fits.
- **Fix:** Budget step counts explicitly; prefer merged windows (same cost per step); measure s/step and RSS for every step of every run.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/BANDS.md, docs/SPIRAL_STUDY.md, docs/PIPELINE.md, docs/POC.md

### L449. snap_meshes.py is S3-latency bound: use --procs 16 and batch by whole windings
- **Trap:** Running the snap with --procs 4 on a 4-CPU box, or on a whole 384-slice window in one call.
- **Evidence:** A 35-winding 0.91 M-node batch took 64 s at --procs 16 vs 159 s at --procs 4, byte-identical output; batches <= 1 M nodes peak ~4.2 GiB; one call on a whole 384-slice window would need 13-15 GiB. FSSPEC_S3_ANON=true for the public m7.
- **Fix:** Snap with --procs 16, batched by whole windings (batching is exact).
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/PIPELINE.md

### L450. Disk, not CPU, gates sibling work: plan where every big intermediate lives
- **Trap:** Building inputs and renders on a 30 GB sibling disk (orchestrator ~0.4 GB) without a storage plan.
- **Evidence:** Per band: SDT 9.5 GB output + 14.55 GB mirror (+7.4-8.1 GB pool); B14 had 3.7 GB free after inputs; renders and ink start only after fit inputs are deleted; 42 ink maps per window ~32 GB. /dev/shm is RAM-backed (~16 GB). The orchestrator's PoC chain had to fetch snapshot git objects into a /dev/shm alternate object store.
- **Fix:** Drop SDT pyramid groups 2/3 and CT mirrors after packing, never build big data on the orchestrator, keep large files out of git with a manifest (path, bytes, sha256, regeneration command).
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/SPIRAL_STUDY.md, docs/PIPELINE.md, docs/units/U4-sdt.md; pherc0268:da1c18f:commit-message

### L451. Snapshot and resume long fits instead of restarting
- **Trap:** Restarting a fit from scratch to change a setting or to export meshes mid-run.
- **Evidence:** fit_window.sh snapshot stops at the next probe and writes checkpoint and meshes; resume rewrites the checkpoint's completed_iterations to the true stop step and relaunches with FIT_SPIRAL_RESUME_PATH, restoring model, optimizer, scheduler and RNG. No unit failed the track_dt resume (Order 6-A6 compliance check).
- **Fix:** Use snapshot/resume (with TRACK_DT=1 or EXTRA_OVERRIDES) and push meshes at each snapshot; on failure push fit.log and do not restart from scratch.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/BANDS.md; pherc0268:c407d09:commit-message

**Tools and infrastructure (L452-L508).** Concrete traps in the villa/VC3D stack, git, bash, harness verifiers and byte-level reproducibility.

### L452. pkill/pgrep patterns can match your own shell
- **Trap:** Killing jobs by command-line pattern from an agent shell whose own command line contains that pattern.
- **Evidence:** Recorded in four lanes: chain2um (two pkill -f calls matched the calling shell, exit 144), census (two kill commands killed the session's own shell), handed (pkill -f killed own shell), factory (exit 144). Also: reg0009b: three wait loops were waiting on themselves and had to be killed (exit 144); no data job was affected.
- **Fix:** Exclude $$ and $PPID; never combine kill-by-pattern with a relaunch naming the same script.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-10-15 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RESUME_NOW.md; dominion:sib-chain2um:logs/sib/chain2um/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-census:logs/sib/census/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-handed:logs/sib/handed/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-factory:logs/sib/factory/REPORT.md; dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#25; dominion:sib-reg0009b:logs/sib/reg0009b/REPORT.md

### L453. Test every scorer on synthetic data with known answers; guard NaN
- **Trap:** A scorer crashed on a missing input (caught by a synthetic test before the real run); NaN from a near-zero SD also produced invalid JSON.
- **Evidence:** tests/test_score.py::test_constant_map_gives_none_not_nan.
- **Fix:** Test every scorer on synthetic data with known answers and guard against NaN (emit None).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-10-15 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#29, tests/test_score.py

### L454. Build evidence into the pipeline for every image
- **Trap:** Stakeholders rightly asked for every patch shown as produced, ink painted on the fibres at a fixed scale, with measurable validation for each claim; curating afterwards was slow.
- **Evidence:** Stakeholders asked for every patch shown as produced, ink painted on the fibres at a fixed scale, with measurable validation for each claim; the release therefore ships an overlay, a panel and stats per surface and a fixed absolute display scale, p 0.40 -> 0.70 (release LESSONS 32; METHODS 7).
- **Fix:** Build overlay, panel and stats per surface into the pipeline instead of curating afterwards.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-10-15 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#32

### L455. Exact-reproduction checks against published artefacts are cheap and remove a whole class of input doubts before fitting
- **Trap:** Fitting spirals on input tools (band tracks U3, distance field U4, low-z track extractor T0, PHerc0268) without checking them against published artefacts.
- **Evidence:** All three reproduced their references exactly: the per-band track store matched the full published store on the test band (2,659,851 tracks, 54,717,756 points, SHA-256 identical); the CPU distance field matched an independent recompute voxel for voxel; the low-z extractor matched 601,994/601,994 published horizontal tracks on the overlap. Verdict: passed.
- **Fix:** Run exact-reproduction checks against published artefacts before fitting; they are cheap and remove a whole class of input doubts.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-10-14 (family period) · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/units/U3-tracks.md, docs/units/U4-sdt.md, docs/BANDS.md (Order 6-A3); dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Spiral-fit input tooling: band tracks (U3), distance field (U4), low-z track extractor (T0))

### L456. Route all decryption through one logging function, and keep views in their own ledger
- **Trap:** Decrypting sealed files or viewing images without a central log.
- **Evidence:** The decryption log holds 1,938 logged decryptions of 713 distinct sealed files (2026-09-24T23:48:13Z to 2026-10-02T16:22:57Z), mostly for scoring, consistency checks and audits. The view log holds 22 rows: 21 owner views from a human-review set of raw CT overviews (HRV-1, cancelled after batch 1) and 1 orchestrator view of a synthetic font chart (not scroll data).
- **Fix:** Route all decryption through one logging function, and keep views in their own ledger. Store the key outside the ephemeral container (a persistent secret) so that seals survive restarts; the project left this to the owner as optional.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-24..2026-10-10 (family period) · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5@a1f9f4635:logs/key_reads.tsv, logs/views.tsv, CHANGELOG.md; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Seal-key and view bookkeeping)

### L457. Read environment values (proxy port) from the live environment; a restart can change them
- **Trap:** A shared build script hard-coded the HTTPS proxy port (127.0.0.1:46883), and a running pipeline kept the port it started with.
- **Evidence:** Every fresh FL-2 container failed the VC build (CMake FetchContent clone of vc-delta3d refused) until the script read $HTTPS_PROXY (fix 21bf4bd3); observed container ports included 35979, 39681, 43757 and 44273. On p4v-03 a container restart changed the port 37747 -> 38625; from 12:48Z the running pipeline's push and the renders of 7 segments failed within seconds, with no data and no DONE markers, until restarted. Also: A harness restart moved the proxy from 127.0.0.1:33023 to :35379; renders then failed in ~3 s ('HTTP 0 fetching .zgroup') and, because a failed render advanced the queue, the runner claimed 3 segments in ~2 min. Earlier a wrapper hard-coded port 46883 and S3 renders failed after a restart.
- **Fix:** proxy_refresh(): re-read the live proxy from /root/.ccr/README.md at start and before every work item and re-export HTTPS_PROXY and related variables; wrappers read $HTTPS_PROXY; a failed fetch must not advance a claim queue.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-10-02 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4v-12:README.md; dominion:sib-p4v-03:logs/sib/p4v-03/fl2/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4v-11:logs/sib/p4v-11/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4v-05:logs/sib/p4v-05/fl2/STATUS.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-FL-4-A4-E3, CHANGELOG.md; dominion:sib-pairs0139:tools/sib/pairs0139/vc_build.sh; dominion:sib-pairs0814b:logs/sib/pairs0814b/ASK.md; dominion:sib-tribunal:logs/sib/tribunal/runs.jsonl; dominion:sib-p4-excl:logs/sib/p4-excl/fl2/STATUS.md

### L458. Flattening tool quirks: vc_flatten --uv-only aborts; libigl ARAP dynamics does not move at voxel scale
- **Trap:** Using `vc_flatten --uv-only` to get UVs, or the libigl ARAP tutorial settings on voxel-unit meshes.
- **Evidence:** vc_flatten --uv-only aborts on save (exit 134, OpenCV imwrite assertion on the 2-channel uv); libigl ARAP with with_dynamics=True moved at most 0.025 vox. ABF++ converges in 2-6 iterations (50 iterations identical to 10).
- **Fix:** Call the unmodified vc::abfFlatten from a small driver that writes u/v float TIFFs (abf_uv_dump.cpp); run ARAP with dynamics off and one pinned vertex.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-flat1:logs/sib/flat1/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-pp-flatcheck:tools/sib/pp-flatcheck/vc-flatcheck/README.md

### L459. Make every package claim mechanically checkable, and prove the verifier with planted faults
- **Trap:** Leaving submission-package claims to be checked by hand (submission-package factory and verifier).
- **Evidence:** A 16-check verifier passed 16/16 on a dry-run known-text window package; a fresh reproduction rebuilt the raw render, CT panel and PNG byte-identically in 55 s.
- **Fix:** Make every package claim mechanically checkable, with no image metadata, a measured scale bar and pinned tools, and prove the verifier with planted faults before it matters.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-25..2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-factory@a3b07b201:logs/sib/factory/REPORT.md; dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json (Submission-package factory and verifier)

### L460. Run loggers must use pipefail, and sib_* test files are not collected by pytest
- **Trap:** Trusting logged exit codes of piped commands; assuming `pytest` ran a lane's tests.
- **Evidence:** handed logrun.sh recorded the exit code of the last pipe stage (tail), so a failing pytest run was logged as exit 0 (fixed with pipefail). Lane test files named sib_*.py do not match pytest's default test_*.py pattern and run only when named explicitly (amx, contam).
- **Fix:** Use `set -o pipefail` in run wrappers and name test files explicitly in commands; importing a script without a __main__ guard also wrote a stray file into the repo root (handed).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-handed:logs/sib/handed/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-amx:logs/sib/amx/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-contam:logs/sib/contam/proposals/PROPOSALS.md

### L461. Thread count changes base inference output only at the 1-grey-level level
- **Trap:** Expecting bitwise-identical inference across thread counts, or failing a regression check on tiny differences.
- **Evidence:** Canary window 2648 x 2648 uint8, 1 thread vs 2 threads: forward 108 px differ (0.0015 %), reverse 71 px (0.0010 %), max |diff| 1. Re-saved base checkpoint loaded with 0 missing/0 unexpected keys.
- **Fix:** Accept max |diff| <= 1 on <= 0.1 % of pixels as tolerance and record thread counts; dry-run display builders against a known manifest (32/32 sha256 matched).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-25 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#D3-PRECHECK-RESULT, #DECL-D3-A3

### L462. Environment traps for the official villa/vesuvius stack on Python 3.13
- **Trap:** Running docker/env setup or `uv pip install -e villa/vesuvius` and assuming the environment is complete.
- **Evidence:** vesuvius 0.2.4 requires Python >= 3.14 while the frozen venv is 3.13, and uv has no ignore-requires-python (boot_pip/boot_pip2 failures). The official training import path also needs scipy, scikit-image, connected-components-3d, numba, fft-conv-pytorch, SimpleITK and pandas, which are not in the freeze; numba 0.66 refuses numpy > 2.4, so numpy had to be 2.4.6 (villa uv.lock). LZW tifxyz files need imagecodecs; zarr v3 is needed for OME-Zarr 0.5 label arrays. 'vesuvius infer not importable' cost FL workers hours. Also: Workers fixed it with pip --ignore-requires-python --no-deps -e on Python 3.13, installed hv-ink-freeze.txt minus its editable git line, and used the PyTorch CPU index (torch 2.14.0+cpu, torchvision 0.29.0+cpu); infer imports then worked and the official ink_9um checkpoint sha256 e635558a... verified. Torch versions still differed between workers (2.14.0 vs 2.14.1+cpu).
- **Fix:** Install vesuvius with `pip install --no-deps --ignore-requires-python -e` (or a .pth path entry), pin extra packages to villa uv.lock versions, install imagecodecs, keep a second venv with zarr>=3 for labels, and check `python -c 'import vesuvius.ink_detection.inference.infer'` before launching.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-amx:logs/sib/amx/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-chain2um:logs/sib/chain2um/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-d2-null:logs/sib/d2-null/READY.md; dominion:sib-fl-pherc1203:logs/sib/fl-pherc1203/NOTES.md; dominion:sib-handed:logs/sib/handed/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-fl-pherc0490b:README.md; dominion:sib-p4v-12:logs/sib/p4v-12/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4v-05:logs/sib/p4v-05/fl2/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4v-03:logs/sib/p4v-03/fl2/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-pairs0139c:logs/sib/pairs0139c/fl2_gate/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-reg0841:logs/sib/reg0841/chainvalid/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-pairs0814:logs/sib/pairs0814/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-sg:logs/sib/sg/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-pairs0814b:logs/sib/pairs0814b/STATUS.md

### L463. A bash loop variable inside push() overwrote the segment path: declare it local
- **Trap:** Using `for d in 2 4 8 16 32` for retry back-off inside a function in a script that also uses a global $d.
- **Evidence:** FL-4 run.sh push(): the loop clobbered the global segment dir $d, so after a grow push the render used --segmentation 2 and copied the tifxyz into ./2; from the 2nd segment on a lane could render a STALE tifxyz under a new name. Found 2026-10-01 18:31Z; fixed with `local d` (DECL-FL-4-A4-A2-E2). Also: push() retried with `for d in 2 4 8 16 32`; this clobbered the segment path $d, so a newly grown segment was rendered with `--segmentation 2` ('Error loading: 2') and a stray 2/ directory appeared.
- **Fix:** Declare function variables `local`; check render input sha256 against the manifest's tifxyz sha256 for every segment.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26..2026-10-02 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-fl-pherc0191:logs/sib/fl-pherc0191/fl4/ASK.md, README.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-FL-4-A4-A2-E2; dominion:sib-pairs0814b:logs/sib/pairs0814b/e2/REPORT.md, logs/sib/pairs0814b/rh/STATUS.md

### L464. Brief file paths must be absolute
- **Trap:** A brief listed the key sheet as a relative path; readers could not open it and the transcript audit would void every job.
- **Evidence:** Caught before launch; the batch was rebuilt with /home/user/dominion/configs/briefs/keysheet_sigma2.png. Also: A key-sheet path in the P4 briefs was relative; the Read tool needs absolute paths; the batch was superseded unlaunched and rebuilt before any read.
- **Fix:** Generate briefs with absolute paths and smoke-test one brief end to end before launching a batch.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:CHANGELOG.md, RULES.md#METRIC-HASH-21

### L465. Sibling-builder manifests drift in schema: check the eligible count against the builder's
- **Trap:** A builder added the coverage field at the top level of each tile while the hash-frozen normaliser reads it under stats.*; a fail-closed tool then treats every tile as ineligible.
- **Evidence:** M2a: norm_manifest (METRIC-HASH-27) dry run gave {eligible: 0, skipped coverage: 100}; the batch was held until a declared fix (METRIC-HASH-29) gave 60 eligible, 40 coverage-skipped. rh-e1 edited neither the manifest nor the hashed tool.
- **Fix:** Before importing any batch, run the declared command into a scratch directory and check the eligible count against the builder's own summary; fix mismatches by a declared tool or builder change, not by editing inputs.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#METRIC-HASH-29, #METRIC-HASH-28; dominion:sib-rh-e1:logs/sib/rh-e1/ASK.md

### L466. Pin actual file hashes, not a report.json that claims them
- **Trap:** Freezing code by copying the code_sha256 list from a lane's report.json.
- **Evidence:** The trainer head commit 08d7e42 changed d2_data.py, d2_train.py and pair_freeze.py without updating report.json, which still listed the earlier (5bc29e1) hashes.
- **Fix:** Compute sha256 of the files actually checked out at the pinned commit and record those in the freeze.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-d2-null:logs/sib/d2-null/READY.md

### L467. Byte-identical reproduction needs a canonical writer and no stray caches
- **Trap:** Expecting a rebuilt submission image to hash identically when PNG compression, metadata chunks or __pycache__ vary.
- **Evidence:** The factory wrote PNGs with one IDAT of STORED deflate blocks (bytes depend only on pixels), a whitelist of IHDR/IDAT/IEND, and tifxyz TIFFs with exactly 10 structural tags. reproduce.sh re-rendered from the public volume in a clean directory in 55 s with raw render, CT panel and PNG byte-identical; three independent builds gave the same PNG sha256. The first dry run wrote tools/__pycache__ into the package (fixed with python -B). FL/P4 helpers reproduced a reference map byte for byte (identical PNG sha256) before production.
- **Fix:** Use canonical writers, run python -B, verify with an independent verifier that trusts nothing in the package (16 checks incl. Cf/invisible characters and chunk whitelist), and require a byte-identical reproduction gate before helpers produce material.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-factory:logs/sib/factory/REPORT.md, logs/sib/factory/reproduce_dryrun.json; dominion:sib-fl-pherc0483a:README.md

### L468. Pin every git ref a frozen detector or tool reads to a commit SHA
- **Trap:** Frozen params and tools referenced branch tips of other lanes; fresh clones lacked those remote refs, so reruns crashed or depended on fetch time.
- **Evidence:** FE params referenced unpinned branch tips (pairs0814b cc81a67, p4-tiles-b 8687bf4 at fetch time); the 2.4 um sub-lane's run 1 crashed at the start of E2 injection on a missing remote ref and was rerun unchanged after fetching. The CU sub-lane c also hit missing remote refs on first launch. Map makers p4v-07 and p4v-11 failed their first gate run because pairs0814b was not fetched.
- **Fix:** Freeze references as commit SHAs (and file sha256), vendor small inputs into the lane, and verify all refs exist before the first run.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-pig-fe-e2:README.md; dominion:sib-p4-pig-fe:logs/sib/p4-pig-fe/REPORT.md; dominion:sib-p4-pig-cu-c:README.md; dominion:sib-p4v-11:logs/sib/p4v-11/STATUS.md

### L469. Verifier brief-equality checks break on a partial last session
- **Trap:** A verifier that normalises briefs but keeps one <IMG> line per image can never match a reference written for 8+1 images when the last session has fewer.
- **Evidence:** E1 (60 tiles) produced 7 sessions of 8+1 and one of 4+1; rh_verify A5 failed only on that session, while the other 7 briefs matched exactly; M2a hit the same defect. The proposed amendment collapses runs of <IMG> lines and checks image counts against the job record instead.
- **Fix:** Write verifiers that compare brief templates with image runs collapsed and check image counts separately; test them on a batch whose size is not a multiple of the session size.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-rh-e1:logs/sib/rh-e1/ASK.md

### L470. Encode every gate bar as tested, fail-closed code
- **Trap:** Gate rules kept in prose are interpreted differently at submission time.
- **Evidence:** SG code v1.2.0: each DECL-SG bar a constant citing its item; each computed item has a test in which it alone fails; R placement is provably image-independent (no image library import; patched loaders raise); a synthetic known-answer run passes all 15 items; merged-layout suite 721 passed, 7 skipped (726 after follow-ups); attested items without a RULES.md record are NOT_EVALUATED.
- **Fix:** Implement bars as constants plus tests at the boundary values (for example 11 fails / 12 passes), keep attestation items explicit, and make the CLI exit non-zero on any non-pass.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-sg:logs/sib/sg/REPORT.md

### L471. Scorer rules keyed on strip-name prefixes break when names change format
- **Trap:** score_p4.py applied a candidate rule only when strip.startswith('w010'); segment-prefixed names would silently fall under a stricter rule.
- **Evidence:** Found before any data on that strip; regression re-scoring of earlier census summaries identical after the fix.
- **Fix:** Key rules on explicit fields, not name prefixes; add a regression test re-scoring committed summaries after any scorer change.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#METRIC-HASH-26

### L472. Verify harness branches with full git history
- **Trap:** Re-verifying a harness batch after a depth-1 (shallow) fetch: commit-order checks (A1, B2) fail closed.
- **Evidence:** Observed once; after git fetch --deepen all three earlier batches passed 12/12.
- **Fix:** Fetch harness branches with full history before verification.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-26 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#METRIC-HASH-36

### L473. Verifiers must accept the code versions declared when each in-flight batch was built
- **Trap:** Updating hashed tools mid-run makes in-flight batches fail the code-hash check; jobs files recorded the wrong variant label.
- **Evidence:** Re-verifying a batch: A0 false before adding its declared versions, 12/12 after; p4_ext wrote 'sigma2' whatever variant it used (no batch affected yet).
- **Fix:** Keep a DECLARED set of per-batch code hashes in the verifier; write the actual variant into every jobs file.

### L474. Google Forms prize submission requires the owner's signed-in account
- **Trap:** Automating the Progress Prize Google Form: the safety classifier first refused the POST ('Real-World Transactions'); after owner permission the formResponse endpoint returned HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

### L475. Keep torchvision/timm out of the HF environment for PHerc.1667 checkpoints
- **Trap:** Installing torchvision or timm alongside transformers 4.57.6 for the PHerc.1667 model code.
- **Evidence:** The P4-O worker instructions state that a mismatched torchvision breaks the transformers import; the working env was torch (CPU) + transformers==4.57.6 + safetensors + numpy + opencv-python-headless + tifffile + imagecodecs + zarr<3.
- **Fix:** Build a minimal venv as recorded and do not add torchvision/timm.
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-ckpt-screen-b:logs/sib/ckpt-screen-b/p4o/WORKER.md

### L476. A crash after the tile is written stops multi-tile calls: run one call per tile and count outputs
- **Trap:** Treating a non-zero exit as a failed tile, or passing a multi-tile list to a builder that crashes after each tile.
- **Evidence:** ckpt-screen-b p4o_tiles.py at ca732ae: run_tile() ends with log(rec), and log() does dict(utc=utc(), **rec) while rec already has 'utc' -> TypeError after the tile PNG and JSON are written; exit 1 and later tiles in the same call never run. Re-running the idempotent command was safe because finished tiles are skipped. Fixed upstream in b87d9dd.
- **Fix:** Make one call per tile, treat a written json+png with verified sha256 as success, and fix log helpers that merge dicts with duplicate keys.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-dev-lcsoft:logs/sib/dev-lcsoft/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-ckpt-screen-b-s1:README.md

### L477. Write outputs in the integrator's exact layout as well as the lane's own directory
- **Trap:** Each worker inventing its own output paths, which forces the integrator to re-hash and remap files before a stage manifest can be built.
- **Evidence:** o5w6 wrote its tile to the WORKER.md layout under the integrator's directory with an identical copy under its own lane directory plus a summary result.json; the png sha256 was re-hashed on disk and matched, giving a direct hand-off to the stage manifest.
- **Fix:** Specify the exact output layout (paths, file names, fleet record) in the worker brief and verify png_sha256 after copy.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-o5w6:README.md

### L478. A blocked worker can still verify its inputs read-only by hash
- **Trap:** Assuming a blocked worker can do nothing useful until unblocked.
- **Evidence:** own-s2 and own-s3 verified the RECIPE.md sha256 (377784c2...6dfb8) and checked read-only that the base branch's reader files had the expected sha256 (byte-identical to commit 98cd075) without importing them; own-s2 also copied the 8 p4-excl input files (7.1M).
- **Fix:** Make hash checks (sha256sum -c, git rev-parse of blobs) the first step of every worker; they cross no permission boundary.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-own-s2:README.md; dominion:sib-own-s3:README.md

### L479. Tile size in pixels differs per segment: make tiling code per-segment
- **Trap:** Hard-coding one tile size for all strips of a scroll.
- **Evidence:** On Paris 4 the 2 cm tile is 8343 px on one strip and 8301 px on another (later strips 8324, 8349 and 8327 px); own-lead's code was made per-segment and re-tested.
- **Fix:** Derive tile pixels from each segment's own grid/metadata and test with two segments.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-own-lead:logs/sib/own-lead/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4-inner:logs/sib/p4-inner/STATUS.md

### L480. Windowed inference equals whole-image inference only if the halo covers the receptive field
- **Trap:** Tiling inference with a halo smaller than the network's receptive field, which leaves seams.
- **Evidence:** own-lead's synthetic tests: windowed inference (window 1024, halo 160 px) equals whole-image inference (diff 0.0) for a receptive-field radius of 151 px; resume after a kill is bit-identical (max weight diff 0.0); AUC matches brute force with ties.
- **Fix:** Set halo >= receptive-field radius and unit-test windowed vs whole-image equality and kill/resume determinism before any real run.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-own-lead:logs/sib/own-lead/STATUS.md

### L481. `git checkout <sha> -- <path>` stages files, which the next commit sweeps in
- **Trap:** Checking out another commit's tools into the working tree and then committing with `git add`/`commit -a`.
- **Evidence:** p4-highz commit 59d1343 accidentally included the checked-out reader tools (8 files) staged by the worker brief's checkout; every blob was byte-identical to the source commit (checked with git rev-parse), so it was a verbatim copy and was disclosed.
- **Fix:** After such a checkout, `git reset -q <path>` and exclude the path, or better, keep shared tools committed on the base branch; check `git diff --cached --stat` before every commit.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-highz:logs/sib/p4-highz/RESUME.md

### L482. A deterministic frozen detector re-run in a second container is a cheap independent check
- **Trap:** Treating a redundant worker's output as wasted compute.
- **Evidence:** The FE E1 sub-lane re-ran the frozen maps (289,883 chunks fetched, 9,977 absent; 1,211.6 s) and scores (70,058,674 positions on 60/60 tiles, 244 s) with sigma0 = 1.0; per-tile r_max matched the parent's E1 scores exactly on all 60 tiles (maximum absolute difference 0.0).
- **Fix:** Keep detectors deterministic and resumable; when two containers produce the same scores, record the comparison as a reproduction rather than discarding the duplicate.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-pig-fe-e1:README.md, logs/sib/p4-pig-fe/1129/scores_E1_raw.json

### L483. Smoke-test pinned verifiers on a live manifest before pinning
- **Trap:** Pinning harness and verifier code that has only been tested on synthetic inputs.
- **Evidence:** The map maker wrote held-out maps to maps/ while the pinned harness split and verifier read heldout_maps/, so the batch could not be built (caused by the orchestrator's own orders). Later a two-line housekeeping change (deleting a checkpoint directory when the disk hit its 5 GB floor) failed the verifier's code-hash check C0.
- **Fix:** Run the verifier on the live partial manifest; keep a set of reviewed accepted versions; re-pin each change with a new hash record and disclose the cause.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-27 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#METRIC-HASH-50, #METRIC-HASH-51

### L484. Pin the builder by sha256 in the driver and push every tile as soon as it finishes
- **Trap:** Letting workers run whatever code is checked out, and batching pushes.
- **Evidence:** Screen C workers ran ckpt-screen-b's builder pinned by sha256 (p4o_tiles.py, infer_1667.py) and adopted a mid-run OOM fix without doubt about which code built each tile; the parent merged tiles with sha256 and code-commit checks. Three workers' sessions were archived mid-run (2026-09-28 08:00Z) and their 8 finished tiles survived because each was pushed on completion.
- **Fix:** Pin code by hash, verify hashes at merge, and push each output unit immediately to the worker's own branch.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-28 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-ckpt-screen-c-s1:README.md; dominion:sib-ckpt-screen-c-s3:README.md; dominion:sib-ckpt-screen-c:logs/sib/ckpt-screen-c/STATUS.md

### L485. Git-ignored weights: a 'model published' commit can contain only the summary
- **Trap:** Assuming `git add <dir>` published the model when *.pth is in .gitignore.
- **Evidence:** own-lead's commit announcing the S1 model held only summary.json because *.pth is gitignored; model_final.pth was force-added in a later commit and the remote copy's sha256 was verified.
- **Fix:** After publishing a binary, list the commit's files and verify the remote blob sha256; use git add -f deliberately for weights.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-own-lead:logs/sib/own-lead/STATUS.md

### L486. A driver that logs an empty hash as a gate failure fakes a result
- **Trap:** A runner wrote 'REPRO FAIL' when inference crashed before producing any map (a git ref it reads had not been fetched), so a setup error looked like a reproducibility failure.
- **Evidence:** p4v-07: 'REPRO FAIL ... png_sha256 (file ) vs own-lead 6954db7d...' with an empty hash, voided two minutes later as a driver bug (ref ...-sib-pairs0814b not fetched); the gate was re-run and passed. p4v-11: an automatic 'REPRO FAIL (infer.py error)' was retracted as a SETUP ERROR (git show exit 128) and the gate re-run after fetching the refs.
- **Fix:** Make gate drivers distinguish 'could not run' from 'ran and differed': require a non-empty hash and an existing artefact before writing PASS/FAIL; fetch every ref the code reads before the gate.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4v-07:README.md, logs/sib/p4v-07/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4v-11:logs/sib/p4v-11/STATUS.md

### L487. Do not suppress tool errors inside a fail-closed gate
- **Trap:** A grow pipeline ran vc_tifxyz_selfcross with output to /dev/null and '|| echo null', so any failure became 'selfx=null' and every surface was silently dropped.
- **Evidence:** FL-2 PHerc0846A: 4 grows of 31.1, 31.1, 10.1 and 21.2 cm^2 all returned selfx=null, kept=false, so 0 segments and 0 tiles; the cause of the null was not recorded.
- **Fix:** Log stderr of every gate tool, treat a missing result as an error to investigate (not a quiet rejection), and alert when a whole pass keeps 0 units.
- **Label:** INFERENCE · **When:** 2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-pairs0814b:logs/sib/fl2-pherc0846a/pipeline.log, tools/sib/fl2-pherc0846a/pipeline.sh

### L488. Assert that every gate item exists in the batch before commit A
- **Trap:** A census whose positive-control window cannot be formed.
- **Evidence:** A window-census gate (the confirmed block) could not be formed because one of its tiles was a 'control' entry and the selection excluded all 'control' entries; commit A was voided before any reader and the gate replaced by two known-text windows.
- **Fix:** Build-time assertion that gate and positive-control items are present; void (never read) a defective commit A.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-09-30 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-P4-25-A11-A2

### L489. vc tools write stray tifxyz copies into the working directory
- **Trap:** Running grow or render from the repository root leaves an untracked directory named '2/' with a copy of the segment.
- **Evidence:** Recorded twice: a 488 KB tifxyz copy appeared as '2/' in the repo root at render start (pairs0139c FL-4) and a byte-identical stray copy of a PHerc1545 segment was written by the first grow (pairs0814b FL-2). Also: Several FL-2/FL-4 workers found an untracked '2/' directory (x/y/z.tif + meta.json, a byte-identical copy of a grown segment) in the repo root after grows; it was moved out and not committed. FL-4 kit A2 moved work to /work/fl4, but the cwd bug reappeared in a later kit.
- **Fix:** Run growers in a scratch working directory, check `git status` before every commit, and make keepalive match the exact command line of the running watchdog.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-pairs0139c:logs/sib/pairs0139c/fl4/PHerc0490A/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-pairs0814b:logs/sib/pairs0814b/fl2/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4v-11:logs/sib/p4v-11/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4v-05:logs/sib/p4v-05/fl2/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4v-01:logs/sib/p4v-01/fl4/PHerc0268/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4-excl:logs/sib/p4-excl/fl2/ASK.md, logs/sib/p4-excl/fl2/STATUS.md

### L490. Watchdogs must test every dependency and never declare done on zero work
- **Trap:** A watchdog accepted a broken environment because it tested only the vc wrapper and docker; the seed count came back empty and the lane wrote 'lane complete (0 segments)' / ALL_DONE.
- **Evidence:** p4v-03's fresh FL-4 session failed setup_env at 23:30:20Z; /opt/hv/bin/python did not exist; the loop ran zero times and wrote a false lane-complete at 23:32:03Z (DECL-FL-4-A4-A1-E2). Kit fix: accept the environment only if the vc wrapper, /opt/hv/bin/python, vc_render_tifxyz and docker all work; a non-numeric or zero seed count exits without any verdict.
- **Fix:** Accept the environment only if wrapper, python, built binaries and docker all work; exit without verdict on non-numeric or zero counts; write ALL_DONE only when every segment is done or skipped; push env-failure log tails and back off 10 min.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-01..2026-10-02 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-FL-4-A4-A1-E2, #DECL-FL-4-A2, #DECL-FL-4-A4-A2; dominion:sib-p4v-03:README.md, logs/sib/p4v-03/fl4/PHerc0268/STATUS.md; dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md (DECL-FL-4-A4-A1-E2)

### L491. Check a pipeline template's effective seed count before planning a fleet around it
- **Trap:** Passing nseeds=48 to a segment-growing template and planning 40 grow attempts per scroll.
- **Evidence:** The template's seed planner walks a fixed 8-entry (z_frac, azimuth) plan and returns at most 8 seeds whatever nseeds is; the second lane on PHerc0826 therefore had 4 seeds, all grew (about 31.13 cm2 each, 0 self-intersections) and the pipeline ended at 32 official tiles. Every worker using the template had the same cap.
- **Fix:** Dry-run the seed step and count seeds before dispatch; extending the plan needs a fleet-wide ruling so all workers share seeds and existing segment names.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4-excl:logs/sib/p4-excl/fl2/ASK.md, logs/sib/p4-excl/fl2/STATUS.md

### L492. Write TIFFs without metadata tags if a pre-commit hook checks them
- **Trap:** tifffile.imwrite adds ImageDescription/Software tags that the repo's pre-commit hook rejects, blocking every later push of a pipeline.
- **Evidence:** tracer FL-4: vgrid TIFFs were rejected; one was rewritten tag-free (pixels identical) and pushed manually, and later pushes would be rejected until the kit set metadata=None, software=False. tribunal kept off-sheet tifxyz meshes outside the repo for the same reason.
- **Fix:** Write TIFFs with metadata=None, software=False (or strip tags) and run the pre-commit hook in the pipeline's own test.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-01 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-tracer:logs/sib/tracer/fl4/PHerc0490A/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-tribunal:logs/sib/tribunal/REPORT.md

### L493. Sync with origin before concluding a tool is missing, and smoke-test the first unit before launching a fleet
- **Trap:** A restarted lane declared tools/fl4/go.sh absent and stopped; the first FL-4 kit failed every render within seconds.
- **Evidence:** p4v-01: 'tools/fl4/go.sh: No such file or directory' came from a stale local checkout; after syncing with origin the file existed. Under the first FL-4 kit 0/8 (p4v-01) and 7/8 (p4v-02) PHerc0268 renders failed on the first attempt.
- **Fix:** Fetch and check out the declared commit before running; run one full unit (grow -> render -> infer -> tile) end to end before fanning out.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-02 · **Sources:** dominion:sib-p4v-01:logs/sib/p4v-01/fl4/PHerc0268/STATUS.md; dominion:sib-p4v-02:README.md

### L494. Resumable runners need per-step completion markers
- **Trap:** Restarting a runner whose markers cover only part of a step.
- **Evidence:** A restart re-ran forward cover/vgrid on a prediction already deleted; its redirect truncated a tracked JSON to empty and the runner pushed it (restored byte-for-byte from git, 189 bytes).
- **Fix:** Set per-direction post markers only after cover + vgrid finish; never redirect into a tracked file before the step succeeds.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-02 · **Sources:** dominion:gifted-bell-gavnl5:RULES.md#DECL-FL-4-A4-A2-E2

### L495. Trace each artifact's code path before mapping pixels to 3-D
- **Trap:** Ink overlays were assumed to be flipped into reading orientation; only the panels were. A 3-D seam test then reported r = -0.20 where the truth was +0.43, and the wrong number was reported first. A validity-mask agreement of 0.80 for all four flips proved nothing.
- **Evidence:** Private record; corrected seam tool stripqc/seam.py (SUPERSEDED_CLAIMS S4).
- **Fix:** Trace who writes each artifact and which flips it applies before mapping pixels to 3-D; use a discriminative orientation check, not one that scores all flips equally.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-09..2026-10-14 (approx.) · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#6, docs/SUPERSEDED_CLAIMS.md#S4, stripqc/seam.py

### L496. Kimimaro parallel=8 deadlocks; spawn without a __main__ guard re-executes the script
- **Trap:** Running villa extract_surface_tracks.py --backend cpu as shipped (hard-coded kimimaro parallel=8) on a 4-CPU sandbox.
- **Evidence:** parallel=8 deadlocked on this box; parallel=1 worked (study 'tracks' verdict 7). Kimimaro uses spawn, so an unguarded entry point re-executes the script.
- **Fix:** Wrap the extractor: force parallel=1 (or a measured safe value) and guard the entry point with if __name__ == '__main__'. Edit nothing upstream in place.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/SPIRAL_STUDY.md

### L497. The tracks DBM is Python dbm.sqlite3: Python < 3.13 cannot open it and fails silently
- **Trap:** Opening the 13.2 GB tracks .dbm with the default Python 3.11 env.
- **Evidence:** On 3.11/3.12 dbm.whichdb returns '' (the file is an SQLite Dict(key, value) table); /opt/hv/bin/python was 3.11.
- **Fix:** Use Python >= 3.13 for any tracks DBM (villa itself needs >= 3.14); check dbm.whichdb(path) == 'dbm.sqlite3'.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/SPIRAL_STUDY.md, docs/units/U3-tracks.md

### L498. Packed track store is used only if the DBM's (name, size, mtime_ns) signature matches
- **Trap:** Copying or renaming a DBM (or fetching it over HTTP, which gives mtime in seconds) silently makes the fast .vctracks store stale.
- **Evidence:** The loader compares metadata.source_db_signature with the DBM and any .db/.dat/.dir/.bak/.pag siblings; on mismatch it prints 'WARNING: ignoring packed track store' and unpickles the DBM. Published DBM mtime_ns 1785303449288514815.
- **Fix:** Preserve mtime (os.utime(path, ns=(atime, mtime_ns))), never leave extra DBM sibling files, or use band DBMs that are signed at creation.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/SPIRAL_STUDY.md, docs/units/U3-tracks.md

### L499. villa 0fb38c45 CLI always resolves the tracks DBM and always loads outer_shell when tracks resolve
- **Trap:** Fitting a band with no tracks or no outer_shell folder: the load fails in normalize_tracks_dbm_path or on the missing shell.
- **Evidence:** B CLI resolves tracks/2um_ds2_ps256_surf_v2.dbm unconditionally (fit_session.py:612-652, fit_spiral.py:1539-1559) and loads outer_shell whenever tracks resolve (fit_spiral.py:1108-1114); the PHerc0343 recipe ships a one-line patch for the shell. On villa main, input_use_tracks exists and defaults to false.
- **Fix:** For no-track bands create an empty dbm.sqlite3 DBM at the conventional path; apply the shell-optional patch (tools/spiral_cpu/patches/0001); on villa main set input_use_tracks: true.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/SPIRAL_STUDY.md, docs/BANDS.md, docs/units/U3-tracks.md

### L500. Paris 4 tools hard-code 9.6 um voxels; PHerc0268 is 8.64 um
- **Trap:** Reusing Paris 4 tooling (grow_track_graph.py) or its cm2 limits on PHerc0268.
- **Evidence:** grow_track_graph.py hard-codes VOXEL_SIZE_UM = 9.6, so cm2 limits are off by (9.6/8.64)^2 = 1.235; the Paris 4 fit frame is level 2 of a 2.4 um scan (9.6 um), PHerc0268 is level-0 8.64 um. Fiber files need coordinate_base_shape_zyx (A) or x4 coordinates (B).
- **Fix:** Check every hard-coded voxel size and coordinate scale when porting tools between scrolls.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/SPIRAL_STUDY.md

### L501. make_surf_sdt.py needs explicit voxel size and CT group on the public stores
- **Trap:** Running the recipe's SDT command unchanged on the public PHerc0268 zarrs.
- **Evidence:** The public store has no meta.json, so --working-voxel-um 8.64 is required; --ct-group must be 4 (the default is the coarsest group 5). --ct-zero removes m7 false positives in the unscanned CT = 0 region. The unmodified script's output matched an independent scipy float64 EDT on 760,800/760,800 written voxels (max |diff| 0).
- **Fix:** Use tools/sdt/run_sdt.sh (byte-exact chunk mirror + unmodified script) and validate with check_sdt.py ref and the fit's own loader (check_loader.py).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/units/U4-sdt.md

### L502. GrowPatch is fast without normal grids and ~140-170x slower when it streams them
- **Trap:** Running vc_grow_seg_from_seed with remotely streamed normal grids.
- **Evidence:** Measured on PHerc0268: ~1.9 s/cm2 without normal grids vs 265-324 s/cm2 with remotely streamed normal grids (published grids total ~35.4 GB).
- **Fix:** Mirror the needed normal-grid files locally or grow without them for screening.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-10 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/SPIRAL_STUDY.md

### L503. Validate QA tools on synthetic controls before trusting per-item numbers
- **Trap:** Trusting per-winding phase-lock numbers from a new tool.
- **Evidence:** phase_lock.py per-winding numbers before 05:45 UTC were wrong (node offset bug); pooled numbers were correct. After the fix it passed synthetic controls: 3.2-5.3 on sheet centres, 0.0-0.87 at half spacing. patch_lock.py added a per-node random-shift NULL baseline (NULL 1.49 / 0.04 vs control 2.82 / 0.76).
- **Fix:** Ship every QA metric with a synthetic positive control and a null baseline.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/POC.md

### L504. VC3D apps run natively as a self-contained bundle, no docker needed
- **Trap:** Requiring the docker daemon (or a rebuild) to run vc_render_tifxyz on worker sandboxes.
- **Evidence:** The 12.95 MB binary + its ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 + 181 libraries (~174 MB compressed, ~0.45 GB unpacked) run with ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 --library-path <libs> vc_render_tifxyz ... on Ubuntu 24.04, bit-identical output.
- **Fix:** Ship the bundle to siblings; set OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 for vc_grow_seg_from_seed (the 41701aa build lacks upstream's BLAS cap); install imagecodecs (or write LZW with Pillow) for tifffile LZW.
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/PIPELINE.md, docs/SPIRAL_STUDY.md

### L505. List S3 chunk rows instead of probing every key
- **Trap:** Mirroring band inputs by testing each chunk key.
- **Evidence:** mirror_band.py switched to listing S3 chunk rows: 496 s -> 5 s. U4's mirror copies only the chunk files a band reads, as raw bytes (nothing decoded or re-encoded; missing chunks stay missing).
- **Fix:** Mirror by listing chunk rows and copying raw bytes for exactly the window needed.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-11 · **Sources:** pherc0268:93f5dbb:commit-message; pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/units/U4-sdt.md

### L506. Publish exactly the mesh that was rendered
- **Trap:** The pipeline published the untrimmed source mesh while the render used a trimmed copy, so 12 published meshes were one node row off their images.
- **Evidence:** Private fix (registration script, PHerc0268 repository commit 9c80b1f).
- **Fix:** Store exactly the mesh that was rendered, and record the crop offsets (prep.json crop.src_row0/src_col0).
- **Label:** VERIFIED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/LESSONS.md#14; pherc0268:gifted-bell-gavnl5:docs/FL_SEARCH.md; pherc0268:9c80b1f:commit-message

### L507. A deterministic rerun is not an independent reproduction
- **Trap:** A fresh-input rerun matched 22 of 22 values (max abs difference 0.000468) and all 5 thresholded decisions, but it used the same software stack and machine, and the original kept rounded numbers, not maps.
- **Evidence:** RESULTS 2; results/control_strips_rerun/ens_sha256.txt.
- **Fix:** Store map sha256s for future bit-level comparison, and call a same-stack rerun "deterministic with fresh inputs", not "independent".
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/RESULTS.md#2, results/control_strips_rerun/ens_sha256.txt

### L508. Rebuild third-party checkpoints from published files and verify
- **Trap:** villa loads {model, config, step}; a community model was published only as safetensors plus config.
- **Evidence:** METHODS 1: scripts/rebuild_dense_native.py; all 508 tensors and the config bit-identical to the original run's checkpoint (private record).
- **Fix:** Rebuild from the public files with a script, sha256-verify inputs, and compare tensors bit for bit.
- **Label:** MEASURED · **When:** 2026-10-14 · **Sources:** dominion:main:docs/METHODS.md#1, scripts/rebuild_dense_native.py

## Part 4. Claims we retracted

112 claims that appeared in a draft, a log entry, a README or the earlier release and were later withdrawn or corrected. Every claim in the first column is RETRACTED: never reuse it as a fact. Use the correction, and check the source before relying on it.
- **claim**: the withdrawn statement, with an ID (R001-R112) for citing.
- **what was wrong**: a one-line summary of the defect, taken from the correction.
- **correction**: what the record supports instead, as recorded. "Also:" adds the same correction as stated in a second source.
- **source**: `repo:ref:path`, with `#SECTION` for a RULES.md or document section. "expmap_raw.json evidence check" means the claim was a draft wording in the experiment-map survey, corrected against the cited file before release.
- Prize-candidate claims are not listed: a candidate was found and tested; details withheld for prize review.

## Part 5. Where to pick up

### Open problems and best next steps

The problems are numbered OP01-OP42 and grouped by area. Each gives the problem, the recorded best next step ("Next") and the relevant lessons. Sources: `dominion:main:results/experiments/experiment_map.json`, the per-branch `ASK.md`/`REPORT.md` files and the PHerc0268 docs, as cited in those lessons.

**Where to start.** No pipeline works end to end. The order is:

1. Geometry validated on ground truth for the target scroll (on-sheet, no layer jumps).
2. An ink model validated on held-out known text of the same scan type.
3. Calibrated readers.
4. Only then a census (OP01).

#### Cross-cutting

- **OP01. No reproducible pipeline produces legible letters on unread scrolls with public models.** Next: start from the experiment-map nulls. Fix geometry first (on-sheet surfaces validated on ground truth), then validate an ink model on a held-out scroll of the same scan type before any census. [L052](#l052-validate-geometry-tile-by-tile-before-running-ink-and-size-test-patches-to-exceed-letter-height-plus-line-spacing) [L176](#l176-a-cross-scroll-ink-model-can-be-completely-blind-on-a-new-scroll-gate-it-on-that-scrolls-known-text-first) [L256](#l256-push-a-known-letters-control-through-the-identical-pipeline-before-reading-any-null)
- **OP02. Public ink models do not transfer across scrolls or scan types without a positive control.** The 22-volume push produced no candidate. On PHerc0841, 9 um maps had AUC 0.73 and 0 letters were read. Next: gate every model on known text of the same scan protocol (e.g. held-out PHerc0139). Alternatives: fine-tune on the target scroll outside the sealed windows with NULL/REV controls (D3), or train at native 9 um with 2.4 um targets on a GPU (D2). [L176](#l176-a-cross-scroll-ink-model-can-be-completely-blind-on-a-new-scroll-gate-it-on-that-scrolls-known-text-first) [L196](#l196-the-base-9-um-model-detects-unseen-scroll-ink-at-pixel-level-auc-073-but-its-maps-are-not-letter-legible) [L218](#l218-a-null-counts-only-when-an-in-batch-positive-control-on-comparable-never-trained-text-passes-in-the-same-session)

#### Ink models and training

- **OP03. No ink model passes held-out bars at 8.64 um.** The best is the public dense model at 0.760 against 0.90. PHerc0268 has about 0.42x the sheet contrast of PHerc0343. Next: train or fine-tune on 8.64 um data with real labels, a frozen held-out set and frozen evaluation code, and a contrast-matched sensitivity control. Do ink work only on validated surfaces. Next: train on a GPU from the pinned trainer, whose bitwise tests pass. First declare DECL-D2-A1, the pair-freeze record (hold-outs pinned by file hash) and the stage-C exclusions. #### Geometry and surfaces

- **OP08. On crushed scrolls no numeric metric detects layer jumps.** Normal-grid grows pass the radial gate but jump at cracks. Next: validate a jump detector against cross-section ground truth. Until one exists, inspect cross-sections (`xsec`) for every surface. Next: a global formulation that assigns a block's ridge fragments to ordered sheets with non-crossing constraints across u and y, measured on the cached native block, plus a shear-line identity test (I6) on matched phantoms. - **OP20. Blind AI readers respond to ink colour, not letter shape.** The colour baseline AUC is 0.975, above every reader, and all confirmations came from one LLM reader family.
